1:7.Promotes Division & Discrimination: In [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:7](ibnkathir://1/7) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 1:7](tabari://1/7), classical exegetes cite Muhammad's statement to 'Adi ibn Hatim in [Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2954](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2954) explicitly identifying 'those on whom anger falls' (al-maghdub 'alayhim) as the Jews and 'those who go astray' (al-dallin) as the Christians. Because reciting Surah Al-Fatihah is obligatory in every unit of the five daily prayers, this exegesis embeds a daily liturgical repudiation of Jews and Christians into routine Islamic worship.

2:7.Theological Defect: This verse states that Allah Himself 'has set a seal on their hearts and on their hearing' (khatama Allahu 'ala qulubihim), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:7](ibnkathir://2/7) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:7](tabari://2/7) explain as a divine stamp preventing belief from entering, immediately followed by sentencing them to a great punishment. Depicting God as actively sealing human faculties against truth and then punishing people for that unbelief contrasts sharply with the biblical portrait of God, who takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked and desires humanity's salvation ([Ezekiel 33:11](bible://ez/33/11); [John 3:17](bible://jn/3/17)).

2:10.Theological Defect: Rather than seeking the spiritual healing of sinners, the text declares that Allah actively intensified the illness of doubt in their hearts ('so God has increased their sickness,' fa-zadahumu Allahu maradan, as glossed by Ibn 'Abbas in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:10](ibnkathir://2/10) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:10](tabari://2/10)) before assigning them a painful punishment. Portraying God as compounding internal spiritual corruption stands in direct tension with the biblical God who takes no pleasure in the ruin of the wicked and calls them to turn and live ([Ezekiel 18:23](bible://ez/18/23)).

2:29.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: This verse establishes a geocentric sequence in which Allah first created everything on Earth and only 'then' (thumma) turned upward to fashion the sky into seven layered heavens—a chronological order explicitly affirmed by Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:29](ibnkathir://2/29) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:29](tabari://2/29). This sequence contradicts modern astrophysics, which demonstrates that the universe and stars existed roughly nine billion years before Earth formed, while also conflicting internally with [Quran 79:27](quran://79/27)–[Quran 79:30](quran://79/30), where Earth is spread out after heaven is built.

2:30.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: The celestial dialogue in which angels object to Adam's creation on the ground that humanity will shed blood—followed in [Quran 2:31](quran://2/31)–[Quran 2:33](quran://2/33) by Allah proving Adam's superiority when he names creatures the angels failed to name—is absent from [Genesis 1:26](bible://gn/1/26) and [Genesis 2:19](bible://gn/2/19). Instead, this exact sequence closely parallels pre-Islamic Rabbinic Midrash in Genesis Rabbah 8:5, Genesis Rabbah 17:4, and Babylonian Talmud Sanhedrin 38b (cf. [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:30](tabari://2/30)), incorporating Jewish homiletic lore as historical revelation.

2:34.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: The narrative of Allah commanding all the angels to prostrate before Adam and Iblis refusing out of pride has no basis in the biblical creation account, deriving instead from Late Antique apocryphal literature such as the Syriac Cave of Treasures (ch. 2–3) and the Life of Adam and Eve (ch. 13–15). Furthermore, grammatically excepting Iblis from the angels commanded to bow here ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:34](ibnkathir://2/34)) creates an internal taxonomic conflict with [Quran 18:50](quran://18/50), which identifies Iblis as one of the jinn.

2:37.Contradicts the Bible: Here Adam's transgression is resolved merely by receiving and reciting certain words (kalimat) from his Lord—identified in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:37](ibnkathir://2/37) with the prayer of [Quran 7:23](quran://7/23)—whereupon Allah immediately pardons him without blood sacrifice or a promised Messiah. This denies the biblical account of the universal human fall, spiritual death, and redemptive atonement foreshadowed in [Genesis 3:15](bible://gn/3/15) and [Genesis 3:21](bible://gn/3/21) and expounded in [Romans 5:12](bible://rom/5/12).
2:37.Theological Defect: In canonical traditions explaining Adam's fall—including [Sahih al-Bukhari 6614](/hadith/bukhari/6614) and [Sahih Muslim 2652a](/hadith/muslim/2652a) (cf. [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:37](tabari://2/37))—Muhammad declares that Adam defeated Moses in debate by asking how Moses could blame him for a sin Allah had predestined for him forty years before creating him. Validating this deterministic defense makes God's prior decree the ultimate cause of human disobedience, undermining moral accountability ([James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13)).

2:41.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Addressing the seventh-century Jews of Medina, Allah commands them to believe in what He has sent down as 'confirming what is with you' (musaddiqan lima ma'akum, [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:41](tabari://2/41)). By appealing to the Torah physically in Jewish possession during Muhammad's lifetime as an intact benchmark of divine truth—alongside [Quran 5:43](quran://5/43) and [Quran 5:68](quran://5/68)—the text concedes the preservation of biblical scripture and creates an inescapable dilemma wherever the Quran contradicts it.

2:55.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: This verse and [Quran 2:56](quran://2/56) assert that when the Israelites demanded to see Allah openly at Sinai, a lightning bolt struck them dead and Allah subsequently resurrected them ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:55](ibnkathir://2/55)). In [Exodus 19:16](bible://ex/19/16) and [Exodus 20:18](bible://ex/20/18)–[Exodus 20:19](bible://ex/20/19), the Israelites tremble at the thunder and ask Moses to mediate without dying; the death-and-resurrection motif at Sinai reflects Rabbinic aggadah in Babylonian Talmud Shabbat 88b, where Israel's souls depart at each divine utterance and are revived.

2:63.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: The claim that Allah uprooted Mount Sinai and suspended it overhead like a canopy to compel Israel to accept the covenant ('raised the mountain above you,' cf. [Quran 7:171](quran://7/171) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:63](ibnkathir://2/63)) is absent from [Exodus 19:17](bible://ex/19/17), where the people simply stood at the lower base (be-tachtit ha-har) of the mountain. The Quran treats as literal history a famous Rabbinic homily from Babylonian Talmud Shabbat 88a, which midrashically read that Hebrew preposition as God overturning the mountain above Israel like an inverted cask.

2:65.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: This passage presents as literal history an incident in which Israelite Sabbath-breakers were physically transformed into apes ('Become apes, skulking away!'), an anatomical metamorphosis (maskh) explicitly affirmed in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:65](ibnkathir://2/65), [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:65](tabari://2/65), and [Sahih Muslim 2663d](/hadith/muslim/2663d) (cf. [Sahih Muslim 1951a](/hadith/muslim/1951a)). No such mass zoological transformation of an Israelite coastal town is attested anywhere in the Hebrew Bible or ancient Near Eastern historical records.

2:73.Contradicts the Bible: Concluding the cow episode begun in [Quran 2:67](quran://2/67), this verse merges two entirely separate Mosaic laws—the red heifer burned into ashes for purification water in [Numbers 19:2](bible://nm/19/2) and [Numbers 19:9](bible://nm/19/9) and the unworked heifer killed in a valley to absolve an unsolved murder in [Deuteronomy 21:3](bible://dt/21/3)–[Deuteronomy 21:4](bible://dt/21/4). It then introduces a non-biblical miracle in which striking the murder victim's corpse with part of the slaughtered cow temporarily revives him to name his killer ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:73](ibnkathir://2/73); [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:73](tabari://2/73)).

2:87.Contradicts the Bible: While stating that Allah supported Jesus with 'the Holy Spirit' (ruh al-qudus), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:87](ibnkathir://2/87) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:87](tabari://2/87) explicitly define the Holy Spirit as the created angel Gabriel (Jibril), corroborated by Muhammad's parallel statements regarding Hassan ibn Thabit in [Sahih al-Bukhari 453](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:453) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 3213](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3213). Redefining the Holy Spirit as an angel directly contradicts the biblical revelation of the Spirit as fully divine Lord and Creator ([Acts 5:3](bible://acts/5/3)–[Acts 5:4](bible://acts/5/4); [John 14:26](bible://jn/14/26)).

2:89.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: This verse states that the new scripture came to the Jews of Medina 'confirming what was with them' (musaddiqan lima ma'ahum, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:89](ibnkathir://2/89)), testifying that the Torah manuscripts physically held by seventh-century Jewish communities were authentic. Because pre-Islamic biblical manuscripts such as the Dead Sea Scrolls match the Torah we possess today, the Quran's endorsement of seventh-century Jewish scriptures refutes later claims of textual corruption.

2:91.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Recording the Medinan Jews' profession of faith in their own scripture, the verse insists that the Quran is 'the truth confirming what is with them' ([Tafsir al-Tabari 2:91](tabari://2/91)). Rather than alleging that the Mosaic text in their hands had been rewritten, the argument relies on the ongoing integrity and divine authority of the existing Torah—reinforcing the same affirmation made in [Quran 2:41](quran://2/41) and [Quran 5:44](quran://5/44).

2:93.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Repeating the Talmudic Shabbat 88a motif of suspending Mount Sinai overhead, this verse alters Israel's covenantal pledge in [Exodus 24:7](bible://ex/24/7)—'All that the Lord has spoken we will do, and we will be obedient' (Hebrew na'aseh ve-nishma)—into 'We hear and disobey' (sami'na wa-'asayna). Scholars note that this reflects an oral bilingual pun turning Hebrew 'asah ('to do') into Arabic 'asa ('to disobey'), paired with 'made to drink the calf in their hearts' adapting [Exodus 32:20](bible://ex/32/20) (cf. [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:93](tabari://2/93)).

2:96.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Referring specifically to the Jews—as confirmed in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:96](ibnkathir://2/96) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:96](tabari://2/96)—this verse declares that 'you will find them the most desirous of people for life, even more so than the idolaters.' Singling out an entire ethno-religious community as more spiritually avaricious for worldly survival than polytheists embeds a sweeping collective caricature into sacred scripture.

2:101.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Here the scripture possessed by seventh-century Jews and Christians is explicitly titled 'the Book of God' (kitaba Allahi), which a group among them tossed behind their backs even as the messenger came 'confirming what was with them' ([Tafsir al-Tabari 2:101](tabari://2/101)). Calling their extant text the Book of God demonstrates that the Quran's critique targeted moral disregard of authentic scripture rather than alleging textual alteration of the Bible.

2:102.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: The account of two angels in Babylon named Harut and Marut teaching people magic and marital discord ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:102](ibnkathir://2/102); [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:102](tabari://2/102)) is absent from canonical biblical history. Philological and historical scholarship traces the narrative to Second Temple and Midrashic fallen-angel traditions concerning Shemihazah, Uzza, and Azael fused with the Zoroastrian Avestan entity names Haurvatat and Ameretat.

2:106.Theological Defect: This verse institutionalizes abrogation (naskh) and divinely induced forgetting of revelation ('Whatever verse We cancel or cause to be forgotten,' nunsiha), corroborated by canonical reports of forgotten or canceled Quranic passages in [Sahih al-Bukhari 5038](/hadith/bukhari/5038), [Sahih al-Bukhari 5005](/hadith/bukhari/5005), and [Sahih Muslim 677a](/hadith/muslim/677a). Depicting God as retracting or erasing His own revealed words conflicts internally with [Quran 6:115](quran://6/115) ('none can alter His words') and contrasts with biblical divine immutability ([Malachi 3:6](bible://mal/3/6); [Isaiah 40:8](bible://is/40/8)).

2:116.Contradicts the Bible: This verse categorically denies divine Sonship—'They say, "God has taken a son." Glory to Him! No!'—a polemic applied directly to Christians in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:116](ibnkathir://2/116) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:116](tabari://2/116). By treating divine Sonship as incompatible with sovereignty, it directly contradicts the foundational biblical testimony to Jesus Christ as the eternal, uniquely begotten Son of God ([John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14); [John 3:16](bible://jn/3/16); [Matthew 3:17](bible://mt/3/17)).

2:120.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Declaring that 'neither the Jews nor the Christians will ever be pleased with you until you follow their creed' and dismissing their faiths as mere vain desires (ahwa'ahum, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:120](ibnkathir://2/120)), this verse frames non-Muslim believers as permanently implacable toward Muslims. Such categorical language discourages mutual trust by teaching that genuine goodwill from Jews and Christians is impossible apart from their conversion.

2:125.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: This verse places Abraham and Ishmael in Mecca purifying the Kaaba ('My House'), yet no pre-Islamic archaeological, epigraphic, or historical evidence attests to either patriarch traveling roughly 1,200 kilometers south into the Hijaz. In the biblical record, Abraham's journeys span Mesopotamia, Canaan, and Egypt ([Genesis 12:6](bible://gn/12/6); [Genesis 12:10](bible://gn/12/10)), while Ishmael settled in the Wilderness of Paran in northern Sinai bordering Canaan and Egypt ([Genesis 21:21](bible://gn/21/21); [Genesis 25:18](bible://gn/25/18)).
2:125.Failed Prophecy: The declaration that Allah made the Meccan House 'a place of meeting and security (amnan) for the people' (cf. [Quran 3:97](quran://3/97); [Quran 29:67](quran://29/67)) has been repeatedly contradicted by history. Major armed assaults inside the sanctuary include the Umayyad sieges of 683 and 692 AD—when the Kaaba burned and was struck by catapult stones—the 930 AD Qarmatian sack that massacred thousands of pilgrims inside the courtyard and carried off the Black Stone, and the bloody 1979 Grand Mosque siege.
2:125.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: In multiple canonical hadiths—including [Sahih al-Bukhari 402](/hadith/bukhari/402), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4483](/hadith/bukhari/4483), and [Sahih Muslim 2399](/hadith/muslim/2399), cited in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:125](ibnkathir://2/125)—'Umar ibn al-Khattab states that he suggested to Muhammad, 'I wish we took the Station of Abraham as a praying place,' whereupon this exact command ('Take the standing place of Abraham as a place of prayer') was immediately revealed verbatim.

2:127.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Depicting Abraham and Ishmael raising the foundations of the Meccan Kaaba ([Tafsir al-Tabari 2:127](tabari://2/127)), this claim is paired by Muhammad in [Sahih al-Bukhari 3366](/hadith/bukhari/3366) and [Sahih Muslim 520a](/hadith/muslim/520a) with the assertion that Jerusalem's sanctuary was built only forty years after Mecca's. Historically, Abraham (c. 2000 BC) preceded Solomon's construction of the Jerusalem Temple (c. 960 BC, [Acts 7:47](bible://acts/7/47)) by over a millennium, exposing a major chronological compression.

2:133.Contradicts the Bible: This verse depicts Jacob's sons on his deathbed naming Ishmael alongside Abraham and Isaac as one of Jacob's 'fathers' (aba'ika), compelling commentators in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:133](ibnkathir://2/133) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:133](tabari://2/133) to argue that 'father' here actually means paternal uncle. Beyond altering Jacob's biblical deathbed blessing in [Genesis 48:15](bible://gn/48/15), inserting Ishmael into Israel's patriarchal lineage contradicts [Genesis 17:19](bible://gn/17/19)–[Genesis 17:21](bible://gn/17/21) and [Exodus 3:6](bible://ex/3/6), where God's covenant passes exclusively through Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

2:144.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Addressing Muhammad directly—'We do see you turning your face about in the sky, and We shall indeed turn you in a direction which you will be pleased with' (qiblatan tardaha)—this verse explicitly tailors divine liturgical law to satisfy Muhammad's personal preference. As Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib reports in [Sahih al-Bukhari 399](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:399) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 4486](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4486) (cited in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:144](ibnkathir://2/144)), Muhammad prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months while personally wishing his qibla were Mecca's Kaaba, whereupon this revelation promptly granted his desire.
2:144.Contradicts the Bible: The verse asserts that Jews and Christians ('those who have been given the Book') already know from their scriptures that facing Mecca's Sacred Mosque is the truth from their Lord ([Tafsir al-Tabari 2:144](tabari://2/144)). In reality, neither the Hebrew Bible nor the New Testament ever mentions a Meccan sanctuary; biblical prayer consistently faced Jerusalem's Temple ([Daniel 6:10](bible://dn/6/10); [Psalms 5:7](bible://ps/5/7)) until Christ proclaimed worship of the Father in spirit and truth transcending geographic shrines ([John 4:21](bible://jn/4/21)–[John 4:24](bible://jn/4/24)).

2:158.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: This verse absorbs the pre-Islamic Meccan rite of pacing seven times (sa'y) between the hills of al-Safa and al-Marwa as 'symbols of God.' In [Sahih al-Bukhari 1643](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1643)—quoted in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:158](ibnkathir://2/158) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:158](tabari://2/158)—'A'ishah explains that Ansar converts hesitated to run between the two hills because they had previously performed that ritual in pre-Islamic paganism for the idol Manat, prompting this revelation to retain and Islamize the Arabian shrine custom.

2:178.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: By prescribing homicide retaliation along stratified social classes—'the free man for the free man, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female'—this verse legally institutionalizes chattel slavery and unequal valuation of human life. Majority classical jurists cited in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:178](ibnkathir://2/178) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:178](tabari://2/178) (cf. [Sahih al-Bukhari 111](/hadith/bukhari/111)) invoke this stratification to rule that a free man is not executed in retaliation for killing a slave, contrasting sharply with the equal image-bearing dignity of every human life in [Genesis 9:6](bible://gn/9/6) and [Galatians 3:28](bible://gal/3/28).

2:191.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Commanding believers to 'kill them wherever you come upon them,' this verse justifies lethal warfare on the premise that al-fitnah is worse than killing—where early authorities led by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:191](ibnkathir://2/191) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:191](tabari://2/191) explicitly define fitnah not merely as political persecution, but as polytheism (shirk) and disbelief. Classical commentators further note that the initial defensive restriction in [Quran 2:190](quran://2/190) was superseded by the broader offensive mandates of [Quran 9:5](quran://9/5) and [Quran 9:36](quran://9/36).

2:193.Incites Violence & Intolerance: This verse orders continuous combat 'until there is no fitnah and the religion is God's' (cf. [Quran 8:39](quran://8/39)), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:193](ibnkathir://2/193) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:193](tabari://2/193) gloss via Ibn 'Abbas as fighting until polytheism (shirk) is eliminated and Islam dominates. Both commentaries connect this mandate directly to Muhammad's declaration in [Sahih al-Bukhari 25](/hadith/bukhari/25) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 392](/hadith/bukhari/392)—'I have been ordered to fight the people until they testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah'—as applied historically by Ibn 'Umar in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4514](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4514).

2:216.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Declaring that 'fighting (al-qital) is prescribed for you, though it is hateful to you,' this verse makes physical warfare an obligatory religious ordinance overriding human conscience and reluctance to shed blood ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:216](ibnkathir://2/216); [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:216](tabari://2/216)). Elevating military combat into a binding divine duty stands in direct theological contrast to Jesus Christ's rejection of armed force to advance God's kingdom ([Matthew 26:52](bible://mt/26/52); [John 18:36](bible://jn/18/36)).

2:217.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: As documented in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:217](ibnkathir://2/217) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:217](tabari://2/217), this revelation answered the scandal surrounding the Nakhlah raid, in which Muhammad's detachment under 'Abdullah ibn Jahsh ambushed a Meccan caravan during the sacred truce month of Rajab, killing 'Amr ibn al-Hadrami and seizing captives and booty. After Muhammad initially paused distribution of the fifth of the plunder amid widespread Arabian condemnation, this verse conveniently ruled that Meccan disbelief was graver than killing in the sacred month, exonerating the raiders and releasing the war spoils.

2:221.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: By instructing believers that 'a believing slave girl is better than a free idolatrous woman' and 'a believing slave is better than a free idolatrous man,' this verse embeds chattel slavery into Islamic family law as an accepted permanent institution ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:221](ibnkathir://2/221)). Paired with [Quran 5:5](quran://5/5), classical jurists also use this passage to enforce asymmetric interfaith marriage rules forbidding Muslim women from marrying Jewish or Christian men while permitting Muslim men to marry Jewish and Christian women.

2:223.Devalues Women: Addressing husbands exclusively, the text compares wives to agricultural land—'Your women are a field (harth) for you, so come to your field when you wish'—explained via Jabir's report in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4528](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4528) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:223](ibnkathir://2/223) regarding permissible sexual positions, alongside [Sahih al-Bukhari 3237](/hadith/bukhari/3237) warning that angels curse a wife who declines her husband's bed. Framing wives as a field at male sexual disposal contrasts sharply with sacrificial, reciprocal marital love in [Ephesians 5:25](bible://eph/5/25) and [Ephesians 5:28](bible://eph/5/28).

2:228.Devalues Women: While acknowledging reciprocal marital duties, this verse codifies structural male hierarchy by decreeing that 'men have a rank above them' (wa-lil-rijali 'alayhinna darajatun) and granting husbands superior unilateral right (ahaqqu bi-raddihinna) to take divorced wives back during the three-cycle waiting period. As recorded in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:228](ibnkathir://2/228) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:228](tabari://2/228), classical jurisprudence enforces the husband's revocation of divorce during this period without requiring the woman's renewed consent.

2:230.Devalues Women: Instituting nikah al-tahlil, this verse forbids a thrice-divorced woman from remarrying her original husband unless she first marries a different man and that second husband subsequently divorces her. In [Sahih al-Bukhari 5260](/hadith/bukhari/5260), [Sahih al-Bukhari 5825](/hadith/bukhari/5825), and [Sahih Muslim 1433a](/hadith/muslim/1433a) (cited in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:230](ibnkathir://2/230)), Muhammad explicitly ruled that actual sexual penetration with the second husband is mandatory even when the woman reported domestic abuse and impotence—directly reversing [Deuteronomy 24:1](bible://dt/24/1)–[Deuteronomy 24:4](bible://dt/24/4) and contradicting [Matthew 19:6](bible://mt/19/6).

2:249.Contradicts the Bible: Narrating King Saul's (Talut, [Quran 2:247](quran://2/247)) march to fight Goliath (Jalut), this verse states that Saul tested and winnowed his soldiers at a river by how they drank water with their hands ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:249](ibnkathir://2/249); [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:249](tabari://2/249)). In biblical history, that distinctive water-drinking troop reduction never occurred under King Saul ( eleventh century BC), belonging instead to the judge Gideon's campaign against the Midianites generations earlier in [Judges 7:4](bible://jgs/7/4)–[Judges 7:7](bible://jgs/7/7).

2:258.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: This verse recounts a debate over life, death, and cosmic power between Abraham and an unnamed monarch—identified across [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:258](ibnkathir://2/258) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:258](tabari://2/258) as King Nimrod, whom [Genesis 10:8](bible://gn/10/8) places in the early post-Flood era generations before Abraham. Completely absent from canonical Genesis, the Abraham-Nimrod confrontation derives from post-biblical Jewish aggadah such as Genesis Rabbah 38:13 (cf. [Quran 21:68](quran://21/68)).

2:259.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: The account of a traveler passing a ruined city—identified in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:259](ibnkathir://2/259) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:259](tabari://2/259) as 'Uzayr (Ezra) or Jeremiah at ruined Jerusalem—who dies for a hundred years beside his donkey and unspoiled food and drink before waking has no basis in the biblical books of Ezra or Jeremiah. Instead, it fuses motifs from the Talmudic tale of Honi the Circle-Drawer sleeping seventy years beside his donkey in Babylonian Talmud Ta'anit 23a and Abimelech's sixty-six-year sleep with unspoiled figs during Jerusalem's desolation in the apocryphal 4 Baruch.

2:260.Contradicts the Bible: Here Abraham asks Allah to show him how the dead are raised to satisfy his heart, whereupon Allah instructs him to take four birds, dismember and distribute pieces of them across separate hills ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:260](ibnkathir://2/260); [Tafsir al-Tabari 2:260](tabari://2/260)), and summon them back alive. This reworks God's covenant-ratification ceremony with Abraham in [Genesis 15:9](bible://gn/15/9)–[Genesis 15:10](bible://gn/15/10), which was not a resurrection experiment and where [Genesis 15:10](bible://gn/15/10) explicitly notes that Abraham 'did not cut the birds in two.'

2:282.Devalues Women: This verse legislates that two female witnesses are required to replace a single male witness in financial contracts ('so that if one of the two women goes astray, the other will remind her'). Refuting modern harmonizations that treat this rule as merely temporary commercial accommodation, Muhammad explicitly cites [Quran 2:282](quran://2/282) in [Sahih al-Bukhari 304](/hadith/bukhari/304), [Sahih al-Bukhari 2658](/hadith/bukhari/2658), and [Sahih Muslim 79a](/hadith/muslim/79a) (cf. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:282](ibnkathir://2/282)) as proof of women's innate 'deficiency of intellect' (nuqsan 'aqliha).

3:3.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Declaring that Allah sent down the Quran 'confirming what was before it, and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel' as 'guidance for the people' ([Quran 3:4](quran://3/4); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:3](ibnkathir://3/3); [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:3](tabari://3/3)), this verse explicitly validates the divine origin and authority of both Jewish and Christian scriptures. Because extant pre-Islamic Torah and Gospel manuscripts—such as Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus—proclaim Christ's divine Sonship and crucifixion, affirming them as divine guidance creates an irresolvable dilemma for Islamic theology.

3:28.Promotes Division & Discrimination: This verse forbids believers from taking non-Muslims as close friends or allies (awliya') in preference to fellow Muslims, warning that anyone who does so 'has nothing from God,' while carving out an exception for precautionary dissimulation (tuqatan). Commenting on this clause in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:28](ibnkathir://3/28) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:28](tabari://3/28), early authorities including Ibn 'Abbas and Abu al-Darda' explain that believers may outwardly smile in the faces of non-Muslims while inwardly cursing them in their hearts.

3:35.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Identifying the Virgin Mary's father as 'Imran—paired with [Quran 66:12](quran://66/12) ('Mary, daughter of 'Imran') and [Quran 19:28](quran://19/28) ('O sister of Aaron')—this verse conflates first-century Mary, mother of Jesus, with Miriam, daughter of Amram ('Imran) and sister of Aaron and Moses from the Exodus ([Exodus 6:20](bible://ex/6/20); [Numbers 26:59](bible://nm/26/59)), compressing roughly 1,400 years of history. Although Muhammad told al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah in [Sahih Muslim 2135](/hadith/muslim/2135) that Israelites merely named people after earlier prophets, that defense cannot explain naming Mary's biological father 'Imran here ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:35](ibnkathir://3/35)).

3:36.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Interpreting Hannah's prayer placing Mary and her offspring under divine protection from Satan, Muhammad declares in [Sahih al-Bukhari 3286](/hadith/bukhari/3286), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4548](/hadith/bukhari/4548), and [Sahih Muslim 2366c](/hadith/muslim/2366c) (quoted in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:36](ibnkathir://3/36)) that Satan stabs every newborn descendant of Adam at birth except Mary and her son Jesus. By exempting Jesus alone among all prophets—implicitly including Muhammad himself—from Satan's universal touch upon humanity, canonical Islamic tradition concedes Christ's unique sinlessness ([Hebrews 4:15](bible://heb/4/15)).

3:37.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: This verse portrays young Mary living inside the Jerusalem Temple sanctuary (al-mihrab) under Zechariah's custody and receiving miraculous food directly from heaven ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:37](ibnkathir://3/37)). Completely absent from the canonical Gospels—and incompatible with Second Temple Jewish law, which barred females from residing inside the sanctuary precincts—this exact narrative derives from the second-century AD apocryphal Protoevangelium of James (ch. 7–8).

3:39.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Announcing John the Baptist's birth, the angels declare that he will come 'confirming a Word from God' (musaddiqan bi-kalimatin mina Allahi), unanimously identified in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:39](ibnkathir://3/39) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:39](tabari://3/39) as Jesus Christ. Bestowing the title 'Word' (Kalimah) personally upon Jesus—a title never given to Muhammad or any other prophet in the Quran—echoes the New Testament revelation of Christ as the eternal divine Word ([John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1); [John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14)).

3:41.Contradicts the Bible: When Zechariah asks for a sign of John's conception, he is told that he will be unable to speak to people 'for three days, except by gestures' (cf. 'three nights' in [Quran 19:10](quran://19/10); [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:41](tabari://3/41)). This directly contradicts the first-century historical Gospel account in [Luke 1:20](bible://lk/1/20) and [Luke 1:62](bible://lk/1/62)–[Luke 1:64](bible://lk/1/64), where Zechariah remained mute throughout Elizabeth's entire nine-month pregnancy until John's circumcision and naming eight days after birth.

3:44.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Presenting the preceding narrative as secret revelation—'That is one of the stories of the unseen; We inspired you with it'—the verse cites priests casting their reed pens (aqlamahum) as lots to decide who would take custody of Mary ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:44](ibnkathir://3/44)). Far from being an unrecorded secret known only through seventh-century divine inspiration, the story of Temple priests casting rods so Zechariah wins guardianship of Mary had circulated openly for nearly five centuries in the second-century AD apocryphal Protoevangelium of James (ch. 8–9).

3:45.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Here the angels announce Jesus with an extraordinary cluster of titles unmatched by any other prophet in Islamic scripture: 'a Word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, eminent in this world and the Hereafter, and one of those brought near' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:45](ibnkathir://3/45); cf. [Sahih al-Bukhari 4712](/hadith/bukhari/4712) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 3435](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3435)). Affirming Jesus as God's Word, the Messiah, and uniquely exalted in both worlds concedes foundational Christological titles rooted in [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1) and [Philippians 2:9](bible://phil/2/9)–[Philippians 2:11](bible://phil/2/11).

3:46.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: The claim that Jesus spoke articulately to people while still a newborn infant 'in the cradle' (elaborated in [Quran 19:29](quran://19/29)–[Quran 19:33](quran://19/33) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:46](ibnkathir://3/46)) is absent from the four first-century Gospels and contradicts [John 2:11](bible://jn/2/11), which identifies the wedding at Cana in adulthood as the beginning of Jesus's miraculous signs. Instead, the cradle-speech episode reflects Late Antique Christian apocryphal infancy folklore preserved in the Syriac and Arabic Infancy Gospel tradition (ch. 1).

3:49.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Having Jesus fashion a bird out of clay and breathe life into it ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:49](ibnkathir://3/49)) incorporates a celebrated childhood tale from the second-century AD apocryphal Infancy Gospel of Thomas (ch. 2) that is completely foreign to the first-century canonical Gospels and contradicts [John 2:11](bible://jn/2/11), where turning water into wine at Cana is explicitly recorded as Jesus's first sign.
3:49.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Even while qualifying Jesus's miracles as occurring by God's permission, this verse attributes to Jesus the act of creating (akhluqu, from khalaqa—the very verb used elsewhere in [Quran 16:20](quran://16/20) and [Quran 22:73](quran://22/73) to distinguish the true Creator from non-divine beings) and breathing life into clay, mirroring God's own animation of Adam ([Genesis 2:7](bible://gn/2/7)) and conceding divine creative power to Christ ([John 1:3](bible://jn/1/3); [Colossians 1:16](bible://col/1/16)).

3:54.Theological Defect: Describing the plot against Jesus, this verse proclaims that 'God schemed too, and God is the best of schemers' (khayru al-makirin, from makr, denoting covert plotting, guile, or trickery). In [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:54](ibnkathir://3/54) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:54](tabari://3/54), commentators explain Allah's makr as disguising another man in Jesus's physical likeness to be crucified in his place (cf. [Quran 4:157](quran://4/157))—making God the author of a public optical deception that misled Christ's own disciples into proclaiming the resurrection, contrary to the God of truth in [Numbers 23:19](bible://nm/23/19) and [Titus 1:2](bible://ti/1/2).

3:55.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Allah promises Jesus to raise him directly to Himself, purify him above unbelievers, and 'place those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:55](ibnkathir://3/55); [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:55](tabari://3/55)). Conceding Jesus's bodily ascension into God's presence ([Acts 1:9](bible://acts/1/9); [Ephesians 1:20](bible://eph/1/20)) elevates Christ above Muhammad, who died and remained buried in Medina, while the verb mutawaffika ('causing you to die,' as glossed by Ibn 'Abbas in [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:55](tabari://3/55)) tensions internally with [Quran 4:157](quran://4/157).

3:59.Contradicts the Bible: Asserting that 'the likeness of Jesus is, with God, as the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust, then He said to him, "Be!" and he was' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:59](ibnkathir://3/59)), this verse reduces Christ to a merely created human being. This directly contradicts the biblical revelation of Jesus as the uncreated, eternal Word through whom all things came into being ([John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1)–[John 1:3](bible://jn/1/3); [Colossians 1:15](bible://col/1/15)–[Colossians 1:17](bible://col/1/17)), while even [Quran 4:171](quran://4/171) titles Jesus Allah's Word and a Spirit from Him—designations never applied to Adam.

3:93.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Commanding Muhammad to challenge his seventh-century Jewish interlocutors in Medina—'Bring the Torah and read it, if you are truthful' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:93](ibnkathir://3/93))—this verse appeals directly to physical Torah scrolls in seventh-century Jewish hands as an intact, authoritative arbiter of historical truth, refuting later Islamic claims that the Hebrew Bible had already been textually corrupted.
3:93.Contradicts the Bible: The verse asserts that all food was lawful to Israel prior to the Mosaic Torah except what Jacob ('Israel') unilaterally forbade himself—identified in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:93](ibnkathir://3/93) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:93](tabari://3/93) as camel meat and milk alongside the sciatic nerve of [Genesis 32:32](bible://gn/32/32). In the actual Torah, however, God Himself had explicitly prohibited consuming flesh with its lifeblood centuries before Jacob in His covenant with Noah ([Genesis 9:4](bible://gn/9/4); cf. [Genesis 7:2](bible://gn/7/2)).

3:96.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: This verse claims that the sanctuary at Becca—universally identified in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:96](ibnkathir://3/96), [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:96](tabari://3/96), and [Sahih al-Bukhari 3366](/hadith/bukhari/3366) as Mecca's Kaaba—was 'the first House laid down for the people' on Earth. Neither archaeology nor ancient Near Eastern epigraphy records any pre-first-millennium BC settlement or sanctuary at Mecca, whereas documented sanctuaries in Mesopotamia, Anatolia, and Canaan—as well as biblical altars at Shechem and Bethel ([Genesis 12:7](bible://gn/12/7)–[Genesis 12:8](bible://gn/12/8); [Genesis 28:18](bible://gn/28/18)–[Genesis 28:19](bible://gn/28/19))—predate Mecca by millennia.

3:97.Failed Prophecy: Of the Meccan Kaaba precinct, this verse unconditionally declares: 'Whoever enters it is secure' (wa-man dakhalahu kana aminan, cf. [Quran 2:125](quran://2/125)). In reality, during the 630 AD conquest of Mecca itself, Muhammad ordered Ibn Khatal executed even while he clung to the curtains of the Kaaba ([Sahih al-Bukhari 1846](/hadith/bukhari/1846); [Sahih Muslim 1357](/hadith/muslim/1357)), and later history saw repeated lethal warfare inside the sanctuary—including the Umayyad catapult sieges of 683 and 692 AD, the 930 AD Qarmatian massacre of thousands of pilgrims inside the courtyard, and the armed 1979 Grand Mosque siege.

3:110.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Elevating the Muslim community as 'the best community ever brought forth for humankind,' this verse sweeps across Jews and Christians ('the People of the Book') to pronounce that while a few believe, 'most of them are wicked' (wa-aktharuhumu al-fasiqun). Commenting on this superiority clause in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4557](/hadith/bukhari/4557) (quoted directly in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:110](ibnkathir://3/110)), Abu Hurayrah explains: 'You are the best of people for the people: you bring them with chains around their necks until they enter Islam.'

3:112.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Referring to non-believing People of the Book, this verse decrees that 'humiliation (al-dhillah) will be stamped upon them wherever they are found, unless they grasp a rope from God and a rope from the people,' adding that divine anger and wretchedness are stamped upon them. In [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:112](ibnkathir://3/112) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:112](tabari://3/112), early authorities led by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah explicitly define 'a rope from the people' as the dhimmi pact requiring Jews and Christians to submit politically and pay the jizyah tribute in subordination (cf. [Quran 9:29](quran://9/29)).

3:118.Promotes Division & Discrimination: This verse commands believers not to take non-Muslims ('outsiders,' bitanatan min dunikum) as intimate friends or confidants, generalizing that 'they will not fail to cause you ruin,' that hatred appears from their mouths, and that 'what their hearts hide is even greater' (cf. [Quran 3:119](quran://3/119)). In [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:118](ibnkathir://3/118) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:118](tabari://3/118), jurists cite 'Umar ibn al-Khattab invoking this prohibition to bar employing trustworthy Christians or Jews in positions of public trust.

3:151.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Linking battlefield psychological terror directly to theological non-conformity, Allah proclaims: 'We shall cast dread (al-ru'b) into the hearts of those who disbelieve, because they have associated with God what He has not sent down any authority for' (cf. [Quran 8:12](quran://8/12)). In [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:151](ibnkathir://3/151), this promise is paired directly with Muhammad's statement in [Sahih Muslim 523a](/hadith/muslim/523a) that he was uniquely aided over prior prophets through military terror cast into enemies a month's march away and the legalization of war booty.

3:178.Theological Defect: Explaining why Allah grants earthly lifespan and respite to unbelievers, this verse states: 'We only spare them so that they will increase in sin! (innama numli lahum li-yazdadu ithman) For them there is a humiliating punishment' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:178](ibnkathir://3/178); [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:178](tabari://3/178)). Depicting God as prolonging human life specifically for the purpose of multiplying human sin and damnation stands in stark opposition to the biblical revelation that God's patience and forbearance are meant to lead sinners to repentance ([Romans 2:4](bible://rom/2/4); [Ezekiel 18:23](bible://ez/18/23)).

3:183.Contradicts the Bible: When Medinan Jews cite God's requirement of a sacrifice consumed by heavenly fire (attested in [Leviticus 9:24](bible://lv/9/24) and [Judges 6:21](bible://jgs/6/21)), Muhammad is instructed to reply: 'Messengers have come to you before me with the clear signs, and with that which you spoke of. So why did you kill them, if you are truthful?' In the entire biblical record, not a single figure associated with fire from heaven consuming a sacrifice—Moses, Aaron, Gideon, David, Solomon, or Elijah—was ever murdered by Israel, forcing [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:183](ibnkathir://3/183) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 3:183](tabari://3/183) to cite Zechariah and John the Baptist, neither of whom performed that miracle.

3:195.Incites Violence & Intolerance: In this divine response, Allah promises those who 'have fought and been killed' (qatalu wa-qutilu, active military combat followed by battlefield death, as explained in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:195](ibnkathir://3/195)) automatic expiation of their sins and direct admission into Paradise (cf. [Quran 9:111](quran://9/111)). Linking the forgiveness of sins directly to waging lethal warfare and dying in combat contrasts fundamentally with New Testament martyrdom, which honors non-violent perseverance under persecution rather than armed bloodshed ([Matthew 5:10](bible://mt/5/10)–[Matthew 5:12](bible://mt/5/12); [Revelation 12:11](bible://rv/12/11)).

4:3.Devalues Women: This verse institutionalizes asymmetric polygyny by permitting a Muslim man to marry up to four wives simultaneously—arising from guardians marrying female orphans without paying fair dowries ([Sahih al-Bukhari 4574](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4574), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:3](ibnkathir://4/3))—while denying women reciprocal marital parity and contrasting with Christ's restoration of lifelong one-flesh monogamy ([Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4)–[Matthew 19:6](bible://mt/19/6)). Although Muhammad exempted himself from this four-wife cap by maintaining nine concurrent wives ([Sahih al-Bukhari 5068](/hadith/bukhari/5068)), he forbade Ali from taking a second wife alongside his daughter Fatima because polygyny would distress and harm her ([Sahih al-Bukhari 5230](/hadith/bukhari/5230)).
4:3.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: When a man fears he cannot afford or deal justly with multiple free wives, [Quran 4:3](quran://4/3) directs him to marry only one free woman or resort to "what your right hands possess" (*mā malakat aymānukum*)—enslaved female captives owned as chattel property ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:3](ibnkathir://4/3), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:3](tabari://4/3)). Classical jurisprudence confirms that sexual access to enslaved concubines required neither a marriage contract, the woman's consent, nor a numerical cap, because captives lacked the legal protections and maintenance rights of free wives (cf. [Sahih al-Bukhari 97](/hadith/bukhari/97)).

4:11.Devalues Women: Codifying structural economic inequality by gender, [Quran 4:11](quran://4/11) decrees that a male heir receives "the equivalent of the share of two females" and caps sole or multiple daughters without brothers at one-half or two-thirds of the estate ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:11](ibnkathir://4/11)). Even though classical jurisprudence relieves women of mandatory household financial maintenance, halving female inheritance structurally enforces lifelong female financial dependence on male relatives, contrasting with the equal spiritual and personal dignity of men and women in Christ ([Galatians 3:28](bible://gal/3/28)).
4:11.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: The rigid fixed fractions assigned in [Quran 4:11](quran://4/11) and [Quran 4:12](quran://4/12) contain no rule for fractional overflow, producing totals exceeding 100% of the estate when specified heirs coexist. If a deceased man leaves a wife (1/8 = 3/24 under [Quran 4:12](quran://4/12)), both parents (1/6 + 1/6 = 8/24), and three daughters (2/3 = 16/24), the mandated Quranic shares sum to 27/24 (112.5%), forcing post-prophetic jurists under Caliph Umar to invent *ʿawl* (proportional share reduction) to resolve an arithmetic inconsistency absent from the text itself.

4:12.Devalues Women: Extending the 2:1 gender disparity of [Quran 4:11](quran://4/11) to surviving spouses, [Quran 4:12](quran://4/12) awards a widower one-half of his childless wife's estate (or one-fourth if she had children) while restricting a widow to only one-fourth of a childless husband's estate and one-eighth if he left children ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:12](ibnkathir://4/12)). Under polygyny ([Quran 4:3](quran://4/3)), up to four co-widows must divide that single one-eighth share among themselves—leaving each widow as little as 1/32 of the estate ([Tafsir al-Tabari 4:12](tabari://4/12)).
4:12.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: When the spousal fractions of [Quran 4:12](quran://4/12) combine with parental and collateral shares in [Quran 4:11](quran://4/11) and [Quran 4:176](quran://4/176), the prescribed inheritance shares mathematically exceed the total estate. In the landmark *ʿawl* case adjudicated after Muhammad's death, a woman survived by a husband (1/2 = 3/6), a mother (1/6), and two full sisters (2/3 = 4/6 under [Quran 4:176](quran://4/176)) generated mandated shares totaling 8/6 (133.3%), demonstrating that the fixed fractional system was formulated without accounting for simultaneous statutory heirs.

4:15.Devalues Women: Targeting women exclusively with indefinite domestic imprisonment, [Quran 4:15](quran://4/15) commands that wives convicted of sexual immorality by four male witnesses be confined inside houses "until death takes them, or God makes a way for them," contrasting sharply with the mild call to repentance in [Quran 4:16](quran://4/16). As recorded in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:15](ibnkathir://4/15) and [Sahih Muslim 1690a](/hadith/muslim/1690a), Muhammad later declared this interim ruling abrogated by one hundred lashes for unmarried offenders ([Quran 24:2](quran://24/2)) and stoning to death for married offenders.

4:24.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: Immediately after prohibiting sexual relations with married women, [Quran 4:24](quran://4/24) carves out the explicit exception "except what your right hands possess" (*illā mā malakat aymānukum*), authorizing Muslim soldiers to have sexual relations with married non-Muslim women captured in battle. [Sahih Muslim 1456a](/hadith/muslim/1456a), [Sahih al-Bukhari 2229](/hadith/bukhari/2229), and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:24](ibnkathir://4/24) record that this verse was revealed after the Battle of Awtas (AD 630) specifically to overcome companions' hesitation about sleeping with captive wives whose non-Muslim husbands were still alive.
4:24.Devalues Women: This verse strips captured wives of marital protection and bodily autonomy upon enslavement ([Sahih Muslim 1456a](/hadith/muslim/1456a)) and frames female sexuality transactionally through the clause "those of them you have enjoyed (*istamtaʿtum*), give them their wages." Early companions including Ibn Abbas and Ubayy ibn Ka'b read and cited [Quran 4:24](quran://4/24) as sanctioning temporary fixed-term pleasure marriage (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) in exchange for a handful of dates or flour ([Sahih Muslim 1405d](/hadith/muslim/1405d), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:24](tabari://4/24)), standing in stark contrast to biblical covenantal marriage ([Matthew 19:5](bible://mt/19/5)–[Matthew 19:6](bible://mt/19/6)).

4:25.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: Codifying a two-tier caste hierarchy between free and enslaved women, [Quran 4:25](quran://4/25) treats marriage to believing slave women purely as a concession for indigent free men who cannot afford free wives, requires the slave owner's permission (*bi-idhni ahlihinna*) to wed them, and assigns enslaved wives "half of the punishment" of free women ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:25](ibnkathir://4/25), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:25](tabari://4/25)). Rather than abolishing human bondage, the text embeds chattel ownership and diminished slave legal status permanently into sacred family and penal law.

4:34.Devalues Women: Establishing male authority (*qawwāmūna*) over women on the grounds of divine preference and financial expenditure, [Quran 4:34](quran://4/34) authorizes husbands who merely fear defiance (*nushūz*) from their wives to admonish them, banish them in bed, and physically strike them (*wa-ḍribūhunna*). Classical exegetes ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:34](ibnkathir://4/34), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:34](tabari://4/34)) and canonical hadiths ([Sahih Muslim 1218a](/hadith/muslim/1218a), [Sahih al-Bukhari 5825](/hadith/bukhari/5825), [Sahih al-Bukhari 5204](/hadith/bukhari/5204)) confirm literal physical beating—stipulating only that it remain "not severe" (*ghayr mubarriḥ*)—in contrast to the New Testament command that husbands love their wives sacrificially as Christ loved the church ([Ephesians 5:25](bible://eph/5/25)).

4:43.Theological Defect: Rather than prohibiting intoxicants outright, [Quran 4:43](quran://4/43) merely instructs believers not to approach prayer while drunk—an interim stage revealed after wine was praised as good provision in [Quran 16:67](quran://16/67) and before intoxicants were condemned as Satan's handiwork in [Quran 5:90](quran://5/90) ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:43](ibnkathir://4/43)). Such reactive, multi-stage reversal of divine moral legislation reflects situational accommodation to companion conduct rather than an eternal, unchanging moral standard.

4:46.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Targeting "those who are Jews" collectively, [Quran 4:46](quran://4/46) accuses them of twisting words out of context and pronounces a sweeping divine curse upon them ("God has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe, except a few"). Both [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:46](ibnkathir://4/46) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:46](tabari://4/46) generalize this polemic as proof of enduring Jewish obstinacy and divine rejection, fostering communal antagonism against Jewish populations.

4:47.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Addressing seventh-century Jews and Christians directly as "You who have been given the Book," [Quran 4:47](quran://4/47) commands them to believe in what Allah sent down "confirming what is with you" (*muṣaddiqan limā maʿakum*; [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:47](tabari://4/47)). By appealing to the Scriptures physically in their possession as an intact standard of confirmation, the Quran concedes the textual preservation of the seventh-century Torah and Gospel—whose manuscripts attest teachings that contradict Islamic theology.
4:47.Promotes Division & Discrimination: To compel Jewish and Christian conversion, [Quran 4:47](quran://4/47) threatens the People of the Book that Allah will "obliterate faces and turn them backward, or curse them as We cursed the companions of the Sabbath"—invoking the narrative of Israelites transformed into despised apes in [Quran 2:65](quran://2/65) ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:47](ibnkathir://4/47)). Using threats of physical disfigurement and dehumanizing curses to coerce religious submission stands antithetical to peaceful persuasion and freedom of conscience.

4:48.Theological Defect: Declaring *shirk* (associating partners with Allah) categorically unforgivable while asserting that Allah pardons "anything less than that for whomever He pleases," [Quran 4:48](quran://4/48) allows grave moral crimes such as murder, theft, and adultery to be waived by arbitrary divine fiat without atonement—confirmed in [Sahih al-Bukhari 7487](/hadith/bukhari/7487). Moreover, its absolute rule that Allah never forgives *shirk* conflicts internally with [Quran 4:153](quran://4/153), which states that after the Israelites committed blatant idolatrous *shirk* by worshiping the Golden Calf, "We pardoned that" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:48](ibnkathir://4/48)).
4:48.Contradicts the Bible: Because the Quran classifies Christian worship of Jesus as the divine Son under *shirk* ([Quran 5:72](quran://5/72)), [Quran 4:48](quran://4/48) consigns Trinitarian believers to unforgivable damnation while offering discretionary pardon without a mediator for all other sins. This directly opposes biblical soteriology, wherein all sin violates God's holiness and requires propitiatory atonement through Christ's blood ([Romans 3:25](bible://rom/3/25)), while every sin and blasphemy—except final, unrepentant rejection of the Holy Spirit—can be forgiven through repentance ([Matthew 12:31](bible://mt/12/31)).

4:51.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Speaking of "those who have been given a portion of the Book," [Quran 4:51](quran://4/51) accuses Jewish scholars of believing in *al-Jibt* (sorcery) and *al-Ṭāghūt* (false deities/devils) and preferring pagan polytheists over Muslims, immediately followed by Allah's collective curse in [Quran 4:52](quran://4/52) ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:51](ibnkathir://4/51), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:51](tabari://4/51)). Casting monotheistic People of the Book as sorcery-believing allies of idolatry embeds enduring interreligious hostility into sacred scripture.

4:74.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Explicitly linking eternal salvation to lethal battlefield combat, [Quran 4:74](quran://4/74) commands those who trade this present life for the Hereafter to "fight in the way of God" (*falyuqātil fī sabīli llāhi*) and guarantees a "great reward" whether the fighter is killed or conquers ([Tafsir al-Tabari 4:74](tabari://4/74), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:74](ibnkathir://4/74)). Sanctifying armed conquest and martyrdom in war as the supreme transaction for Paradise contrasts directly with Jesus's repudiation of the sword ([Matthew 26:52](bible://mt/26/52)) and declaration that His kingdom is not of this world ([John 18:36](bible://jn/18/36)).

4:76.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Dividing humanity into a militant binary where believers fight for Allah and disbelievers fight for *al-Ṭāghūt* (false deities/Satan), [Quran 4:76](quran://4/76) issues the direct imperative "So fight against the allies of Satan!" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:76](ibnkathir://4/76), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:76](tabari://4/76)). Branding human non-believers as satanic combatants to be subdued through physical warfare directly opposes the New Testament teaching that spiritual warfare is waged not against flesh and blood ([Ephesians 6:12](bible://eph/6/12)) and that believers must love their enemies ([Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44)).

4:77.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Recording the historical shift from Meccan non-violence to Medinan militarism, [Quran 4:77](quran://4/77) recalls how believers were earlier told "Restrain your hands" (*kuffū aydiyakum*), yet once armed warfare was prescribed upon them (*kutiba ʿalayhimu l-qitāl*), those reluctant to fight were rebuked for fearing men as they ought to fear God ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:77](ibnkathir://4/77), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:77](tabari://4/77)). Classical exegesis cites this passage to confirm that early peaceful restraint was tactical and temporary until the Muslim polity gained military strength.

4:82.Failed Prophecy: Staking its claim to divine authorship on an explicit falsification test, [Quran 4:82](quran://4/82) asserts: "If it had been from (someone) other than God, surely they would have found in it much contradiction (*ikhtilāfan kathīran*)" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:82](ibnkathir://4/82)). Yet the Quran exhibits substantive internal discrepancies—including inheritance fractions summing above 100% ([Quran 4:11](quran://4/11)–[Quran 4:12](quran://4/12)), *shirk* declared unforgivable in [Quran 4:48](quran://4/48) yet pardoned in [Quran 4:153](quran://4/153), six-day creation ([Quran 7:54](quran://7/54)) versus eight-day creation ([Quran 41:9](quran://41/9)–[Quran 41:12](quran://41/12)), and divine abrogation ([Quran 2:106](quran://2/106))—failing its own internal criterion.

4:88.Theological Defect: Questioning why Muslims were divided over defectors, [Quran 4:88](quran://4/88) declares that "God has overthrown them for what they have earned" and asks rhetorically, "Do you wish to guide someone whom God has led astray (*man aḍalla llāhu*)? Whomever God leads astray – you will not find a way for him" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:88](ibnkathir://4/88)). Making God the active agent who misguides human beings and forecloses any path to repentance conflicts with the biblical portrait of God who takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked and calls all people everywhere to repent and live ([Ezekiel 18:23](bible://ez/18/23), [Acts 17:30](bible://acts/17/30)).

4:89.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Describing unbelievers and defectors who wish Muslims would abandon Islam, [Quran 4:89](quran://4/89) forbids taking them as allies until they emigrate and commands: "If they turn back, seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from them an ally or a helper" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:89](ibnkathir://4/89), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:89](tabari://4/89)). Alongside Muhammad's explicit decree "Whoever changes his Islamic religion, kill him" ([Sahih al-Bukhari 3017](/hadith/bukhari/3017), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4341](/hadith/bukhari/4341)), this verse provides scriptural grounding for lethal coercion against apostasy and religious defection.

4:91.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Addressing wavering tribal groups seeking neutrality with both Muslims and their own people, [Quran 4:91](quran://4/91) commands that unless they withdraw, offer peace, and restrain their hands, Muslims must "seize them and kill them wherever you come upon them," concluding that Allah has granted "clear authority" against them ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:91](ibnkathir://4/91), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:91](tabari://4/91)). Treating non-alignment and suspected disloyalty as capital offenses punishable on sight exemplifies coercive political-religious enforcement.

4:95.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Establishing a spiritual caste hierarchy based on military participation, [Quran 4:95](quran://4/95) proclaims that peaceful believers who stay at home are not equal to armed fighters (*al-mujāhidūna*) striving with their wealth and lives, elevating warriors "in rank above the ones sitting (at home)" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:95](ibnkathir://4/95), [Sahih Muslim 1898a](/hadith/muslim/1898a)). Conditioning supreme divine favor on physical warfare stands in direct antithesis to Christ's beatitude "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God" ([Matthew 5:9](bible://mt/5/9)).
4:95.Theological Defect: According to multiple canonical reports from Muhammad's scribe Zayd ibn Thabit and al-Bara' ([Sahih al-Bukhari 4990](/hadith/bukhari/4990), [Sahih al-Bukhari 2831](/hadith/bukhari/2831)), Muhammad initially dictated [Quran 4:95](quran://4/95) without any disability exemption until the blind companion Ibn Umm Maktum protested his blindness on the spot, prompting an immediate revision inserting "other than the injured" (*ghayru ulī ḍ-ḍarar*). An ad-hoc textual amendment triggered in real time by a human bystander's objection challenges the Sunni dogma of an eternally pre-existent, uncreated Quran inscribed verbatim on a heavenly tablet ([Quran 85:21](quran://85/21)–[Quran 85:22](quran://85/22)).

4:101.Promotes Division & Discrimination: While permitting shortened prayers on journeys for fear of attack, [Quran 4:101](quran://4/101) concludes with the unqualified categorical generalization: "Surely the disbelievers are a clear enemy to you" (*inna l-kāfirīna kānū lakum ʿaduwwan mubīnā*; [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:101](ibnkathir://4/101), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:101](tabari://4/101)). Defining non-Muslims intrinsically as "clear enemies" institutionalizes permanent suspicion toward outsiders, contrasting with Christ's command to love one's enemies and pray for persecutors ([Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44)).

4:104.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Urging sustained offensive military pressure, [Quran 4:104](quran://4/104) commands believers: "Do not weaken in pursuit of the people! If you are suffering, surely they too are suffering just as you are suffering, while you hope from God what they do not hope for" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:104](ibnkathir://4/104), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:104](tabari://4/104)). Incentivizing relentless armed pursuit of non-Muslim adversaries through exclusive promises of afterlife reward sanctifies protracted warfare as an instrument of divine service.

4:116.Theological Defect: Reiterating the moral asymmetry of [Quran 4:48](quran://4/48), [Quran 4:116](quran://4/116) asserts that Allah never forgives *shirk* while pardoning "anything less than that for whomever He pleases"—a passage revealed in connection with Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq, a Medinan thief who stole armor, framed an innocent person, and then apostatized in Mecca ([Tafsir al-Tabari 4:116](tabari://4/116), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:116](ibnkathir://4/116)). Treating serious ethical crimes against fellow humans as arbitrarily pardonable without restitution or atonement while treating theological dissent from Islam as eternally unforgivable prioritizes sectarian allegiance over universal moral justice.

4:128.Devalues Women: Exposing a stark legal double standard in marital conflict, whereas [Quran 4:34](quran://4/34) permits a husband who fears *nushūz* (defiance) from his wife to banish and physically strike her, [Quran 4:128](quran://4/128) decrees that when a wife fears *nushūz* (ill-treatment, cruelty, or aversion) or desertion from her husband, the couple should simply "make peace" by the wife relinquishing her own marital rights ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:128](ibnkathir://4/128)). Canonical hadiths confirm this verse was revealed when Muhammad's aging wife Sawdah bint Zam'ah feared he would divorce her and surrendered her conjugal turn to young Aisha just to remain married ([Sahih al-Bukhari 5212](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5212), [Sahih Muslim 1463a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1463a)).

4:129.Devalues Women: Directly undermining the justice prerequisite of [Quran 4:3](quran://4/3) ("if you fear that you will not act justly, then marry only one"), [Quran 4:129](quran://4/129) openly concedes: "You will never be able to act justly between women, even though you are eager (to do so)" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:129](ibnkathir://4/129), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:129](tabari://4/129)). Rather than abolishing polygyny upon admitting its inherent emotional and practical inequity, the verse retains plural marriage and merely asks husbands not to leave an unfavored co-wife completely "like one left hanging"—neither cared for as a wife nor freed to remarry.

4:136.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Addressing Muslims directly, [Quran 4:136](quran://4/136) commands them to believe in God, His messenger, the Book sent down to him, "and the Book which He sent down before," warning that whoever disbelieves in Allah's Books "has gone far astray" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:136](ibnkathir://4/136)). Requiring seventh-century Muslims to place active faith in the previously revealed Scriptures presupposes that the extant Torah and Gospel remained recognizable, authoritative Books of God rather than lost or falsified texts.

4:139.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Condemning those "who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers," [Quran 4:139](quran://4/139) mocks the idea that any honor or dignity could be found among non-Muslims, asserting "Surely honor belongs to God – all (of it)!" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:139](ibnkathir://4/139), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:139](tabari://4/139)). Prohibiting supportive bonds across religious lines and denying honorable standing to non-believers enforces social segregation along confessional boundaries.

4:142.Theological Defect: Describing the hypocrites as attempting to deceive God, [Quran 4:142](quran://4/142) explicitly attributes active deception to Allah Himself: "They (try to) deceive God, when He is deceiving them (*wa-huwa khādiʿuhum*)" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:142](ibnkathir://4/142), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:142](tabari://4/142); cf. [Quran 3:54](quran://3/54)). Predicating deceit (*khidāʿ*) directly of the divine nature compromises God's moral perfection and stands in sharp opposition to the biblical revelation of God "who never lies" ([Titus 1:2](bible://ti/1/2), [Numbers 23:19](bible://nm/23/19)).

4:143.Theological Defect: Depicting wavering hypocrites suspended between faith and unbelief, [Quran 4:143](quran://4/143) asserts that for anyone whom Allah Himself misguides (*man yuḍlili llāhu*), no human path to guidance exists ([Tafsir al-Tabari 4:143](tabari://4/143), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:143](ibnkathir://4/143)). Attributing human spiritual lostness to God's own active misguidance removes genuine moral agency and renders divine condemnation of the misguided ethically incoherent.

4:144.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Issuing a direct prohibition to the entire Muslim community, [Quran 4:144](quran://4/144) commands: "You who believe! Do not take disbelievers as allies (*awliyāʾ*) instead of the believers. Do you wish to make for God clear authority against you?" [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:144](ibnkathir://4/144) explains that Allah forbids believers from befriending non-Muslims, offering them sincere counsel, or cultivating close companionship with them under threat of divine punishment.

4:153.Contradicts the Bible: Claiming that the Israelites demanded of Moses at Sinai, "Show us God openly!" and were struck by a lethal lightning bolt for their audacity ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:153](ibnkathir://4/153)), [Quran 4:153](quran://4/153) inverts the biblical Sinai account, where the terrified Israelites begged Moses *not* to let God address them directly lest they die ([Exodus 20:18](bible://ex/20/18)–[Exodus 20:19](bible://ex/20/19), [Deuteronomy 5:25](bible://dt/5/25)), while only seventy elders beheld the God of Israel peacefully without being harmed ([Exodus 24:9](bible://ex/24/9)–[Exodus 24:11](bible://ex/24/11)). Furthermore, its statement that Allah pardoned Israel's Golden Calf idolatry contradicts [Quran 4:48](quran://4/48)'s rule that Allah never forgives *shirk*.

4:154.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Asserting as historical fact that "We raised the mountain above them at their covenant" ([Quran 4:154](quran://4/154); cf. [Quran 2:63](quran://2/63), [Quran 7:171](quran://7/171)), the Quran recounts Allah physically uprooting and suspending Mount Sinai over the Israelites' heads to coerce obedience ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:154](ibnkathir://4/154), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:154](tabari://4/154)). This episode is absent from [Exodus 19:17](bible://ex/19/17), where Israel simply stood "at the foot of the mountain" (*be-taḥtît hā-hār*), and derives directly from a late rabbinic homiletical midrash in the Babylonian Talmud (*Shabbat* 88a; *Avodah Zarah* 2b) playing literally on the Hebrew preposition "under" to imagine Sinai held overhead like an inverted barrel.

4:155.Theological Defect: Enumerating covenantal accusations against the Jewish people, [Quran 4:155](quran://4/155) states that Allah placed a divine seal upon their hearts (*ṭabaʿa llāhu ʿalayhā*) because of unbelief, leaving all save a small remnant unable to believe ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:155](ibnkathir://4/155), [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:155](tabari://4/155)). Asserting that God Himself permanently sealed Jewish hearts against faith while simultaneously condemning them to eternal punishment for failing to believe exemplifies fatalistic divine determinism.

4:157.Contradicts the Bible: Denying the central redemptive event of the Bible, [Quran 4:157](quran://4/157) asserts regarding Jesus the Messiah: "Yet they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it seemed like that to them (*wa-lākin shubbiha lahum*)." Written six centuries after the first-century eyewitness Gospels, this denial directly contradicts Old Testament Messianic prophecy ([Isaiah 53:5](bible://is/53/5)–[Isaiah 53:12](bible://is/53/12), [Psalms 22:16](bible://ps/22/16)) and the unanimous apostolic testimony to Christ's public crucifixion and death ([Matthew 27:35](bible://mt/27/35), [John 19:30](bible://jn/19/30), [Acts 2:23](bible://acts/2/23)).
4:157.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: By claiming in the seventh century that Jesus of Nazareth was neither crucified nor killed ([Quran 4:157](quran://4/157)), the Quran rejects one of the best-documented events of ancient Mediterranean history (c. AD 30–33). Across modern critical historiography, Jesus's execution by crucifixion under the Roman prefect Pontius Pilate is universally recognized as bedrock historical fact, independently corroborated by first- and second-century non-Christian historians including Tacitus (*Annals* 15.44) and Flavius Josephus (*Antiquities* 18.3.3) alongside multiple first-century Christian sources.
4:157.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: To explain *shubbiha lahum* ("it was made to appear so to them"), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:157](ibnkathir://4/157) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:157](tabari://4/157) transmit traditions that Allah cast Jesus's physical likeness onto a substitute companion who was crucified in his place while onlookers watched. This substitution motif closely echoes second- and third-century Gnostic Docetic writings—such as the *Second Treatise of the Great Seth* and Irenaeus's report of Basilides (*Against Heresies* 1.24.4)—which invented phantom or substitute crucifixions because Gnostic dualism viewed matter and bodily suffering as beneath a heavenly emissary.
4:157.Theological Defect: Under the substitution interpretation endorsed by [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:157](ibnkathir://4/157) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 4:157](tabari://4/157), Allah Himself miraculously disguised another person as Jesus at Calvary, deceiving Jesus's own devoted disciples and mother into witnessing his crucifixion and proclaiming his resurrection. Such a scenario makes Allah the direct author of a massive historical illusion that inadvertently founded global Christianity—and then held billions of Christians eternally culpable ([Quran 5:72](quran://5/72)) for believing the very sensory evidence Allah Himself staged.

4:158.Contradicts the Bible: Completing the crucifixion denial of [Quran 4:157](quran://4/157), [Quran 4:158](quran://4/158) claims "Rather, God raised him to Himself" *instead* of allowing Jesus to die on the cross ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:158](ibnkathir://4/158)). In the New Testament, Christ's bodily ascension to the Father occurs forty days *after* His atoning death and bodily resurrection from the tomb ([Luke 24:46](bible://lk/24/46)–[Luke 24:51](bible://lk/24/51), [Acts 1:3](bible://acts/1/3), [Acts 1:9](bible://acts/1/9)); bypassing the cross eliminates the substitutionary sacrifice by which sinners are reconciled to God.
4:158.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Even while disputing Calvary, [Quran 4:158](quran://4/158) explicitly concedes Jesus's bodily ascension alive into God's heavenly presence ("Rather, God raised him to Himself"), with [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:158](ibnkathir://4/158) affirming that Jesus remains alive in heaven and will descend before the Day of Judgment. This concession places Jesus in an exalted heavenly status unmatched by Muhammad, whose body died and remained buried in Medina.

4:171.Contradicts the Bible: Addressing Christians directly, [Quran 4:171](quran://4/171) commands "do not say, 'Three'" and asserts that "God is far above having a son," reducing the Messiah Jesus to "only the messenger of God." This polemic flatly contradicts Jesus's own Trinitarian baptismal commission in the singular name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit ([Matthew 28:19](bible://mt/28/19)) and the apostolic proclamation of the eternal divine Son made flesh ([John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1), [John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14), [Colossians 2:9](bible://col/2/9)).
4:171.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Even while contesting Christ's deity, [Quran 4:171](quran://4/171) uniquely titles Jesus "His Word (*kalimatuhu*) which He cast into Mary, and a Spirit from Him (*rūḥun minhu*)"—titles applied to no other prophet in Islam and reaffirmed in [Sahih al-Bukhari 3435](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3435), [Sahih al-Bukhari 7440](/hadith/bukhari/7440), and [Sahih al-Bukhari 4712](/hadith/bukhari/4712). Because mainstream Sunni theology maintains that Allah's Word is an eternal, uncreated attribute of God—supported by Muhammad seeking refuge in Allah's perfect Words ([Sahih Muslim 2708a](/hadith/muslim/2708a)), since seeking refuge in anything created is *shirk*—identifying Jesus personally as God's Word inadvertently concedes the Johannine Logos Christology of [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1).

4:176.Devalues Women: Concluding Surah an-Nisa' with collateral (*kalālah*) inheritance law for an estate without parents or children, [Quran 4:176](quran://4/176) reiterates the 2:1 gender inequality of [Quran 4:11](quran://4/11): a surviving brother inherits a childless sister's entire estate, whereas a surviving single sister receives only one-half of her brother's estate, and mixed brothers and sisters divide shares so that "for the male is the equivalent of the share of two females" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:176](ibnkathir://4/176)).
4:176.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Assigning two-thirds of a *kalālah* estate to two or more sisters in [Quran 4:176](quran://4/176) directly produces the historic *ʿawl* mathematical contradiction when combined with [Quran 4:12](quran://4/12) and [Quran 4:11](quran://4/11). When a deceased woman leaves a husband (entitled to 1/2 = 3/6 under [Quran 4:12](quran://4/12)), a mother (1/6 under [Quran 4:11](quran://4/11)), and two sisters (2/3 = 4/6 under [Quran 4:176](quran://4/176)), the divinely mandated fractions total 8/6 (133.3% of the estate)—or 9/6 (150%) if the mother's 1/3 share applies—proving the fractional schedule cannot be executed as written.

5:5.Devalues Women: Codifying one-directional interfaith marriage rules, [Quran 5:5](quran://5/5) permits Muslim men to marry chaste Jewish and Christian women ("those who have been given the Book before you"), whereas Islamic law—grounded in [Quran 2:221](quran://2/221) and [Quran 60:10](quran://60/10) ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:5](ibnkathir://5/5))—strictly forbids Muslim women from marrying Jewish or Christian men. This gender asymmetry treats wives as legally subordinate to their husbands' religious authority and uses marriage demographics to ensure patriarchal confessional dominance.

5:13.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Speaking of the Children of Israel, [Quran 5:13](quran://5/13) pronounces a divine curse upon them, declares that Allah made their hearts hard, and instructs Muhammad: "You will continue to see treachery from them, except for a few of them" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:13](ibnkathir://5/13), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:13](tabari://5/13)). Presenting ongoing treachery (*khāʾinah*) and divinely hardened hearts as persistent traits of nearly all Jews embeds an enduring stereotype of collective untrustworthiness into scripture.

5:14.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Targeting "those who say, 'Surely we are Christians,'" [Quran 5:14](quran://5/14) asserts that Christians forgot a portion of their covenant and that Allah therefore stirred up permanent "enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:14](ibnkathir://5/14)). Depicting all Christian communities as divinely consigned to irreconcilable mutual hatred until the end of time delegitimizes Christian fellowship and fuels sectarian contempt.
5:14.Theological Defect: In [Quran 5:14](quran://5/14), Allah explicitly claims first-person moral authorship over Christian discord: "So We stirred up (*fa-aghraynā*) enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection" ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:14](tabari://5/14), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:14](ibnkathir://5/14)). Portraying God as actively instigating perpetual malice and sectarian animosity among human beings contradicts the holiness of the biblical "God of peace" ([Romans 15:33](bible://rom/15/33), [Hebrews 13:20](bible://heb/13/20)), whose Son prayed for believers' loving unity ([John 17:21](bible://jn/17/21)).

5:15.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Addressing Jews and Christians directly as "People of the Book," [Quran 5:15](quran://5/15) claims Muhammad came "making clear to you much of what you have been hiding (*tukhfūna*) of the Book" ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:15](tabari://5/15), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:15](ibnkathir://5/15)). One can conceal or withhold only an authentic document currently in one's possession; accusing seventh-century Jews and Christians of hiding passages presupposes that their extant written Scriptures remained textually intact rather than rewritten—yet our surviving pre-Islamic biblical manuscripts contain the very doctrines Islam rejects.

5:17.Contradicts the Bible: Declaring unconditionally, "Certainly they have disbelieved (*laqad kafara*) – those who say, 'Surely God is the Messiah, son of Mary,'" [Quran 5:17](quran://5/17) argues that no one could stop Allah "if He wished to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:17](ibnkathir://5/17)). Aside from mischaracterizing Trinitarian theology as equating Jesus exhaustively with the Father rather than the incarnate Word, branding belief in Christ's deity as unbelief directly contradicts the New Testament proclamation of Jesus as "our great God and Savior" ([Titus 2:13](bible://ti/2/13), [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1), [John 20:28](bible://jn/20/28), [Colossians 2:9](bible://col/2/9)).

5:18.Contradicts the Bible: Rebuking Jews and Christians for saying, "We are the sons of God, and His beloved," [Quran 5:18](quran://5/18) retorts, "Why then does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are mortals (*bashar*) from among those He created" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:18](ibnkathir://5/18), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:18](tabari://5/18)).
