This objection misunderstands and rejects a foundational teaching of both Testaments: God adopts believers as His covenant children ([Exodus 4:22](bible://ex/4/22), [John 1:12](bible://jn/1/12), [Romans 8:15](bible://rom/8/15), [Galatians 4:5](bible://gal/4/5)–[Galatians 4:6](bible://gal/4/6)) and disciplines them precisely *because* a loving Father corrects the children He loves ([Proverbs 3:12](bible://prv/3/12), [Hebrews 12:6](bible://heb/12/6)).

5:20.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Placing a speech in the mouth of Moses to the Exodus-era Israelites prior to entering Canaan ([Quran 5:21](quran://5/21)), [Quran 5:20](quran://5/20) has Moses say: "My people! Remember the blessing of God on you, when He made prophets among you, and made you kings (*wa-jaʿalakum mulūkan*)". Historically, Israel had zero Israelite kings during or prior to Moses's lifetime—even throughout the subsequent era of the Judges "there was no king in Israel" ([Judges 21:25](bible://jgs/21/25)) until Saul was anointed more than three centuries later ([Acts 13:20](bible://acts/13/20)–[Acts 13:21](bible://acts/13/21))—forcing commentators in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:20](ibnkathir://5/20) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:20](tabari://5/20) to redefine "kings" metaphorically as any commoner owning a house, a wife, and a servant.
5:20.Contradicts the Bible: Having Moses remind wilderness-generation Israelites that God had already "made prophets among you, and made you kings" ([Quran 5:20](quran://5/20)) conflicts directly with the biblical historical record, where Moses merely *foretold* that future generations after settling Canaan would one day ask to set a king over themselves ([Deuteronomy 17:14](bible://dt/17/14)) and Israel remained governed by tribal elders and judges without any monarchy for centuries until Saul ([Judges 17:6](bible://jgs/17/6), [Acts 13:20](bible://acts/13/20)–[Acts 13:21](bible://acts/13/21)).

5:31.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Following Cain's murder of Abel, [Quran 5:31](quran://5/31) recounts that "God sent a raven scratching in the earth, to show him how to hide the nakedness of his brother" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:31](ibnkathir://5/31), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:31](tabari://5/31)). This raven-burial episode is completely absent from the biblical account in [Genesis 4:8](bible://gn/4/8)–[Genesis 4:16](bible://gn/4/16) and reproduces post-biblical Jewish aggadic folklore preserved in *Midrash Tanhuma* (*Bereshit* 10) and *Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer* 21 (where ravens scratch the ground to bury a dead raven and teach Abel's burial), incorporating uninspired rabbinic legend into the Quran as historical revelation.

5:32.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Linked directly to the Cain-and-Abel raven story of [Quran 5:31](quran://5/31) by the transition "Because of that (*min ajli dhālika*), We prescribed for the Sons of Israel: Whoever kills a person... it is as if he killed all the people, and whoever gives life to one, it is as if he gave life to all the people" ([Quran 5:32](quran://5/32); [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:32](tabari://5/32)), this passage reproduces a famous rabbinic homily from *Mishnah Sanhedrin* 4:5 (compiled c. AD 200). In *Mishnah Sanhedrin* 4:5, rabbis commented on the plural "bloods" (*demê*) of Abel in [Genesis 4:10](bible://gn/4/10) to warn court witnesses about the value of a single life—meaning the Quran mistook a human Talmudic legal reflection on Genesis for a direct legislative decree spoken by God to Israel.

5:33.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Mandating corporal terror as divine penal law, [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33) decrees that the retribution for those who fight Allah and His Messenger and spread corruption (*fasād*) in the land is "that they be killed, or crucified, or their hands and their feet be cut off on opposite sides, or they be banished from the land." Classical commentaries ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:33](ibnkathir://5/33), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:33](tabari://5/33)) and canonical hadiths ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6802](/hadith/bukhari/6802), [Sahih al-Bukhari 233](/hadith/bukhari/233), [Sahih Muslim 1671a](/hadith/muslim/1671a)) tie this verse directly to Muhammad amputating the hands and feet of the 'Ukl and 'Uraynah tribesmen, branding their eyes with heated irons, and leaving them in the stony desert of al-Harrah begging for water until they died.

5:38.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Prescribing permanent bodily mutilation for property offenses, [Quran 5:38](quran://5/38) commands: "As for the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands as retribution for what they have earned – an exemplary punishment from God" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:38](ibnkathir://5/38)). Canonical hadiths confirm that Muhammad enforced irreversible hand amputation for thefts worth as little as a quarter of a dinar or a three-dirham shield ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6789](/hadith/bukhari/6789), [Sahih Muslim 1684a](/hadith/muslim/1684a), [Sahih Muslim 1686a](/hadith/muslim/1686a)), contrasting sharply with Mosaic financial restitution ([Exodus 22:1](bible://ex/22/1)) and the New Testament ethic of redemptive labor and generosity ([Ephesians 4:28](bible://eph/4/28)).

5:41.Theological Defect: Speaking of Medinan Jews and hypocrites who rush into disbelief ([Sahih Muslim 1700a](/hadith/muslim/1700a)), [Quran 5:41](quran://5/41) states: "Those are the ones whose hearts God does not wish to purify (*lam yuridi llāhu an yuṭahhira qulūbahum*). For them is disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:41](ibnkathir://5/41)). Asserting that God Himself wills *not* to purify sinners' hearts while consigning them to eternal torment for remaining impure undermines both divine mercy and coherent moral accountability.
5:41.Promotes Division & Discrimination: In [Quran 5:41](quran://5/41), Jewish interlocutors are characterized as avid "listeners to lies" and distorters of words whom Allah refuses to purify and marks for "disgrace in this world" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:41](ibnkathir://5/41), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:41](tabari://5/41)). Framing an entire neighboring religious community as spiritually irredeemable and divinely assigned to worldly humiliation reinforces social and legal subordination.

5:43.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Marveling that Medinan Jews brought a legal dispute to Muhammad ([Sahih Muslim 1699a](/hadith/muslim/1699a)), [Quran 5:43](quran://5/43) asks in the present tense: "Yet how do they make you their judge, when they have the Torah (*wa-ʿindahumu t-tawrātu*), containing the judgment of God?" ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:43](tabari://5/43), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:43](ibnkathir://5/43)). This explicit affirmation that seventh-century Jews physically possessed the Torah *containing God's authoritative judgment* refutes modern claims of pre-Islamic textual corruption (*taḥrīf al-lafẓ*), since the Hebrew Bible circulating in AD 630 is identical to the Masoretic and Dead Sea Scrolls text known today.

5:44.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Declaring "Surely We sent down the Torah, containing guidance and light," by which prophets, rabbis, and scholars judged, [Quran 5:44](quran://5/44) concludes unequivocally: "Whoever does not judge by what God has sent down – those are the disbelievers" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:44](ibnkathir://5/44), [Sahih Muslim 1700a](/hadith/muslim/1700a)). Requiring ongoing judicial obedience to the Torah under penalty of unbelief presupposes its continued textual integrity and divine authority in the seventh century.

5:45.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Quoting the Mosaic *lex talionis*—"life for life, eye for eye, nose for nose, ear for ear, tooth for tooth" ([Exodus 21:23](bible://ex/21/23)–[Exodus 21:25](bible://ex/21/25))—directly as what "We wrote for them in it," [Quran 5:45](quran://5/45) brands anyone failing to judge by Allah's revealed Torah statutes among "the evildoers" (*aẓ-ẓālimūn*; [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:45](tabari://5/45)). Identifying specific Exodus statutes inside the written Torah held by Muhammad's Jewish contemporaries confirms that the Quran refers to the actual canonical Pentateuch rather than a hypothetical lost scroll.

5:46.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Tracing divine revelation to Jesus son of Mary, [Quran 5:46](quran://5/46) states that Jesus came "confirming what was with him of the Torah" (*muṣaddiqan limā bayna yadayhi mina t-tawrāti*) and that Allah gave him the Gospel (*al-Injīl*) "containing guidance and light" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:46](ibnkathir://5/46), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:46](tabari://5/46)). Because Jesus confirmed the first-century Hebrew Scriptures—fully attested today by the pre-Christian Dead Sea Scrolls—the Old Testament cannot have been corrupted either before or after Christ's ministry.

5:47.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Formulating the sharpest horn of the Islamic Dilemma, [Quran 5:47](quran://5/47) commands seventh-century Christians in the present imperative: "So let the People of the Gospel judge by what God has sent down in it (*walyahkum ahlu l-injīli bimā anzala llāhu fīhi*)," pronouncing all who fail to judge by that revealed Gospel "the wicked" (*al-fāsiqūn*; [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:47](tabari://5/47)). If the seventh-century Gospel—preserved verbatim in fourth-century codices such as Sinaiticus and Vaticanus—had already been corrupted, Allah would be commanding Christians on pain of wickedness to judge by a falsified text; if it was uncorrupted, its testimony to Christ's deity ([John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1)) and crucifixion ([Luke 24:46](bible://lk/24/46)) falsifies the Quran.

5:48.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Addressing Muhammad directly, [Quran 5:48](quran://5/48) declares that Allah sent down the Book "confirming what was before it of the Book, and as a guardian/witness over it" (*muṣaddiqan limā bayna yadayhi mina l-kitābi wa-muhayminan ʿalayhi*; [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:48](tabari://5/48), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:48](ibnkathir://5/48)). By staking the Quran's legitimacy on confirming and safeguarding the prior Jewish and Christian Scriptures while simultaneously denying their core teachings on the Incarnation and Crucifixion, the Quran creates an irreconcilable self-contradiction.

5:51.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Issuing one of Islam's foundational social-boundary decrees, [Quran 5:51](quran://5/51) commands believers, "Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies/friends (*awliyāʾ*)," warning that "whoever of you takes them as allies is surely one of them" ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:51](tabari://5/51)). In [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:51](ibnkathir://5/51), classical exegesis cites this command to forbid trusting, befriending, or elevating Jews and Christians as "enemies of Islam and its people," contrasting sharply with Christ's Parable of the Good Samaritan ([Luke 10:29](bible://lk/10/29)–[Luke 10:37](bible://lk/10/37)) and command to love across ethnic and religious divides.

5:57.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Reinforcing the confessional separatism of [Quran 5:51](quran://5/51), [Quran 5:57](quran://5/57) commands believers not to take as *awliyāʾ* (allies or close friends) either "those who were given the Book before you, or the disbelievers" who mock Islamic rites ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:57](ibnkathir://5/57), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:57](tabari://5/57)). Rather than answering criticism through patient love, blessing, and persuasion ([Luke 6:27](bible://lk/6/27)–[Luke 6:28](bible://lk/6/28), [Romans 12:14](bible://rom/12/14)), the verse codifies communal estrangement from Jews, Christians, and other non-Muslims.

5:60.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Addressing the People of the Book ([Quran 5:59](quran://5/59)), [Quran 5:60](quran://5/60) rebukes them by invoking "Whomever God has cursed, and whomever He is angry with – some of whom He made apes, and pigs, and slaves of *al-Ṭāghūt*" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:60](ibnkathir://5/60), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:60](tabari://5/60); cf. [Quran 2:65](quran://2/65), [Quran 7:166](quran://7/166)). Associating Jewish and Christian interlocutors with people cursed under divine wrath and turned into apes and swine deploys dehumanizing polemic that has historically fueled anti-Jewish contempt.
5:60.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: In [Quran 5:60](quran://5/60) (alongside [Quran 2:65](quran://2/65) and [Quran 7:166](quran://7/166)), the Quran presents the physical transformation (*maskh*) of cursed human beings into literal apes and pigs as an actual historical punishment ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:60](ibnkathir://5/60)). Canonical hadiths rule out allegorical reinterpretation: when asked directly whether modern apes and swine descend from those metamorphosed people, Muhammad affirmed the literal bodily metamorphosis of ancient humans into apes and pigs while stating that metamorphosed humans died without leaving offspring ([Sahih Muslim 2663d](/hadith/muslim/2663d), [Sahih Muslim 2663b](/hadith/muslim/2663b)).

5:64.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Accuses the Jews of claiming that God's hand is tied, pronounces a divine curse upon them for their words, and declares that Allah Himself cast enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:64](ibnkathir://5/64), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:64](tabari://5/64)). By elevating collective condemnation of the Jewish people into permanent sacred writ, the verse institutionalizes interreligious hostility across generations.
5:64.Theological Defect: Asserts that Allah actively cast perpetual enmity and hatred (*al-ʿadāwata wa-l-baghḍāʾ*) among the Jews until the Day of Resurrection ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:64](tabari://5/64)), making God the direct author of ongoing communal malice and division rather than the God of peace ([Romans 15:33](bible://rom/15/33)) who commands reconciliation ([Matthew 5:9](bible://mt/5/9)).

5:66.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Declares that if seventh-century Jews and Christians had observed the Torah and the Gospel (*al-Tawrāh wa-l-Injīl*), God would have lavished provision upon them ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:66](ibnkathir://5/66), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:66](tabari://5/66)). This demand presupposes that the Jewish and Christian scriptures circulating in Muhammad's own lifetime remained textually intact, accessible, and divinely authoritative rather than lost or corrupted.

5:68.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Commands Muhammad to declare to the People of the Book that they stand on nothing until they observe the Torah and the Gospel ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:68](tabari://5/68)), reinforcing the Islamic Dilemma alongside [Quran 5:47](quran://5/47). Because extant pre-Islamic manuscripts demonstrate what the seventh-century Torah and Gospel contained, either Allah commanded obedience to corrupted scriptures, or those scriptures are reliable and refute the Quran's denial of Christ's deity ([John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1)) and crucifixion ([Mark 15:24](bible://mk/15/24)).

5:72.Contradicts the Bible: Condemns as disbelievers anyone confessing that God is the Messiah, son of Mary, and places on Jesus's lips a denial of His own divinity ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:72](ibnkathir://5/72)). This directly contradicts the New Testament Gospels, in which Jesus proclaims His pre-existent divine identity ([John 8:58](bible://jn/8/58)), declares His unity with the Father ([John 10:30](bible://jn/10/30)), and accepts Thomas's worshipful confession, 'My Lord and my God!' ([John 20:28](bible://jn/20/28)).

5:73.Contradicts the Bible: Denounces Christians as disbelievers for allegedly saying 'God is the third of three' (*thālithu thalāthah*, [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:73](tabari://5/73), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:73](ibnkathir://5/73)). Historic Trinitarian monotheism never teaches that God is one deity among a pantheon of three gods, but confesses one indivisible divine Being ([Deuteronomy 6:4](bible://dt/6/4)) eternally existing as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit ([Matthew 28:19](bible://mt/28/19)).

5:74.Contradicts the Bible: Summons Trinitarian Christians ([Quran 5:72](quran://5/72), [Quran 5:73](quran://5/73)) to repent and seek forgiveness for confessing Christ's deity and the Trinity ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:74](tabari://5/74)). This inverts the biblical Gospel, which teaches that forgiveness of sins and eternal life are received specifically by believing in Jesus as the divine Son of God ([John 8:24](bible://jn/8/24), [John 20:31](bible://jn/20/31), [Acts 4:12](bible://acts/4/12)).

5:75.Contradicts the Bible: Reduces the Messiah to 'only a messenger' like prophets who passed away before Him and argues that eating food alongside Mary disproves His divinity ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:75](tabari://5/75), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:75](ibnkathir://5/75)). That argument overlooks the Incarnation—where the eternal Word assumed true human flesh ([John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14), [Philippians 2:6](bible://phil/2/6), [Philippians 2:7](bible://phil/2/7)) and ate food even after rising bodily from the dead ([Luke 24:42](bible://lk/24/42), [Luke 24:43](bible://lk/24/43))—while mistakenly pairing Mary with Jesus in polemic against Christian worship.

5:78.Contradicts the Bible: Asserts that unbelieving Israelites were cursed 'by the tongue of David, and of Jesus, son of Mary' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:78](ibnkathir://5/78), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:78](tabari://5/78)). While Jesus pronounced prophetic woes against hypocrisy, He explicitly commanded His followers to bless rather than curse ([Luke 6:28](bible://lk/6/28)) and interceded from the cross for the forgiveness of those executing Him ([Luke 23:34](bible://lk/23/34)).

5:80.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Condemns to divine wrath and abiding torment those who take disbelievers as allies or close friends (*awliyāʾ*, [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:80](tabari://5/80), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:80](ibnkathir://5/80)), reinforcing the confessional segregation of [Quran 5:51](quran://5/51) by treating social and political solidarity outside the Muslim community as culpable rebellion.

5:81.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Declares that genuine faith in God, the Prophet, and the Quran renders taking non-believers as friends or allies (*awliyāʾ*) impossible, branding the majority who maintain such bonds as ungodly rebels (*fāsiqūn*, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:81](ibnkathir://5/81), [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:81](tabari://5/81)).

5:82.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Categorizes the Jews alongside polytheists as 'the most violent of people in enmity to those who believe' ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:82](tabari://5/82), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:82](ibnkathir://5/82)), codifying sweeping collective suspicion toward Jewish communities as timeless divine revelation.

5:87.Devalues Women: Although framed as a prohibition against forbidding lawful pleasures, canonical Hadiths in [Sahih al-Bukhari 5075](/hadith/bukhari/5075), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4615](/hadith/bukhari/4615), and [Sahih Muslim 1404a](/hadith/muslim/1404a) record that Muhammad authorized his campaigning soldiers to contract temporary sexual marriages (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) with women in exchange for a garment for a few nights and recited this verse to justify it. Sanctioning fixed-term paid sexual contracts reduces marriage from a lifelong covenant ([Matthew 19:5](bible://mt/19/5), [Matthew 19:6](bible://mt/19/6)) to temporary sexual transactions.

5:89.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: Institutionalizes chattel slavery within sacred jurisprudence by prescribing 'the freeing of a slave' (*taḥrīru raqabah*) alongside feeding or clothing ten poor people as a routine legal expiation for broken oaths ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:89](ibnkathir://5/89)), presupposing the ongoing ownership and availability of enslaved human beings rather than abolishing slavery.
5:89.Theological Defect: Establishes a transactional oath-expiation mechanism (*kaffārah*) under which deliberate oaths sworn in God's name can be dissolved whenever another course appears preferable—exemplified in [Sahih al-Bukhari 6721](/hadith/bukhari/6721), [Sahih al-Bukhari 6623](/hadith/bukhari/6623), and [Sahih Muslim 1649c](/hadith/muslim/1649c), where Muhammad routinely broke sworn oaths via expiation, contradicting the biblical sanctity of oaths and truthful speech ([Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2), [Matthew 5:33](bible://mt/5/33), [Matthew 5:37](bible://mt/5/37)).

5:90.Theological Defect: Declares wine (*al-khamr*) to be an impure abomination of Satan's handiwork (*rijsun min ʿamali al-shayṭān*, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:90](ibnkathir://5/90)), yet [Quran 47:15](quran://47/15) and [Quran 83:25](quran://83/25) promise believers rivers and sealed vessels of wine (*khamr* and *raḥīq*) in Paradise, turning a substance classified on earth as intrinsic Satanic filth into a heavenly reward.

5:97.Failed Prophecy: Declares that Allah established the Kaaba, the Sacred House, as an inviolable asylum of security (*qiyāman li-l-nās*) restraining violence and protecting the weak from the strong ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:97](tabari://5/97), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:97](ibnkathir://5/97); cf. [Quran 2:125](quran://2/125), [Quran 3:97](quran://3/97)). History repeatedly falsified this guarantee of security: Umayyad armies bombarded and burned the Kaaba in AD 683 and 692, the Qarmatians slaughtered pilgrims inside the sanctuary and carried off the Black Stone in AD 930, and armed insurgents seized the Grand Mosque in bloody combat in AD 1979.

5:110.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Attributes to Jesus two childhood miracles completely absent from the first-century canonical Gospels—speaking as an infant from the cradle and fashioning a clay bird before breathing life into it ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:110](ibnkathir://5/110)). Both episodes reproduce late second- to sixth-century Christian apocryphal legends, specifically the *Infancy Gospel of Thomas* (2:1–4) and the Syriac/Arabic infancy tradition (ch. 1), incorporating late folkloric hagiography as historical revelation.
5:110.Contradicts the Bible: Identifies 'the holy spirit' (*rūḥ al-qudus*) supporting Jesus as the created angel Gabriel ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:110](ibnkathir://5/110)) rather than the divine Third Person of the Trinity ([Acts 5:3](bible://acts/5/3), [Acts 5:4](bible://acts/5/4)), and portrays 'the Gospel' (*al-Injīl*) as a written book taught directly to Jesus alongside the Torah rather than the apostolic proclamation of His saving life, death, and resurrection ([Mark 1:1](bible://mk/1/1), [Luke 24:46](bible://lk/24/46), [Romans 1:16](bible://rom/1/16)).
5:110.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Uniquely attributes to Jesus—alone among all prophets in the Quran—the act of creating (*takhluqu*, from *khalaqa*) living form from clay and breathing life into it (echoing God's creative breath in [Genesis 2:7](bible://gn/2/7)), alongside healing the congenitally blind and lepers and raising the dead ([John 9:6](bible://jn/9/6), [John 11:43](bible://jn/11/43), [John 11:44](bible://jn/11/44)), conceding miraculous works that in biblical revelation manifest divine authority.

5:112.Contradicts the Bible: Depicts Jesus's disciples addressing Him by the matronymic 'Jesus, son of Mary'—a title never used by His apostles in the New Testament and employed disparagingly only by skeptics in [Mark 6:3](bible://mk/6/3)—and questioning in the standard Hafs reading whether His Lord is even able (*hal yastaṭīʿu rabbuka*) to send down a table from the sky ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:112](tabari://5/112)). Notably, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:112](ibnkathir://5/112) acknowledges that the story of this descending table (*al-māʾidah*) is absent from the Gospel known to Christians.

5:113.Contradicts the Bible: Portrays Jesus's apostles (*al-ḥawāriyyūn*) as demanding to eat from a sky-sent table so that their hearts may be reassured and so they may finally 'know that you have spoken the truth to us' ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:113](tabari://5/113), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:113](ibnkathir://5/113)), contradicting their prior New Testament confessions of settled faith in Jesus as the Messiah and Holy One of God ([Matthew 16:16](bible://mt/16/16), [John 6:68](bible://jn/6/68), [John 6:69](bible://jn/6/69)).

5:114.Contradicts the Bible: Places on Jesus's lips a supplication for a literal table of food (*māʾidah*) descending from the sky to institute a recurring festival (*ʿīd*) for the first and last of His followers ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:114](tabari://5/114), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:114](ibnkathir://5/114)), conflating elements of the Last Supper Eucharist ([Luke 22:19](bible://lk/22/19), [Luke 22:20](bible://lk/22/20)), wilderness manna ([Exodus 16:15](bible://ex/16/15)), and Peter's vision of a food-bearing sheet lowered from heaven ([Acts 10:11](bible://acts/10/11), [Acts 10:13](bible://acts/10/13)).

5:115.Contradicts the Bible: Concludes the unhistorical sky-table episode with Allah threatening any recipient who disbelieves afterward with a torment inflicted on no one else in the worlds—which [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:115](tabari://5/115) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:115](ibnkathir://5/115) connect to traditions that unbelievers among the table's recipients were transformed into apes and swine, an event wholly alien to first-century apostolic history ([Acts 1:13](bible://acts/1/13), [Acts 1:14](bible://acts/1/14)).

5:116.Contradicts the Bible: Depicts Allah interrogating Jesus over whether He instructed humanity, 'Take me and my mother as two gods (*ilāhayni*) instead of God' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:116](ibnkathir://5/116)), misidentifying the biblical Trinity of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit ([Matthew 28:19](bible://mt/28/19), [John 14:26](bible://jn/14/26)) as tritheistic worship of Allah, Jesus, and Mary.
5:116.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Commits a major historical-theological error by attributing to Christians ([Tafsir al-Tabari 5:116](tabari://5/116), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 5:116](ibnkathir://5/116)) the doctrine that Mary and Jesus are 'two gods instead of God'—a belief rejected by every historic Christian council and creed, reflecting at most distorted awareness of fringe fourth-century Arabian Mariolatry (*Collyridianism*) condemned by Epiphanius of Salamis (*Panarion* 79).

5:117.Contradicts the Bible: Attributes to Jesus a denial of divine worship and restricts His awareness of His followers strictly to His earthly sojourn ('when You took me [*tawaffaytanī*], You became the Watcher over them,' [Tafsir al-Tabari 5:117](tabari://5/117)), contradicting the risen Christ's reception of worship ([Matthew 28:17](bible://mt/28/17)) and continuous, omniscient presence with His Church 'always, to the end of the age' ([Matthew 28:20](bible://mt/28/20)), while using the death-verb *tawaffā* in tension with [Quran 4:157](quran://4/157).

6:20.Contradicts the Bible: Asserts that 'Those to whom We have given the Book' recognize Muhammad or his revelation 'as they recognize their own sons' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 6:20](ibnkathir://6/20), [Tafsir al-Tabari 6:20](tabari://6/20)). While conceding that seventh-century Jews and Christians held authentic scripture, this claim conflicts with pre-Islamic manuscripts of the Hebrew Bible and Greek New Testament, which contain no prophecy of Muhammad and warn against accepting any post-apostolic gospel ([Galatians 1:8](bible://gal/1/8)).

6:25.Theological Defect: Declares that Allah Himself placed coverings (*akinnah*) over unbelievers' hearts so they cannot understand the Quran and heaviness (*waqran*) in their ears so that even if they witness every sign they will not believe ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 6:25](ibnkathir://6/25), [Tafsir al-Tabari 6:25](tabari://6/25)). Yet the verse simultaneously condemns those same listeners for concluding that Muhammad's recitations are 'nothing but old tales' (*asāṭīru al-awwalīn*), punishing people for an inability to comprehend that God actively engineered.

6:34.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Proclaims categorically that 'No one can change the words of God' (*wa-lā mubaddila li-kalimāti Allāh*, [Tafsir al-Tabari 6:34](tabari://6/34), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 6:34](ibnkathir://6/34)). This theological axiom affirms the incorruptibility of divine scripture—undermining later polemical claims that humans corrupted God's prior words in the Torah and the Gospel ([Isaiah 40:8](bible://is/40/8), [Matthew 24:35](bible://mt/24/35))—while also standing in tension with Quranic abrogation in [Quran 2:106](quran://2/106) and [Quran 16:101](quran://16/101).

Shortly afterward, [Quran 9:84](quran://9/84) was revealed closing that loophole and adopting 'Umar's objection, exposing Muhammad's misreading of his own revelation (contrast Christ's call to boundless forgiveness in [Matthew 18:22](bible://mt/18/22)).

9:84.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Forbidding Muhammad and his community from ever offering funeral prayers over deceased disbelievers or hypocrites or even standing beside their graves ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 9:84](ibnkathir://9/84), [Tafsir al-Tabari 9:84](tabari://9/84)), [Quran 9:84](quran://9/84) severs basic funerary compassion across religious boundaries even in death (contrast [Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44), [Romans 12:15](bible://rom/12/15)).
9:84.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: As documented in [Sahih Muslim 2400a](/hadith/muslim/2400a) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 4671](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4671), when Muhammad stood to pray over 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab seized Muhammad's garment and protested until [Quran 9:84](quran://9/84) came down ratifying 'Umar's demand over Muhammad's earlier appeal to [Quran 9:80](quran://9/80). Like the three *Muwafaqat 'Umar* episodes in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4483](/hadith/bukhari/4483), revelation here tracks a senior companion's political intervention.

9:85.Theological Defect: Repeating the declaration of [Quran 9:55](quran://9/55), [Quran 9:85](quran://9/85) states that Allah grants disbelievers wealth and children solely intending 'to punish them by means of it in this world, and (that) they themselves should pass away while they are disbelievers' (*wa-tazhaqa anfusuhum wa-hum kafirun*). Both the Arabic subjunctive construction and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 9:85](ibnkathir://9/85) (cf. [Tafsir al-Tabari 9:85](tabari://9/85)) affirm that Allah actively wills for them to die in unbelief so their torment is worsened, contradicting the biblical revelation that God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked and extends saving grace to all people ([Ezekiel 33:11](bible://ez/33/11), [Titus 2:11](bible://ti/2/11)).

9:103.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Here Allah commands Muhammad to collect financial levies (*sadaqah*) from his followers' wealth to cleanse and purify them from sin, adding, 'and pray over them; surely your prayers are a rest (*sakan*, tranquility) for them' ([Tafsir al-Tabari 9:103](tabari://9/103)). As [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 9:103](ibnkathir://9/103) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 1497](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1497) record, tying purification payments directly to the spiritual reassurance of Muhammad's personal blessing so closely linked revenue collection to his person that several Arab tribes later held the obligation ended at his death—standing in sharp contrast to the free forgiveness of sins without monetary tribute in [Acts 8:20](bible://acts/8/20) and [Romans 3:24](bible://rom/3/24).

9:111.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Framing holy war as a binding commercial transaction (*ishtara*, 'purchased'), [Quran 9:111](quran://9/111) declares that Allah has bought believers' lives and wealth in exchange for Paradise specifically as 'they fight in the way of God, and they kill and are killed' (*fa-yaqtuluna wa-yuqtalun*). Both [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 9:111](ibnkathir://9/111) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 9:111](tabari://9/111) present this martial contract—cited by early Muslims as a sale incumbent upon every believer's neck—as a permanent divine incentive for lethal religious warfare (cf. [Quran 4:74](quran://4/74), [Quran 61:10](quran://61/10)–[Quran 61:11](quran://61/11)).
9:111.Contradicts the Bible: To validate its martial bargain, [Quran 9:111](quran://9/111) claims that Allah's guarantee of Paradise to believers who kill and are killed (*yaqtuluna wa-yuqtalun*) in holy war is 'a promise binding on Him in the Torah, and the Gospel, and the Qur'an' ([Tafsir al-Tabari 9:111](tabari://9/111), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 9:111](ibnkathir://9/111)). In reality, the Gospel never promises eternal salvation for killing in warfare; Jesus explicitly forbade sword-fighting by His disciples ([Matthew 26:52](bible://mt/26/52)), commanded love for enemies ([Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44)), and testified that His kingdom is not of this world, else His servants would fight ([John 18:36](bible://jn/18/36)).

9:113.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Explicitly prohibiting Muhammad and all believers from asking forgiveness for polytheists 'even though they may be family' (*uli qurba*), [Quran 9:113](quran://9/113) severs intercessory prayer for deceased non-Muslim loved ones ([Tafsir al-Tabari 9:113](tabari://9/113)). As recorded in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 9:113](ibnkathir://9/113) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 4772](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4772), this verse was revealed to stop Muhammad from praying for his own uncle and lifelong protector Abu Talib, enforcing a rigid confessional boundary that overrides natural familial devotion (contrast [Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44), [Luke 6:28](bible://lk/6/28)).

9:114.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Reinforcing the prohibition in [Quran 9:113](quran://9/113), [Quran 9:114](quran://9/114) portrays Abraham as formally disowning (*tabarra'a minhu*) his own father once he recognized him as 'an enemy to God' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 9:114](ibnkathir://9/114), [Tafsir al-Tabari 9:114](tabari://9/114); cf. [Quran 60:4](quran://60/4)). Elevating Abraham's repudiation of his parent as a normative model instructs believers to sever filial solidarity with non-Muslim family members, diverging sharply from biblical commands to honor parents and intercede even for adversaries ([Exodus 20:12](bible://ex/20/12), [Luke 23:34](bible://lk/23/34)).

9:123.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Addressing the Muslim community, [Quran 9:123](quran://9/123) commands, 'Fight those of the disbelievers who are close to you, and let them find sternness (*ghilzah*, harshness) in you.' Both [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 9:123](ibnkathir://9/123) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 9:123](tabari://9/123) codify this verse as a permanent strategic mandate for concentric military expansion—requiring Islamic rulers to subjugate neighboring non-Muslim territories first and successively advance outward, as applied against Byzantine Syria and Persia—directly opposing Christ's ethic of neighborly mercy and enemy love ([Luke 10:27](bible://lk/10/27), [Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44)).

9:128.Theological Defect: During Caliph Abu Bakr's post-Yamama compilation—initiated after 'Umar warned that much of the Quran risked permanent loss as reciters died in battle—chief compiler Zayd ibn Thabit testified that he located the final two verses of Surah at-Tawbah ([Quran 9:128](quran://9/128)–[Quran 9:129](quran://9/129)) solely with a single individual, Abu Khuza'ima al-Ansari, 'and with no one else' ([Sahih al-Bukhari 4679](/hadith/bukhari/4679), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4986](/hadith/bukhari/4986), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4989](/hadith/bukhari/4989), [Sahih al-Bukhari 7191](/hadith/bukhari/7191)). Even though commentators argue Zayd meant no other written copy existed, [Sahih al-Bukhari 4986](/hadith/bukhari/4986) specifies that Zayd was searching both written fragments and 'the chests of men,' contradicting claims of unbroken mass transmission (*tawatur*).

10:3.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Declaring that Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days (*fi sittati ayyamin*) before sitting upon the Throne ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:3](ibnkathir://10/3), [Tafsir al-Tabari 10:3](tabari://10/3)), [Quran 10:3](quran://10/3) conflicts arithmetically with the itemized creation schedule in [Quran 41:9](quran://41/9)–[Quran 41:12](quran://41/12). That passage totals eight days—two days to create the earth ([Quran 41:9](quran://41/9)), four days to set its mountains and measure its sustenance ([Quran 41:10](quran://41/10)), and two further days to form the seven heavens ([Quran 41:12](quran://41/12))—requiring commentators to argue retroactively that the four sustenance days overlapped the first two earth days despite the sequential particle *thumma* ('then').

10:18.Theological Defect: Here the Quran condemns polytheists for venerating objects beside Allah 'that neither harm them nor benefit them' (*ma la yadurruhum wa-la yanfa'uhum*; [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:18](ibnkathir://10/18), [Tafsir al-Tabari 10:18](tabari://10/18)). Yet in [Sahih al-Bukhari 1597](/hadith/bukhari/1597), Caliph 'Umar ibn al-Khattab kisses the Kaaba's Black Stone while applying this exact Quranic description to it—declaring that it is merely a stone that can neither benefit nor harm anyone—and states that he kisses it solely because he saw Muhammad doing so, preserving pre-Islamic stone veneration inside normative Hajj ritual (contrast [Exodus 20:4](bible://ex/20/4)).

10:37.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Asserting that this Quran could not have been forged apart from God, [Quran 10:37](quran://10/37) defines its mission as 'a confirmation (*tasdiq*) of what was before it, and a distinct setting forth of the Book' ([Tafsir al-Tabari 10:37](tabari://10/37), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:37](ibnkathir://10/37)). Confirming the authenticity of the prior Jewish and Christian Scriptures circulating in the 7th century AD without alleging textual corruption reinforces the Islamic Dilemma alongside [Quran 10:94](quran://10/94) and [Quran 5:47](quran://5/47), because those extant Scriptures contradict Quranic denials of Christ's divinity and crucifixion ([John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1), [Matthew 27:50](bible://mt/27/50)).

10:64.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Proclaiming that 'no one can change (*la tabdila*) the words of God'—a principle repeated in [Quran 6:115](quran://6/115) and [Quran 18:27](quran://18/27) ([Tafsir al-Tabari 10:64](tabari://10/64), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:64](ibnkathir://10/64))—[Quran 10:64](quran://10/64) affirms the unalterable permanence of divine revelation. Even though commentators seek to narrow this statement to Allah's promises to believers, the Quran itself designates the Torah and Gospel as God's revealed Book and Words ([Quran 3:3](quran://3/3), [Quran 5:43](quran://5/43)), undercutting later claims that human scribes corrupted the Biblical text ([Isaiah 40:8](bible://is/40/8), [Matthew 24:35](bible://mt/24/35)).

10:68.Contradicts the Bible: Dismissing divine Sonship as a baseless human invention—'They say, "God has taken a son." Glory to Him! He is the wealthy One... You have no authority for this'—[Quran 10:68](quran://10/68) and its classical exegesis ([Tafsir al-Tabari 10:68](tabari://10/68), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:68](ibnkathir://10/68)) treat divine Fatherhood as though it implied creaturely need or biological procreation. This repudiation directly contradicts the prior Scriptures confirmed in [Quran 10:37](quran://10/37), where the Father, prophets, and apostles reveal Jesus Christ as the eternal, uniquely begotten Son of God ([Psalms 2:7](bible://ps/2/7), [Matthew 3:17](bible://mt/3/17), [John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14), [John 3:16](bible://jn/3/16)).

10:90.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: As the sea closes over him, Pharaoh recites an Islamic-style monotheistic confession—'I believe that there is no god but the One in whom the Sons of Israel believe. I am one of those who submit' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:90](ibnkathir://10/90), [Tafsir al-Tabari 10:90](tabari://10/90)). Absent from canonical biblical history, Pharaoh's drowning conversion adapts post-biblical Jewish aggadic lore—attested in *Mekhilta de-Rabbi Ishmael* (Beshallah 5–6) and expanded in *Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer* 43—where Pharaoh confesses Israel's God amid the waters of the Red Sea.
10:90.Contradicts the Bible: Depicting Pharaoh as making an explicit monotheistic profession of faith and submission to Israel's God while drowning ([Tafsir al-Tabari 10:90](tabari://10/90), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:90](ibnkathir://10/90)) directly contradicts the historical Exodus narrative. In Scripture, Pharaoh pursues Israel in hardened defiance and perishes beneath the returning sea with his chariot host without any deathbed repentance ([Exodus 14:23](bible://ex/14/23), [Exodus 14:28](bible://ex/14/28), [Psalms 136:15](bible://ps/136/15)).

10:91.Theological Defect: Explaining Allah's rejection of Pharaoh's drowning confession ('Now? When you had disobeyed before'), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:91](ibnkathir://10/91) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 10:91](tabari://10/91) cite Muhammad's report (recorded by Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, graded *hasan*) that the angel Gabriel crammed black sea-mud into Pharaoh's mouth 'out of fear that divine mercy would reach him.' Having just answered Moses's prayer in [Quran 10:88](quran://10/88)–[Quran 10:89](quran://10/89) that Pharaoh not believe until seeing the torment, the tradition portrays an archangel physically gagging a dying penitent lest God forgive him (contrast Christ receiving the dying thief's repentance in [Luke 23:42](bible://lk/23/42)–[Luke 23:43](bible://lk/23/43)).

10:92.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Declaring, 'Today We rescue you with your body (*bi-badanika*), so that you may be a sign for those who succeed you,' [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:92](ibnkathir://10/92) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 10:92](tabari://10/92) explain that Allah cast Pharaoh's intact corpse in its recognizable armor onto high ground because some Israelites doubted his death. This detail reproduces the rabbinic midrash of *Mekhilta de-Rabbi Ishmael* (Beshallah 6; cf. Babylonian Talmud *Pesahim* 118b), which narrated that the sea cast up Pharaoh's corpse specifically to reassure skeptical Israelites.
10:92.Contradicts the Bible: Claiming that Allah uniquely delivered Pharaoh's intact corpse (*bi-badanika*) ashore as an enduring sign for succeeding generations ([Tafsir al-Tabari 10:92](tabari://10/92), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:92](ibnkathir://10/92)) diverges from [Exodus 14:28](bible://ex/14/28), [Exodus 14:30](bible://ex/14/30), and [Psalms 136:15](bible://ps/136/15), where drowned Egyptian soldiers wash ashore collectively without Pharaoh's body being singled out for preservation. Modern attempts to equate this sea-cast corpse with artificially eviscerated, embalmed New Kingdom royal mummies from inland Theban tombs contradict both Egyptian mummification practice and classical commentary.

10:94.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Commanding Muhammad directly, 'If you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, ask those who have been reciting the Book before you,' [Quran 10:94](quran://10/94) treats the Scriptures held by 7th-century AD Jews and Christians as the authoritative benchmark of divine truth ([Tafsir al-Tabari 10:94](tabari://10/94), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:94](ibnkathir://10/94)). Directing Islam's prophet to consult readers of the Torah and Gospel presupposes their intact textual preservation—confirmed by 4th- and 5th-century AD biblical codices—creating an acute dilemma when those same Scriptures proclaim Christ's divine Sonship ([Matthew 3:17](bible://mt/3/17)) and saving crucifixion ([Luke 24:46](bible://lk/24/46)).

10:99.Theological Defect: Asserting that had Allah pleased, everyone on earth would have believed together, [Tafsir al-Tabari 10:99](tabari://10/99) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:99](ibnkathir://10/99) explain through predestinarian decree that Allah withheld universal faith because He pre-inscribed before creation who would remain in unbelief and enter Hellfire (citing [Quran 11:118](quran://11/118)–[Quran 11:119](quran://11/119)). Meanwhile, its Meccan rhetorical question against coercing belief ('Will you compel the people until they become believers?') was later superseded by Medinan mandates for armed subjugation in [Quran 9:5](quran://9/5) and [Quran 9:29](quran://9/29) (contrast [Titus 2:11](bible://ti/2/11)).

10:100.Theological Defect: Declaring that 'it is not for any person to believe, except by the permission of God, and He places abomination (*al-rijs*) on those who do not understand,' [Tafsir al-Tabari 10:100](tabari://10/100) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 10:100](ibnkathir://10/100) gloss *al-rijs* as divine wrath, ruin, and misguidance. Because no human soul can believe unless Allah decrees permission while He actively casts spiritual defilement upon others, human unbelief becomes divinely determined rather than a free refusal of universal saving grace ([John 3:16](bible://jn/3/16), [Romans 10:13](bible://rom/10/13)).

11:7.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Combining a six-day creation formula with Near Eastern primordial-ocean cosmology, [Quran 11:7](quran://11/7) states that before the heavens and earth existed 'His throne was upon the water'—which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:7](ibnkathir://11/7) explains literally as Allah's physical Throne resting above primeval water later divided beneath the Throne. Moreover, [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:7](tabari://11/7) explicates this verse by citing Muhammad's seven-day creation schedule in [Sahih Muslim 2789](/hadith/muslim/2789), where soil on Saturday, mountains on Sunday, and trees on Monday are created days before light on Wednesday and Adam on Friday—conflicting with astrophysics, the six-day total here, and the eight-day sum in [Quran 41:9](quran://41/9)–[Quran 41:12](quran://41/12).

11:17.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Commending 'the Book of Moses as a model (*imaman*) and mercy' prior to the Quran ([Tafsir al-Tabari 11:17](tabari://11/17), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:17](ibnkathir://11/17); cf. [Quran 46:12](quran://46/12)), [Quran 11:17](quran://11/17) endorses the Torah as a reliable standard and divine blessing without suggesting textual loss or alteration. Affirming the Mosaic Scriptures in the 7th century AD validates a biblical corpus whose patriarchal covenants and messianic prophecies contradict Quranic theology ([Genesis 17:19](bible://gn/17/19), [Luke 24:27](bible://lk/24/27)).

11:40.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Describing the onset of Noah's Flood with the clause 'when Our command came and the oven (*al-tannur*) boiled' (repeated in [Quran 23:27](quran://23/27)), [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:40](tabari://11/40) records early authorities including Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan al-Basri identifying *al-tannur* as a literal bread-baking stone oven—allegedly passed down from Eve to Noah—from which boiling water erupted ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:40](ibnkathir://11/40)). Entirely absent from [Genesis 7:11](bible://gn/7/11), the motif of scalding, boiling Floodwaters derives from post-biblical rabbinic aggadah in Babylonian Talmud *Sanhedrin* 108b, *Zevachim* 113b, and *Genesis Rabbah* 28:9.

11:42.Contradicts the Bible: Introducing an unattested fourth son of Noah—named 'Yam' or 'Kan'an' in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:42](ibnkathir://11/42) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:42](tabari://11/42)—who stands isolated refusing Noah's plea to board the Ark, [Quran 11:42](quran://11/42) directly contradicts the biblical Flood record (and stands in internal tension with [Quran 21:76](quran://21/76) and [Quran 37:76](quran://37/76), which state unqualifiedly that Allah rescued Noah and his family). Scripture consistently testifies that Noah had three sons—Shem, Ham, and Japheth—and that all three entered the Ark with Noah as his saved household ([Genesis 6:10](bible://gn/6/10), [Genesis 7:13](bible://gn/7/13), [Hebrews 11:7](bible://heb/11/7)).

11:43.Contradicts the Bible: Narrating that Noah's son sought refuge on a mountain until waves came between them and 'he was among the drowned' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:43](ibnkathir://11/43), [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:43](tabari://11/43)), [Quran 11:43](quran://11/43) contradicts the historical record of Genesis. None of Noah's sons perished in the deluge; Shem, Ham, and Japheth all boarded the Ark on the day the Flood began, disembarked safely afterward, and repopulated the earth ([Genesis 7:13](bible://gn/7/13), [Genesis 8:18](bible://gn/8/18), [Genesis 9:18](bible://gn/9/18)).

11:44.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Placing the Ark's landing specifically on Mount *al-Judi*—identified in upper Mesopotamia near Mosul by [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:44](tabari://11/44) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:44](ibnkathir://11/44)—diverges from the Hebrew text of [Genesis 8:4](bible://gn/8/4) ('the mountains of Ararat'). In Late Antiquity, Aramaic and Syriac translations (*Targum Onkelos* and the Syriac *Peshitta* on [Genesis 8:4](bible://gn/8/4)) localized 'Ararat' as Mount *Qardu* (Corduene / Judi), showing the Quran's reliance on regional post-biblical Syrian geography.

11:45.Contradicts the Bible: Portraying Noah after the Flood petitioning Allah because his drowned son belonged to the family Allah had promised to save ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:45](ibnkathir://11/45), [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:45](tabari://11/45)), [Quran 11:45](quran://11/45) diverges sharply from [Genesis 8:18](bible://gn/8/18)–[Genesis 8:20](bible://gn/8/20) and [Genesis 9:1](bible://gn/9/1), where Noah disembarks with his wife, all three sons, and their wives intact to offer thanksgiving sacrifices and receive God's covenant blessing ([Hebrews 11:7](bible://heb/11/7)).

11:46.Contradicts the Bible: Here Allah rebukes Noah by revoking his drowned son's kinship—'Noah! Surely he is not one of your family; surely it is an unrighteous deed'—and admonishing Noah 'not to be one of the ignorant' ([Tafsir al-Tabari 11:46](tabari://11/46), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:46](ibnkathir://11/46)). Besides contradicting the survival of Noah's entire household in [Genesis 7:13](bible://gn/7/13) and [Genesis 9:18](bible://gn/9/18), this ambiguous phrasing led early Muslim exegetes recorded in [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:46](tabari://11/46) (including al-Hasan al-Basri and Mujahid, citing [Quran 66:10](quran://66/10)) to claim that Noah's wife committed adultery and bore an illegitimate child.
11:46.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Declaring that Noah's biological son 'is not one of your family' strictly on account of religious unbelief ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:46](ibnkathir://11/46), [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:46](tabari://11/46)) subordinates natural parent-child kinship to confessional conformity and rebukes even a father's grief for his lost child, paralleling [Quran 9:113](quran://9/113)–[Quran 9:114](quran://9/114) and contrasting with biblical compassion for estranged or unbelieving kin ([Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44), [Romans 9:3](bible://rom/9/3)).

11:69.Contradicts the Bible: Recounting Abraham's hospitality at Mamre solely as a visit from created angelic messengers (*rusuluna*, identified as Gabriel and fellow angels in [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:69](tabari://11/69) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:69](ibnkathir://11/69)), [Quran 11:69](quran://11/69) removes the central biblical theophany of [Genesis 18:1](bible://gn/18/1), [Genesis 18:13](bible://gn/18/13), and [Genesis 18:22](bible://gn/18/22), where YHWH Himself appears personally to Abraham accompanied by two angels who subsequently proceed to Sodom ([Genesis 19:1](bible://gn/19/1)).

11:70.Contradicts the Bible: Claiming that Abraham's visitors did not reach out their hands to his roasted calf—causing Abraham to distrust and fear them until they announced their mission to Lot ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:70](ibnkathir://11/70), [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:70](tabari://11/70))—directly contradicts [Genesis 18:8](bible://gn/18/8), which states explicitly that Abraham stood beside them under the trees while 'they ate' without fear, and reverses [Genesis 18:10](bible://gn/18/10)–[Genesis 18:20](bible://gn/18/20), where Isaac is promised before Sodom's judgment is disclosed.
11:70.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: The non-biblical detail that Abraham's angelic guests refused to eat the roasted calf of [Quran 11:69](quran://11/69) because angels do not consume earthly food ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:70](ibnkathir://11/70), [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:70](tabari://11/70)) derives from post-biblical Jewish midrash and pseudepigrapha—including Babylonian Talmud *Bava Metzia* 86b, *Genesis Rabbah* 48:14, *Targum Pseudo-Jonathan* on [Genesis 18:8](bible://gn/18/8), and *Testament of Abraham* 4—which reworked Genesis to claim the angels only appeared to eat.

11:71.Contradicts the Bible: Here Sarah stands present, laughs *before* receiving any birth announcement, and is then promised both 'Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob' prior to Isaac's conception ([Tafsir al-Tabari 11:71](tabari://11/71)). Beyond reversing [Genesis 18:10](bible://gn/18/10)–[Genesis 18:12](bible://gn/18/12) (where Sarah laughs inwardly inside the tent *after* overhearing YHWH's promise of a son), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:71](ibnkathir://11/71) admits that foretelling Isaac would live to father Jacob precludes young Isaac from being the sacrificial son—nullifying any genuine test in [Genesis 22:2](bible://gn/22/2) and [Hebrews 11:17](bible://heb/11/17) so commentators can reassign the sacrifice to Ishmael.

11:105.Theological Defect: Dividing humanity on Judgment Day into 'miserable (*shaqiyy*) and happy (*sa'id*),' [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:105](ibnkathir://11/105) records 'Umar ibn al-Khattab asking Muhammad upon this verse's revelation whether humans labor for a matter already decided or still open, to which Muhammad replied, 'For something that has already been concluded, O 'Umar, and the pens have run with it' ([Tafsir al-Tabari 11:105](tabari://11/105)). This matches [Sahih Muslim 2644](/hadith/muslim/2644) and [Sahih Muslim 2647a](/hadith/muslim/2647a), where every person's status as *shaqiyy* (damned) or *sa'id* (blessed) is pre-inscribed before birth (contrast [Deuteronomy 30:19](bible://dt/30/19), [Titus 2:11](bible://ti/2/11)).

11:118.Theological Defect: Stating that 'if your Lord had pleased, He would indeed have made the people one community, but they will continue to differ,' [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:118](ibnkathir://11/118) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:118](tabari://11/118) affirm that Allah possessed full power to unite humanity upon right guidance yet deliberately willed ongoing religious division save for those granted selective mercy in [Quran 11:119](quran://11/119). Making spiritual discord a product of divine pleasure contrasts directly with God's universal salvific desire and Christ's prayer for unity in truth ([Titus 2:11](bible://ti/2/11), [John 17:21](bible://jn/17/21)).

11:119.Theological Defect: Completing [Quran 11:118](quran://11/118), [Quran 11:119](quran://11/119) adds 'and for that (purpose) He created them. But the word of your Lord is fulfilled: "I shall indeed fill Gehenna with jinn and people—all (of them)!"' Concluding his exegesis, [Tafsir al-Tabari 11:119](tabari://11/119) (alongside al-Hasan al-Basri in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 11:119](ibnkathir://11/119); cf. [Sahih al-Bukhari 4947](/hadith/bukhari/4947)) rules that Allah created one group specifically for Paradise and the other for Hellfire to fulfill His oath to fill Gehenna—directly opposing Scripture's teaching that eternal fire was prepared for the devil and his angels rather than humanity ([Matthew 25:41](bible://mt/25/41), [Ezekiel 33:11](bible://ez/33/11)).

12:19.Contradicts the Bible: Having a passing caravan's water-drawer discover Joseph by lowering a bucket into a well and conceal him as commercial merchandise, as detailed in [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:19](tabari://12/19) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:19](ibnkathir://12/19), contradicts the older Hebrew account on two points. [Genesis 37:24](bible://gn/37/24) explicitly states that the cistern was empty and held no water, and [Genesis 37:27](bible://gn/37/27) through [Genesis 37:28](bible://gn/37/28) records that Judah and Joseph's brothers directly negotiated his sale to the passing caravan rather than strangers secretly finding him.

12:20.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Reporting that Joseph was sold for "counted dirhams" (`darahima ma'dudatin`)—explained by early authorities in [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:20](tabari://12/20) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:20](ibnkathir://12/20) as twenty to forty silver coins counted out by unit rather than weighed—projects minted coinage onto patriarchal antiquity. Stamped coinage was not invented until the seventh to sixth centuries BC in Lydia and Persia, and the Arabic term *dirham* derives from the Greek *drachma*, whereas [Genesis 37:28](bible://gn/37/28) historically specifies twenty weighed shekels of uncoined silver.

12:24.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Asserting that Joseph inclined toward Potiphar's wife until he beheld "the proof of his Lord" (`burhana rabbihi`) compresses a rabbinic legend that classical exegetes in [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:24](tabari://12/24) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:24](ibnkathir://12/24) supply verbatim: Jacob's apparition appeared before Joseph biting his fingers to restrain him. That extra-biblical episode comes directly from late antique Jewish exegesis preserved in Babylonian Talmud *Sotah* 36b and *Genesis Rabbah* 87:7, contrasting with Joseph's resolute verbal refusal in [Genesis 39:8](bible://gn/39/8) and [Genesis 39:9](bible://gn/39/9).

12:26.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Introducing a household witness (`shahidun min ahliha`) to adjudicate the accusation against Joseph—identified by Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and al-Dahhak and endorsed by al-Tabari in [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:26](tabari://12/26) as a miraculously speaking infant in the cradle, as also noted in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:27](ibnkathir://12/27)—incorporates late antique midrashic and Syriac narrative embellishments. No household arbitrator or speaking infant exists in [Genesis 39:19](bible://gn/39/19), where Potiphar immediately believes his wife's report.

12:27.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Establishing Joseph's innocence through a forensic inspection of whether his shirt was torn from behind (`qudda min duburin`) reflects extra-biblical Jewish aggadic and Syriac Christian retellings of the Joseph cycle ([Tafsir al-Tabari 12:27](tabari://12/27); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:27](ibnkathir://12/27)), later preserved in *Sefer ha-Yashar*. By contrast, [Genesis 39:12](bible://gn/39/12) states that Joseph slipped out of his outer garment and left the entire cloak behind in Potiphar's wife's hand as he fled outdoors.

12:28.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Depicting Potiphar inspecting the back-torn shirt and immediately declaring his wife guilty and Joseph innocent ([Tafsir al-Tabari 12:28](tabari://12/28); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:28](ibnkathir://12/28)) adapts post-biblical homiletic tradition in a way that leaves a visible narrative seam. Because Joseph is already fully vindicated here, his subsequent imprisonment by the same household in [Quran 12:35](quran://12/35) lacks the coherent legal cause preserved in [Genesis 39:19](bible://gn/39/19) and [Genesis 39:20](bible://gn/39/20), where Potiphar jails Joseph because he believed the accusation.

12:31.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Narrating that Potiphar's wife hosted a banquet for Egyptian noblewomen, handed each guest a knife (`sikkinan`), and paraded Joseph before them until they cut their own hands in astonishment ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:31](ibnkathir://12/31); [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:31](tabari://12/31)) reproduces a well-known Jewish midrashic tale. This citron-and-knife banquet episode is entirely absent from [Genesis 39:14](bible://gn/39/14) and originates in rabbinic folklore preserved in *Midrash Tanhuma* Vayeshev 5 and *Sefer ha-Yashar*.

12:41.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Having Joseph tell Pharaoh's imprisoned baker that his master "will crucify him" (`fa-yuslabu`) so birds eat from his head ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:41](ibnkathir://12/41); [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:41](tabari://12/41)) projects Roman- and Persian-era crucifixion back into second-millennium BC Egypt. Crucifixion is unattested in Middle Bronze Age pharaonic punishment and first emerged over a millennium later in sixth-century BC Persia and Carthage, whereas [Genesis 40:19](bible://gn/40/19) accurately describes pharaonic decapitation followed by suspending the corpse on a wooden pole.

12:67.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Recording Jacob's instruction that his eleven sons must not enter Egypt through a single city gate—explained by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:67](ibnkathir://12/67) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:67](tabari://12/67) as a precaution against the evil eye—adapts a specifically rabbinic motif. This instruction does not appear in [Genesis 42:1](bible://gn/42/1) through [Genesis 42:5](bible://gn/42/5), but matches Jacob's verbatim warning in *Genesis Rabbah* 91:2 and 91:6 not to enter through one gate out of fear of the evil eye.

12:99.Contradicts the Bible: Describing Joseph welcoming and embracing both of his parents (`abawayhi`) alive when his family enters Egypt—explicitly identified as his father Jacob and biological mother Rachel by Ibn Ishaq and endorsed by al-Tabari in [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:99](tabari://12/99)—directly contradicts the Genesis historical record. According to [Genesis 35:19](bible://gn/35/19), Rachel had died in Canaan while giving birth to Benjamin and was buried on the road to Ephrath years before Joseph was ever taken to Egypt.

12:100.Contradicts the Bible: Stating that Joseph raised both of his parents (`abawayhi`) onto the throne in Egypt while they and his eleven brothers bowed down to fulfill [Quran 12:4](quran://12/4) ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:100](ibnkathir://12/100); [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:100](tabari://12/100)) contradicts [Genesis 35:19](bible://gn/35/19) and [Genesis 48:7](bible://gn/48/7), which record Rachel's death and burial in Canaan long before the migration to Egypt. In [Genesis 37:10](bible://gn/37/10), Jacob himself had questioned how the "moon" in Joseph's dream could bow to him on earth given Rachel's prior death.
12:100.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Presenting Joseph's biological mother as traveling alive to Egypt and ascending his court seat alongside Jacob (`abawayhi`, confirmed as Jacob and Rachel by al-Tabari in [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:99](tabari://12/99) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:100](tabari://12/100)) converts the symbolic sun-and-moon imagery of [Genesis 37:9](bible://gn/37/9) into a literal Egyptian enthronement scene. This overlooks the patriarchal chronology of [Genesis 35:19](bible://gn/35/19) and [Genesis 48:7](bible://gn/48/7), in which Rachel died giving birth to Benjamin in Canaan prior to Joseph's enslavement.

12:102.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Presenting the preceding Joseph narrative as previously unknown "news of the unseen" (`anba'i al-ghaybi`) revealed supernaturally to prove prophethood ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:102](ibnkathir://12/102); [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:102](tabari://12/102)) conflicts with its documented literary pedigree. Not only had the core biography circulated for over a millennium in [Genesis 37:2](bible://gn/37/2), but its distinctive extra-biblical episodes in [Quran 12:24](quran://12/24), [Quran 12:26](quran://12/26), [Quran 12:31](quran://12/31), and [Quran 12:67](quran://12/67) reflect late antique Jewish midrashim and Syriac homilies current in Near Eastern oral culture.

12:111.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Declaring the Quran "a confirmation of what was before it" (`tasdiqa alladhi bayna yadayhi`)—identified in [Tafsir al-Tabari 12:111](tabari://12/111) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 12:111](ibnkathir://12/111) as the previously revealed Biblical books—affirms the authority of the Torah and Gospel circulating in the seventh century AD. This concession creates an internal dilemma because those confirmed scriptures contradict [Quran 12:100](quran://12/100) regarding Rachel's prior death in [Genesis 35:19](bible://gn/35/19) and teach Christ's divine sonship and crucifixion in [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1) and [Matthew 27:35](bible://mt/27/35).

13:2.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Describing the heavens as an elevated roof raised "without pillars that you can see"—interpreted by early authorities in [Tafsir al-Tabari 13:2](tabari://13/2) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 13:2](ibnkathir://13/2) either as a solid architectural dome or as resting on invisible pillars across seven concentric layers—reflects ancient Near Eastern firmament cosmology. The verse simultaneously pairs the sun and the moon as analogous celestial bodies running orbital courses to an appointed term, presupposing a geocentric model in which both luminaries revolve around Earth.

13:3.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Portraying the earth as stretched out flat (`madda al-arda`) while asserting universally that "of every fruit He made in it two pairs" (`min kulli al-thamarati ja'ala fiha zawjayni ithnayn`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 13:3](ibnkathir://13/3); [Tafsir al-Tabari 13:3](tabari://13/3)) conflicts with both geodesy and plant biology. Numerous fruiting plants reproduce without distinct male and female pairs through parthenocarpy, asexual vegetative propagation, or self-pollinating hermaphroditic flowers, including seedless bananas and cultivated figs.

13:7.Theological Defect: Recording Meccan skeptics asking why no miraculous sign was sent down to Muhammad and answering solely that "You are only a warner"—matching [Quran 17:59](quran://17/59) and [Quran 29:50](quran://29/50) ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 13:7](ibnkathir://13/7); [Tafsir al-Tabari 13:7](tabari://13/7))—concedes the absence of public nature miracles during his Meccan ministry. This Quranic disclaimer directly conflicts with later canonical Hadith tradition such as [Sahih al-Bukhari 3868](/hadith/bukhari/3868), which claims Muhammad split the moon into two visible halves when the Meccans demanded a sign.

13:27.Theological Defect: Responding to disbelievers' request for a prophetic sign by declaring that "surely God leads astray whomever He pleases" (`inna Allaha yudillu man yasha'u`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 13:27](ibnkathir://13/27); [Tafsir al-Tabari 13:27](tabari://13/27)) makes God the direct causal author of human spiritual error. Making divine will the origin of unbelief while condemning the misguided eternally contrasts with [Ezekiel 18:32](bible://ez/18/32) and [John 12:32](bible://jn/12/32), which affirm God's call to universal repentance and Christ drawing all humanity toward salvation.

13:31.Theological Defect: Asserting that "if God pleased, He would indeed guide all the people" while promising relentless afflictions descending near disbelievers' homes—explained in [Tafsir al-Tabari 13:31](tabari://13/31) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 13:31](ibnkathir://13/31) both as sovereign withholding of guidance and as Muhammad's armed expeditions subduing Mecca by the sword—combines theological fatalism with coercive force. Humans are thus threatened with earthly conquest and eternal ruin for lacking guidance that Allah explicitly chose not to grant.

13:33.Theological Defect: Stating that disbelievers had their scheming made attractive to them and were barred from the right path because "whomever God leads astray, for him there is no guide" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 13:33](ibnkathir://13/33); [Tafsir al-Tabari 13:33](tabari://13/33)) portrays spiritual blindness as an inescapable condition imposed by divine decree. Holding human beings morally culpable after God actively leads them astray undermines coherent divine justice.

13:39.Theological Defect: Declaring that "God blots out whatever He pleases, and He confirms, and with Him is the mother of the Book" is explained by early exegetes in [Tafsir al-Tabari 13:39](tabari://13/39) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 13:39](ibnkathir://13/39) both as Allah erasing and replacing revealed rulings and as leaving predestined salvation or damnation unalterably fixed. Making revealed divine law subject to erasure while locking eternal misery in advance conflicts with God's unchanging character and truth in [Numbers 23:19](bible://nm/23/19) and [James 1:17](bible://jas/1/17).

13:43.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Invoking "whoever has knowledge of the Book" (`'ilmu al-kitabi`) alongside God as a sufficient witness to prophethood appeals directly to Jewish and Christian scholars possessing the Torah and Gospel, as Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah confirm for this Meccan passage in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 13:43](ibnkathir://13/43) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 13:43](tabari://13/43). Citing seventh-century AD Jewish and Christian scripture holders as authoritative witnesses concedes that their extant Biblical texts remained intact and trustworthy.

14:4.Theological Defect: Asserting that after a messenger speaks in his people's tongue, "God leads astray whomever He pleases and guides whomever He pleases" (`fa-yudillu Allahu man yasha'u`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 14:4](ibnkathir://14/4); [Tafsir al-Tabari 14:4](tabari://14/4)) makes divine volition the decisive cause of human rejection right after revelation is delivered. This deterministic model contrasts sharply with [Matthew 18:14](bible://mt/18/14) and [John 3:17](bible://jn/3/17), which teach that the Father does not will for the lost to perish, but sent His Son so that the world might be saved.

14:27.Theological Defect: Declaring that "God leads astray the evildoers, and God does whatever He pleases" (`wa-yudillu Allahu al-zalimina`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 14:27](ibnkathir://14/27); [Tafsir al-Tabari 14:27](tabari://14/27)) portrays Allah actively causing people to falter both in earthly life and, according to canonical exegesis, during the interrogation of the grave. Grounding human misguidance in sheer sovereign arbitrariness ("God does whatever He pleases") removes any consistent moral standard of redemptive grace.

14:37.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Portraying Abraham settling his descendants in an uncultivated valley beside the "Sacred House"—unanimously identified in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 14:37](ibnkathir://14/37) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 14:37](tabari://14/37) as Mecca and the Kaaba—lacks historical or archaeological attestation. No pre-Christian inscription, classical geographic survey, or archaeological stratum documents either the existence of Mecca in the second millennium BC or any patriarchal journey into the central Hijaz.
14:37.Contradicts the Bible: Having Abraham relocate Hagar and Ishmael's lineage to Mecca's barren valley beside the Kaaba ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 14:37](ibnkathir://14/37); [Tafsir al-Tabari 14:37](tabari://14/37)) directly contradicts the Biblical geography of Ishmael's life. [Genesis 21:14](bible://gn/21/14) and [Genesis 21:21](bible://gn/21/21) record that Hagar departed into the Wilderness of Beersheba and that Ishmael grew up and married an Egyptian woman in the Wilderness of Paran adjacent to Sinai and southern Canaan, more than 1,000 kilometers north of Mecca.

15:9.Theological Defect: Promising unfailing divine protection for "the Reminder" (`al-dhikr`) is undermined by canonical Sunni Hadith collections documenting revealed Quranic passages omitted from the Uthmanic codex ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:9](ibnkathir://15/9)). Authoritative reports in [Sahih Muslim 1452b](/hadith/muslim/1452b), [Sahih Muslim 1452a](/hadith/muslim/1452a), [Sahih Muslim 1050](/hadith/muslim/1050), and [Sahih Muslim 1691a](/hadith/muslim/1691a) record Companions testifying that recited verses on adult breastfeeding, stoning, and entire surah sections were lost or forgotten.
15:9.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Pledging that God Himself guards "the Reminder" (`al-dhikr`, [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:9](tabari://15/9)) employs the same title applied to earlier Biblical scriptures whose Jewish and Christian custodians are designated "People of the Reminder" (`ahl al-dhikr`) in [Quran 16:43](quran://16/43) and [Quran 21:7](quran://21/7) ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:43](ibnkathir://16/43)). Because God promises to preserve His Reminder, later claims that human scribes corrupted the Torah and Gospel contradict the Quran's own theology of scriptural preservation.

15:12.Theological Defect: Stating with respect to mockery of messengers, "In this way We put it into the hearts of the sinners" (`kadhalika naslukuhu fi qulubi al-mujrimina`), is explained by Anas ibn Malik, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Qatadah in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:12](ibnkathir://15/12) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:12](tabari://15/12) as Allah directly instilling polytheism and denial into human hearts. Depicting God as implanting unbelief inside sinners before condemning them for not believing makes divine judgment self-contradictory.

15:16.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Asserting that God placed constellations or celestial towers (`burujan`) inside the sky dome and adorned it for onlookers—linked directly to the demon-guarded firmament of [Quran 15:17](quran://15/17) ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:16](ibnkathir://15/16); [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:16](tabari://15/16))—treats optical star patterns as physical structures built into a single overhead ceiling. In reality, constellation stars are unrelated suns dispersed across hundreds or thousands of light-years in three-dimensional space.

15:17.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Portraying the physical sky as a fortified boundary guarded against every ascending devil—elaborated in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4701](/hadith/bukhari/4701), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4800](/hadith/bukhari/4800), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:17](ibnkathir://15/17), and [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:17](tabari://15/17) as stacked jinn climbing up toward the lowest heaven—presupposes an enclosed solid firmament separating Earth's air from an upper celestial court.
15:17.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Depicting demons ascending to the physical boundary of the sky until repelled from its gates ([Tafsir al-Tabari 15:17](tabari://15/17); [Sahih al-Bukhari 4800](/hadith/bukhari/4800)) adapts late antique Near Eastern demonological lore. In pseudepigraphal texts such as *Testament of Solomon* 20:12–17, demons likewise fly up toward the firmament among the stars to overhear heavenly decrees before being driven down.

15:18.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Explaining meteors (`shihabun mubin`) as fiery missiles launched to chase away devils who steal a hearing from the heavenly assembly—explicitly identified with visible shooting stars in [Sahih Muslim 2229a](/hadith/muslim/2229a), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:18](ibnkathir://15/18), and [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:18](tabari://15/18)—confuses astronomical phenomena with supernatural artillery. Shooting stars are small interplanetary meteoroids orbiting the sun that incandescently vaporize through friction upon entering Earth's upper atmosphere.
15:18.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Linking shooting stars (`shihabun mubin`) to eavesdropping spirits struck down by celestial fire ([Sahih Muslim 2229a](/hadith/muslim/2229a); [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:18](tabari://15/18)) echoes pre-Islamic Arabian soothsayer lore and late antique pseudepigrapha. Specifically, *Testament of Solomon* 20:15–17 explains falling stars looking like lightning bolts as exhausted or repelled demons plummeting from the starry firmament after attempting to overhear divine plans.

15:19.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Stating that God spread out the earth (`madadnaha`) and cast firm mountains (`alqa fiha rawasiya`) onto its surface ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:19](ibnkathir://15/19); [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:19](tabari://15/19)) reflects a flat-earth cosmological model stabilized from above by heavy mountain pegs. Geologically, Earth is an oblate spheroid and mountain ranges are thrust upward from within the crust by plate tectonics rather than dropped onto a spread-out plane.

15:28.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Opening a heavenly scene in which God announces to the angels that He is creating a mortal from dried clay as preparation for commanding angelic prostration in [Quran 15:29](quran://15/29) ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:28](ibnkathir://15/28); [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:28](tabari://15/28)) draws from late antique apocryphal Adam literature. This angelic court announcement is absent from [Genesis 2:7](bible://gn/2/7) and closely parallels the Syriac Christian *Cave of Treasures* 2:12–14.

15:29.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Commanding the angels to fall prostrate (`sajidina`) before newly enlivened Adam ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:29](ibnkathir://15/29); [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:29](tabari://15/29)) reproduces the extra-biblical veneration narrative of *Life of Adam and Eve* 13–14 and Syriac *Cave of Treasures* 2:13–19. Canonical Scripture never commands angels to bow before Adam ([Genesis 2:7](bible://gn/2/7)), instead reserving the divine command 'Let all God's angels worship Him' exclusively for the eternal divine Son in [Hebrews 1:6](bible://heb/1/6)—a Christological motif that late antique apocrypha transferred onto Adam.

15:30.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Asserting that "the angels bowed down – all of them together" (`kulluhum ajma'una`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:30](ibnkathir://15/30); [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:30](tabari://15/30)) follows Christian apocryphal homilies depicting collective angelic homage to Adam in *Cave of Treasures* 2:20–22. At the same time, its universal phrasing sets up an internal categorical tension with [Quran 15:31](quran://15/31) and [Quran 18:50](quran://18/50) over how Iblis could violate a command addressed strictly to angels if he was a jinn.

15:31.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Exempting Iblis directly from the all-angelic prostration of [Quran 15:30](quran://15/30) because "he refused to be among those who bowed down" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:31](ibnkathir://15/31); [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:31](tabari://15/31)) mirrors the rebel angel Satan in *Life of Adam and Eve* 14:1–3. Adapting this fallen-angel motif while elsewhere reclassifying Iblis as one of the jinn in [Quran 18:50](quran://18/50) leaves unresolved why a non-angel was culpable under an order issued exclusively to angels.

15:32.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Depicting God questioning Iblis—"O Iblis, what is the matter with you, that you are not among those who bow down?" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:32](ibnkathir://15/32); [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:32](tabari://15/32))—tracks the dramatic interrogation scene of *Life of Adam and Eve* 14:2–3 and *Cave of Treasures* 2:22–24. No such pre-fall dialogue over bowing to Adam appears anywhere in [Genesis 3:1](bible://gn/3/1) or the Hebrew scriptures.

15:33.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Recording Iblis's objection that he would never bow to a mortal created "from dried clay, from molded mud" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:33](ibnkathir://15/33); [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:33](tabari://15/33)) reproduces the elemental-superiority argument of late antique apocrypha. In Syriac *Cave of Treasures* 2:23–24 and *Life of Adam and Eve* 14:3, the rebel spirit similarly refuses to venerate a creature fashioned from dust and mud rather than fire and spirit.

15:39.Theological Defect: Recording Iblis addressing God with the charge, "My Lord, because You have sent me astray" (`bi-ma aghwaytani`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:39](ibnkathir://15/39); [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:39](tabari://15/39)), leaves unrefuted the premise that Allah Himself authored Satan's rebellion and misguidance. Making God the causal source of demonic and human straying conflicts with the Biblical witness in [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13) and [Habakkuk 1:13](bible://hb/1/13) that God neither tempts anyone to evil nor approves wickedness.

15:82.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Claiming that the ancient pre-Mosaic inhabitants of al-Hijr (Thamud at Hegra, modern Mada'in Salih) "carved out of the mountains houses, feeling secure" (`buyutan aminina`)—an identification affirmed in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 15:82](ibnkathir://15/82), [Tafsir al-Tabari 15:80](tabari://15/80), and [Sahih al-Bukhari 3379](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3379)—misidentifies Monumental Nabataean architecture.
