Dated Nabataean Aramaic facade inscriptions and archaeological excavations prove that Hegra's rock-cut chambers were first-century BC to first-century AD funerary tombs rather than ancient residential houses.

16:15.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Asserting that God cast firm mountains (`alqa fi al-ardi rawasiya`) onto the earth "so that it does not sway with you" (`an tamida bikum`)—elaborated in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:15](ibnkathir://16/15) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:15](tabari://16/15) through reports that the newly created earth shook until mountains pinned it still—contradicts modern geophysics. Mountains are not stabilizing weights dropped from above to prevent shaking, but uplift structures formed by colliding tectonic plates along active fault zones where earthquakes concentrate.

16:36.Theological Defect: Dividing the nations who heard prophetic preaching into "some of them whom God guided, and some of them upon whom straying was justified" (`haqqat 'alayhi al-dalalatu`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:36](ibnkathir://16/36); [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:36](tabari://16/36)) frames human belief and unbelief as the outcome of a prior divine decree of misguidance. Predestining entire populations to inescapable error while condemning them for disbelief contrasts with God's universal saving grace in [John 3:16](bible://jn/3/16) and [Titus 2:11](bible://ti/2/11).

16:37.Theological Defect: Telling Muhammad, "Even if you are eager for their guidance, surely God does not guide those whom He leads astray, and they have no helpers" (`la yahdi man yudillu`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:37](ibnkathir://16/37); [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:37](tabari://16/37)), portrays Allah as actively leading people into error and refusing to restore them even when His own messenger earnestly seeks their salvation. Such divine obstruction of repentance stands in direct contrast to [Ezekiel 33:11](bible://ez/33/11) and [Romans 10:21](bible://rom/10/21).

16:43.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Commanding Muhammad's audience to "ask the people of the Reminder, if you do not know" (`fas'alu ahla al-dhikri`) directs seventh-century AD listeners to verify prophetic history with Jewish and Christian scholars reading the Torah and Gospel, as Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and al-A'mash confirm in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:43](ibnkathir://16/43) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:43](tabari://16/43). Treating contemporary Jews and Christians as an authoritative court of appeal presupposes that their extant Biblical scriptures were authentic and uncorrupted.

16:66.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Stating that cattle milk is produced inside their bellies (`fi butunihi`) "between excretions and blood" (`min bayni farthin wa-damin`)—explained literally in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:66](ibnkathir://16/66) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:66](tabari://16/66) as digested stomach matter separating directly into feces, blood, and milk—reflects pre-modern anatomical conjecture. In mammalian physiology, milk is synthesized outside the abdominal digestive tract within external mammary alveolar glands using bloodstream nutrients that never mingle with or sit adjacent to intestinal chyme or dung.

16:68.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Initiating a divine inspiration (`wahy`) to the female worker bee that continues directly in [Quran 16:69](quran://16/69) with the command to "eat from every kind of fruit" as the source of honey ([Tafsir al-Tabari 16:68](tabari://16/68); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:68](ibnkathir://16/68)) mischaracterizes honeybee foraging biology. Worker honeybees are specialized floral pollinators that collect nectar and pollen from blossoms rather than feeding indiscriminately on fruits.

16:69.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Commanding honeybees to "eat from every kind of fruit" (`kuli min kulli al-thamarati`) so that a healing drink emerges "from their bellies" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:69](ibnkathir://16/69); [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:69](tabari://16/69)) conflates floral nectar collection with universal fruit consumption. Honeybees do not eat every kind of fruit to manufacture honey; instead, worker bees draw liquid nectar from flowers into a non-digestive foregut honey-crop (`proventriculus`-isolated sac) and regurgitate it orally into honeycomb cells.

16:71.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: Presenting free masters' refusal to share their wealth equally with "those whom their right hands possess" (`ma malakat aymanuhum`) as a divinely instituted hierarchy proving Allah has no partners ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:71](ibnkathir://16/71); [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:71](tabari://16/71)) normalizes chattel slavery as part of God's permanent social design. Codifying human ownership and economic subjugation as an unquestioned theological premise contrasts with the equal creation of all people in God's image in [Genesis 1:27](bible://gn/1/27) and [Galatians 3:28](bible://gal/3/28).

16:75.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: Contrasting "an owned slave who has no power over anything" (`'abdan mamlukan la yaqdiru 'ala shay'in`) with a prosperous freeman to illustrate absolute superiority ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:75](ibnkathir://16/75); [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:75](tabari://16/75)) embeds the legal powerlessness and property status of enslaved people into divine revelation as an enduring moral baseline.

16:93.Theological Defect: Declaring that God could have united humanity as one community, "but He leads astray whomever He pleases and guides whomever He pleases" (`wa-lakin yudillu man yasha'u`), while immediately adding, "You will indeed be questioned about what you have done" ([Tafsir al-Tabari 16:93](tabari://16/93); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:93](ibnkathir://16/93)), creates an acute moral contradiction. Human beings are summoned to judgment and punished for the very religious division and misguidance that God Himself actively willed and produced.

16:101.Theological Defect: Institutionalizing the replacement of one revealed verse with another (`wa-idha baddalna ayatan makana ayatin`)—explained by Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Tabari in [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:101](tabari://16/101) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:101](ibnkathir://16/101) as divine abrogation (`naskh`) alongside [Quran 2:106](quran://2/106)—conflicts internally with [Quran 6:115](quran://6/115) and [Quran 18:27](quran://18/27), which state that none can alter God's words. Subjecting divine decrees to serial cancellation also contrasts with God's immutable nature and counsel in [Malachi 3:6](bible://mal/3/6) and [James 1:17](bible://jas/1/17).
16:101.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Preserving the firsthand objection of Meccan contemporaries who watched Muhammad retract and replace earlier recitations and protested, "You are only a forger!" (`innama anta muftarin`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:101](ibnkathir://16/101); [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:101](tabari://16/101)), documents how ad-hoc policy shifts operated during his career. Rather than offering an objective test to distinguish convenient revisions from eternal truth, the text simply asserts divine prerogative and dismisses eyewitness critics as ignorant.

16:102.Contradicts the Bible: Stating that "the holy spirit" (`ruh al-qudus`) brought the Quran down from God—unanimously identified in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:102](ibnkathir://16/102) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:102](tabari://16/102) in parallel with [Quran 2:97](quran://2/97) as the created angel Gabriel (`Jibril`)—reduces the Holy Spirit to a finite angelic messenger. This directly contradicts Biblical revelation, which identifies the Holy Spirit as God Himself in [Acts 5:3](bible://acts/5/3) through [Acts 5:4](bible://acts/5/4), unites Him in the one divine Name in [Matthew 28:19](bible://mt/28/19), and calls Him the eternal Spirit in [Hebrews 9:14](bible://heb/9/14).

16:103.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Recording contemporary Meccan eyewitness reports that "only a human being teaches him"—identified by Ibn Ishaq, Ibn 'Abbas, and Qatadah in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:103](ibnkathir://16/103) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:103](tabari://16/103) as a foreign Christian artisan in Mecca such as Jabr, Bal'am, or Ya'ish whom Muhammad frequented—answers the charge with a linguistic non-sequitur. Pointing out that the mentor's native tongue was foreign (`a'jamiyyun`) while the recitation is Arabic overlooks that oral Biblical and apocryphal stories are readily conveyed across languages and retold in Arabic, alongside numerous Syriac, Aramaic, and Ethiopic loanwords inside the Quran itself.

16:106.Theological Defect: Granting explicit divine exemption to a believer who verbally renounces God and utters polytheistic words under coercion so long as "his heart is secure in belief"—revealed when 'Ammar ibn Yasir reviled Muhammad under pressure per [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:106](ibnkathir://16/106) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:106](tabari://16/106)—establishes the juristic doctrine of religious dissimulation (`taqiyyah`). Sanctioning outward denial of God to avoid persecution contrasts sharply with Christ's command of faithful public confession before men in [Matthew 10:32](bible://mt/10/32) and [Matthew 10:33](bible://mt/10/33) and the apostolic standard of steadfast witness unto death in [Revelation 2:10](bible://rv/2/10).

16:112.Failed Prophecy: Striking a parable of a once-secure, abundantly supplied town clothed by God in "hunger and fear"—identified by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and scholarly consensus in [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:112](tabari://16/112) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:112](ibnkathir://16/112) as Mecca afflicted by famine and fear of Muhammad's raids—contradicts the Quran's own sanctuary guarantees. Passages such as [Quran 2:125](quran://2/125), [Quran 28:57](quran://28/57), and [Quran 29:67](quran://29/67) proclaim Mecca an inviolable safe sanctuary (`haraman aminan`), a claim further falsified historically by the destructive Umayyad sieges of Mecca in 683 AD and 692 AD and the Qarmatian sack and massacre of pilgrims in 930 AD.

16:124.Contradicts the Bible: Claiming that "the sabbath was only made for those who differed concerning it"—explained in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 16:124](ibnkathir://16/124), [Tafsir al-Tabari 16:124](tabari://16/124), and [Sahih al-Bukhari 876](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:876) as Israel erring by rejecting Friday and having Saturday imposed upon them because of their dispute—contradicts the Torah's account of the Sabbath. In [Genesis 2:2](bible://gn/2/2) through [Genesis 2:3](bible://gn/2/3), God Himself blessed and hallowed the seventh day at creation long before Israel existed, and in [Exodus 20:8](bible://ex/20/8) through [Exodus 20:11](bible://ex/20/11) and [Exodus 31:16](bible://ex/31/16) He instituted the seventh-day Sabbath directly as a perpetual creation covenant rather than a fallback substitute for Friday.

17:1.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: This verse states that Allah carried His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Distant Mosque (*al-Masjid al-Aqsa*), identified in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:1](ibnkathir://17/1) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 17:1](tabari://17/1) as the Jerusalem Temple (*Bayt al-Maqdis*). While modern defenders argue *masjid* merely denotes an open site of prostration, [Sahih Muslim 162a](/hadith/muslim/162a) describes Muhammad tethering al-Buraq to the prophets' ring, physically entering (*dakhaltu*) the mosque building, praying inside it, and exiting—even though Rome had demolished the Second Temple in AD 70 and the Umayyad Al-Aqsa structure was not built until decades after Muhammad's death.

17:2.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Allah affirms that He gave Moses the Book and made it 'a guidance for the Sons of Israel,' which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:2](ibnkathir://17/2) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 17:2](tabari://17/2) identify directly as the Torah (*al-Tawrah*) without alleging textual corruption. Together with [Quran 5:43-44](quran://5/43) and [Quran 10:94](quran://10/94), this unqualified endorsement of Mosaic Scripture reinforces the Islamic Dilemma by validating the authority of biblical texts that contradict Islamic theology.

17:15.Contradicts the Bible: Declaring that 'no one bearing a burden bears the burden of another,' [Quran 17:15](quran://17/15) is interpreted in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:15](ibnkathir://17/15) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 17:15](tabari://17/15) as an absolute denial that any soul can carry another's sins. This directly rejects the biblical doctrine of vicarious substitutionary atonement prophesied in [Isaiah 53:5-6](bible://is/53/5) and fulfilled by Christ bearing the sins of many on the cross in [Hebrews 9:28](bible://heb/9/28) and [Galatians 3:13](bible://gal/3/13).
17:15.Theological Defect: Although [Quran 17:15](quran://17/15) asserts both that no soul bears another's burden and that Allah never punishes before sending a messenger, canonical hadiths contradict both principles. [Sahih Muslim 2767a](/hadith/muslim/2767a) and [Sahih Muslim 2767d](/hadith/muslim/2767d) report that on Judgment Day Allah transfers mountain-sized sins from Muslims onto Jews and Christians as their ransom from Hellfire, while [Sahih Muslim 203](/hadith/muslim/203) places Muhammad's own father—who died during the unwarned pre-Islamic interval—in the Fire.

17:16.Theological Defect: In the standard Hafs text of [Quran 17:16](quran://17/16), Allah states that when He wills to destroy a town, He commands (*amarna*) its affluent elite, whereupon they act wickedly (*fa-fasaqu*) so that the decree of destruction is justified. While some commentators in [Tafsir al-Tabari 17:16](tabari://17/16) supply an unstated object ('commanded them to obey'), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:16](ibnkathir://17/16) records the classical exegesis that Allah subjugated them to commit immorality so they would merit punishment, portraying God as instigating sin (contrast [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13)).

17:45.Theological Defect: Allah states in [Quran 17:45](quran://17/45) that whenever Muhammad recites the Quran, God actively places an obscuring veil between the prophet and those who disbelieve in the Hereafter. As [Tafsir al-Tabari 17:45](tabari://17/45) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:45](ibnkathir://17/45) confirm, this divine barrier covers unbelievers' hearts precisely lest they comprehend and benefit from the message, standing in sharp tension with the biblical revelation of God's saving grace appearing to all people ([Titus 2:11](bible://ti/2/11), [John 3:16-17](bible://jn/3/16)).

17:46.Theological Defect: Expanding upon the preceding verse, [Quran 17:46](quran://17/46) declares that Allah places coverings (*akinnah*) over unbelievers' hearts and heaviness (*waqr*) in their ears specifically so that they do not understand the recitation. Both [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:46](ibnkathir://17/46) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 17:46](tabari://17/46) affirm that Allah Himself blocks their comprehension and guidance, depicting human unbelief as divinely engineered rather than calling all people everywhere to repentance ([Ezekiel 18:23](bible://ez/18/23), [Acts 17:30](bible://acts/17/30)).

17:47.Theological Defect: Here [Quran 17:47](quran://17/47) (like [Quran 25:8](quran://25/8)) condemns Muhammad's Meccan critics as evildoers for alleging, 'You are only following a man who is bewitched (*mashuran*),' which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:47](ibnkathir://17/47) defines as someone afflicted by magic (*sihr*). Yet [Sahih al-Bukhari 6063](/hadith/bukhari/6063) and [Sahih Muslim 2189a](/hadith/muslim/2189a) report on Aisha's authority that Labid ibn al-A'sam successfully bewitched Muhammad so that he imagined doing things with his wives that he had not done, confirming the very affliction the Quran rebukes critics for claiming.

17:59.Theological Defect: In [Quran 17:59](quran://17/59), Allah explains that He refrained from sending miraculous signs (*al-ayat*) to Mecca because ancient nations rejected them—an occasion [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:59](ibnkathir://17/59) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 17:59](tabari://17/59) tie to Quraysh's unanswered demands for physical wonders (cf. [Quran 17:90-93](quran://17/90), [Quran 29:50](quran://29/50)). This admission conflicts directly with [Sahih al-Bukhari 3637](/hadith/bukhari/3637), [Sahih al-Bukhari 3868](/hadith/bukhari/3868), and [Sahih Muslim 2802a](/hadith/muslim/2802a), which claim Muhammad answered Meccan demands by physically splitting the moon in two.

17:61.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: The account in [Quran 17:61](quran://17/61) of Allah commanding the angels to prostrate before Adam and Iblis refusing because Adam was formed from clay (cf. [Quran 7:11-12](quran://7/11), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:61](ibnkathir://17/61)) is absent from canonical Scripture. Rather, this motif reproduces late-antique apocryphal legends preserved in the *Life of Adam and Eve* (12-16) and the Syriac *Cave of Treasures* (2-3), while contradicting the biblical prohibition against angels or humans rendering worshipful prostration to any creature ([Matthew 4:10](bible://mt/4/10), [Revelation 22:8-9](bible://rv/22/8)).

17:97.Theological Defect: Explicitly attributing spiritual error to divine agency, [Quran 17:97](quran://17/97) declares that 'whoever He leads astray (*wa-man yudlil*) – you will not find for them any allies other than Him,' before describing Allah dragging them blind, mute, and deaf on their faces into perpetually rekindled Hellfire. As [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:97](ibnkathir://17/97) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 17:97](tabari://17/97) confirm, no one can guide whom Allah misguides, portraying God as condemning people for a state He Himself decreed (contrast [Ezekiel 33:11](bible://ez/33/11)).

17:101.Contradicts the Bible: While [Quran 17:101](quran://17/101) (cf. [Quran 27:12](quran://27/12)) states that Moses received 'nine clear signs' and invites Muhammad to 'ask the Sons of Israel,' the Hebrew Scriptures record ten distinct plagues upon Egypt ([Exodus 7:14](bible://ex/7/14) to [Exodus 12:30](bible://ex/12/30)) alongside preliminary signs ([Exodus 4:2-7](bible://ex/4/2)). Consequently, exegetes in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:101](ibnkathir://17/101) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 17:101](tabari://17/101) combine non-plague wonders (the staff, glowing hand, famine, or sea) with five plagues from [Quran 7:133](quran://7/133), omitting half the Exodus plagues including the Passover death of the firstborn ([Exodus 12:29](bible://ex/12/29)).

17:111.Contradicts the Bible: Inscribed inside Jerusalem's Dome of the Rock in AD 691, [Quran 17:111](quran://17/111) commands believers to praise God 'who has not taken a son, nor has He any associate in the kingdom.' Both [Tafsir al-Tabari 17:111](tabari://17/111) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 17:111](ibnkathir://17/111) argue that divine Fatherhood or shared dominion would imply weakness, directly contradicting the biblical revelation of Jesus Christ as the eternal Son of God who shares the Father's throne ([Psalms 2:7](bible://ps/2/7), [Matthew 3:17](bible://mt/3/17), [John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14), [Hebrews 1:8](bible://heb/1/8)).

18:4.Contradicts the Bible: Stating that the Quran was sent down 'to warn those who have said, "God has taken a son,"' [Quran 18:4](quran://18/4) issues an unqualified threat of divine punishment against confessing divine Sonship (cf. [Quran 17:111](quran://17/111), [Quran 19:35](quran://19/35)). Even though [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:4](tabari://18/4) notes early attempts to include pagan Arab beliefs alongside Christian doctrine, the categorical denial that God has a Son directly repudiates the core New Testament proclamation of Jesus Christ ([Matthew 16:16-17](bible://mt/16/16), [John 20:31](bible://jn/20/31)).

18:5.Contradicts the Bible: Continuing [Quran 18:4](quran://18/4), [Quran 18:5](quran://18/5) denounces those who affirm divine Sonship as possessing no knowledge and uttering nothing but a 'monstrous' word and a 'lie' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:5](ibnkathir://18/5), [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:5](tabari://18/5)). This directly contradicts both Old Testament messianic revelation ([Psalms 2:7](bible://ps/2/7), [Proverbs 30:4](bible://prv/30/4)) and the Father's own public testimony from heaven declaring Jesus His beloved Son ([Matthew 3:17](bible://mt/3/17)).

18:9.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Introducing 'the companions of the cave and al-Raqim,' [Quran 18:9](quran://18/9) incorporates into divine scripture the pre-Islamic Christian legend of the Seven Sleepers of Ephesus—Christian youths said to have hidden from Emperor Decius's persecution (AD 249-251) and awakened under Theodosius II (c. AD 447). Before the rise of Islam, this hagiographical tale circulated widely across the Near East in 6th-century Syriac homilies such as those of Jacob of Serugh (d. AD 521), explaining why Meccan and Jewish interlocutors already knew it as an old regional story ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:9](ibnkathir://18/9)).

18:17.Theological Defect: Concluding its description of the cave, [Quran 18:17](quran://18/17) declares that 'whoever God guides is the rightly guided one, and whoever He leads astray (*wa-man yudlil*) – you will not find for him an ally guiding him.' As [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:17](ibnkathir://18/17) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:17](tabari://18/17) affirm, Allah actively misguides whom He wills so that no guide can ever rescue them, conflicting with the biblical teaching that God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked and calls all to turn and live ([Ezekiel 33:11](bible://ez/33/11)).

18:22.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Pre-Islamic Syriac recensions of the Sleepers of Ephesus circulated competing counts of the youths (with Jacob of Serugh counting eight and Greek-Syriac variants counting seven). Reflecting these conflicting oral traditions, [Quran 18:22](quran://18/22) rehearses rival guesses ('three, the fourth of them was their dog... five, the sixth of them was their dog... seven, the eighth of them was their dog') and instructs Muhammad not to specify a definitive figure beyond saying, 'My Lord knows about their number' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:22](ibnkathir://18/22), [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:22](tabari://18/22)).

18:25.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Asserting that the youths 'remained in their cave for three hundred years and add nine,' [Quran 18:25](quran://18/25) diverges from the historical setting of the Christian Ephesus legend between Decius (AD 250) and Theodosius II (c. AD 447), an interval under two centuries. Whereas [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:25](ibnkathir://18/25) harmonizes the verse as converting 300 solar years into 309 lunar years, [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:25](tabari://18/25) records early exegetes arguing that [Quran 18:25](quran://18/25) merely reports Christian estimates that Allah declines to confirm in [Quran 18:26](quran://18/26).

18:27.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Commanding Muhammad to recite from the Book of his Lord, [Quran 18:27](quran://18/27) establishes the theological axiom that 'no one can change His words (*la mubaddila li-kalimatihi*),' which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:27](ibnkathir://18/27) defines as meaning no one can alter, distort, or corrupt them (cf. [Quran 6:115](quran://6/115), [Quran 10:64](quran://10/64)). Because the Quran affirms that the Torah and the Gospel are Allah's own revealed words ([Quran 3:3-4](quran://3/3), [Quran 5:44-47](quran://5/44)), this principle of divine textual incorruptibility refutes later polemical claims that humans corrupted the Bible.

18:50.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Fuses pre-Islamic Arabian *jinn* folklore—portraying Iblis as a fiery spirit fathering physical offspring (*dhurriyyah*, [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:50](tabari://18/50))—onto the Late Antique apocryphal legend of Satan refusing to bow before newly created Adam ([Quran 18:50](quran://18/50); cf. [Genesis 2:7](bible://gn/2/7)), blending local Arabian demonology with non-canonical Syriac and pseudepigraphal Adam traditions.
18:50.Theological Defect: While six parallel passages ([Quran 2:34](quran://2/34), [Quran 7:11](quran://7/11), [Quran 15:30-31](quran://15/30), [Quran 17:61](quran://17/61), [Quran 20:116](quran://20/116), [Quran 38:73-74](quran://38/73)) address the prostration command exclusively to the angels and except Iblis from their group, [Quran 18:50](quran://18/50) abruptly classifies him as 'one of the jinn' possessing physical 'descendants.' As [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:50](tabari://18/50) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:50](ibnkathir://18/50) document, this produced an unresolved exegetical conflict over whether Iblis was an angel or a non-angelic jinn inexplicably bound by an angelic command.

18:57.Theological Defect: In [Quran 18:57](quran://18/57), Allah declares that He has placed coverings (*akinnah*) over disbelievers' hearts lest they understand the message and deafness (*waqr*) in their ears, adding, 'Even if you call them to the guidance, they will never be guided.' Both [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:57](ibnkathir://18/57) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:57](tabari://18/57) confirm that this divine barrier permanently forecloses their repentance, contrasting with the biblical God whose saving grace invites all people to repentance ([Titus 2:11](bible://ti/2/11), [Acts 17:30](bible://acts/17/30)).

18:60.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Launching an episode wholly absent from the Pentateuch, [Quran 18:60](quran://18/60) depicts Moses—explicitly identified in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4727](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4727) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:60](ibnkathir://18/60) as the biblical Moses of Israel accompanied by Joshua ([Exodus 24:13](bible://ex/24/13))—questing for 'the junction of the two seas' to study under al-Khidr ([Quran 18:65](quran://18/65)). Scholars trace this composite tale to late-antique Near Eastern lore combining the *Alexander Romance* search for the Spring of Life at the confluence of the seas with rabbinic theodicy legends (preserved in the *Story of Rabbi Joshua ben Levi* traveling silently with Elijah).

18:61.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: In [Quran 18:61](quran://18/61) (and [Quran 18:63](quran://18/63)), Moses and his servant mark their destination when their dead, salted fish revives and swims off into the sea—an event [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:61](ibnkathir://18/61) attributes to water splashing from the 'Spring of Life' (*'Ayn al-Hayat*). This specific episode reproduces a famous scene from the pre-Islamic *Alexander Romance* (Pseudo-Callisthenes II.39), in which Alexander's cook washes a dried salted fish in the Spring of Life and watches it come back to life and escape into the water, transferring an Alexander motif directly onto Moses.

18:74.Theological Defect: In [Quran 18:74](quran://18/74), Allah's divinely instructed servant al-Khidr ([Quran 18:65](quran://18/65)) kills an innocent young boy (*ghulaman*), prompting Moses to object that he has slain a pure, sinless soul without retaliation for murder ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:74](ibnkathir://18/74), [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:74](tabari://18/74)). Because al-Khidr affirms in [Quran 18:82](quran://18/82) that 'I did not do it on my own command,' the narrative attributes the extrajudicial killing of an innocent minor directly to divine command, violating biblical justice ([Deuteronomy 24:16](bible://dt/24/16), [Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20)).

18:80.Theological Defect: Explaining why the child was slain, [Quran 18:80](quran://18/80) states that his parents were believers and 'we feared that he would burden them both with insolent transgression and disbelief,' while [Quran 18:81](quran://18/81) adds the utilitarian goal of replacing him with a purer child. Citing Muhammad's declaration in [Sahih Muslim 2662a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2662a), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:80](ibnkathir://18/80) confirms that the boy was created an unbeliever by innate decree from the day he was made (cf. [Sahih Muslim 2662c](/hadith/muslim/2662c)), depicting Allah as predestining a child to unbelief and executing him preemptively.

18:83.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Introducing Dhu al-Qarnayn ('the Two-Horned One'), [Quran 18:83](quran://18/83) opens an itinerary—traveling to the sun's western setting-place ([Quran 18:86](quran://18/86)), its eastern rising-place ([Quran 18:90](quran://18/90)), and a northern mountain pass to cast an iron-and-copper gate against Gog and Magog ([Quran 18:94-96](quran://18/94))—that reproduces the 6th-century Syriac *Alexander Legend* (*Neshana d-Aleksandros*), a Christian apocalyptic romance depicting Alexander the Great (portrayed with Ammon's two ram's horns on ancient coinage) as a pious monotheist.
18:83.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Portraying the protagonist of the Alexander tradition in [Quran 18:83-84](quran://18/83) as a devout monotheistic ruler receiving direct revelation from Allah ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:83](ibnkathir://18/83), [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:83](tabari://18/83)) contradicts the historical reality of Alexander III of Macedon (356-323 BC), a committed polytheist who sacrificed to Greek and Babylonian gods and claimed divine parentage from Zeus-Ammon. Modern efforts to re-identify Dhu al-Qarnayn as Cyrus the Great fail because neither Persian nor classical records attribute Alexander's fetid-sea journey or Gog-and-Magog iron gate to Cyrus.

18:86.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: In [Quran 18:86](quran://18/86), Dhu al-Qarnayn travels west until 'he reached the setting-place of the sun (*maghriba al-shamsi*)' and 'found it setting in a muddy spring (*fi 'aynin hami'atin*)'—or 'a hot spring (*hamiyatin*)' in the canonical Kufan reading recorded in [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:86](tabari://18/86). Although later commentators like [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:86](ibnkathir://18/86) reinterpret 'found it' as a coastal optical illusion, the Arabic noun *'ayn* denotes a localized spring rather than an ocean, and reaching a physical western endpoint where the sun descends reflects flat-earth cosmology (cf. [Sahih al-Bukhari 3199](/hadith/bukhari/3199)).
18:86.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Dhu al-Qarnayn's westward march in [Quran 18:86](quran://18/86) to the physical setting-place of the sun in a murky, muddy body of water beside a western nation directly parallels the pre-Islamic Syriac *Alexander Legend*, in which Alexander journeys to the western edge of a flat earth where the sun sets beyond the fetid, foul water (*yama sarya*) and executes judgment upon wicked inhabitants.

18:90.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Mirroring [Quran 18:86](quran://18/86), [Quran 18:90](quran://18/90) states that Dhu al-Qarnayn traveled east until 'he reached the rising-place of the sun (*matli'a al-shamsi*)' and found it rising directly upon an unsheltered people—whom early reports in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:90](ibnkathir://18/90) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 18:90](tabari://18/90) (echoing the Syriac *Alexander Legend*) describe as diving into water or tunnels to survive the sun's immediate emergence. Depicting a traveler walking to physical eastern and western terrestrial endpoints of sunrise and sunset presupposes a flat earth rather than a rotating globe orbiting a distant star.

18:94.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: In [Quran 18:94](quran://18/94), northern inhabitants ask Dhu al-Qarnayn to construct a barrier against 'Yajuj and Majuj' (Gog and Magog). Whereas biblical prophecy in [Ezekiel 38:2](bible://ez/38/2) and [Revelation 20:8](bible://rv/20/8) never links Gog and Magog to Alexander or a physical wall, the motif of Alexander erecting an iron gate in a northern pass to confine Gog and Magog developed in post-biblical lore (Josephus, *Jewish War* 7.7.4) and assumed its exact Quranic apocalyptic plot in the 6th-century Syriac *Alexander Legend*.

18:96.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Describing physical geography, [Quran 18:96-98](quran://18/96) states that Dhu al-Qarnayn sealed a pass between two cliffs with solid iron blocks heated fiery red and coated with molten copper, trapping Gog and Magog behind it until the end times ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 18:96](ibnkathir://18/96)). Canonical hadiths confirm this barrier was understood literally, with Muhammad reporting a finger-sized breach opened that day ([Sahih al-Bukhari 3346](/hadith/bukhari/3346), [Sahih al-Bukhari 7059](/hadith/bukhari/7059), [Sahih Muslim 2880a](/hadith/muslim/2880a)) holding back hordes outnumbering Muslims 999 to 1 ([Sahih Muslim 222a](/hadith/muslim/222a))—yet global satellite cartography confirms no such metal dam or walled-off population exists on Earth.

19:7.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Declares that Allah had never before assigned the name Yahya (John) to anyone ([Quran 19:7](quran://19/7))—an interpretation endorsed by Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and preferred in [Tafsir al-Tabari 19:7](tabari://19/7) (cf. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 19:7](ibnkathir://19/7)). Whereas [Luke 1:61](bible://lk/1/61) merely records Zechariah's neighbors observing that none of his immediate relatives bore the name John, the Hebrew equivalent *Yehohanan* (*Yohanan*) was already borne by numerous earlier Old Testament figures, including individuals recorded in [Jeremiah 40:8](bible://jer/40/8), [Ezra 10:6](bible://ezr/10/6), and [Nehemiah 12:22](bible://neh/12/22). Even Mujahid's secondary reading of *samiyyan* as 'one similar to him' runs counter to al-Tabari's primary lexical judgment and the direct narrative parallel with [Luke 1:61](bible://lk/1/61).

19:17.Contradicts the Bible: Identifies 'Our Spirit' (*ruhana*) dispatched to Mary in human form as the created angel Gabriel ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 19:17](ibnkathir://19/17); [Tafsir al-Tabari 19:17](tabari://19/17); cf. [Quran 16:102](quran://16/102) and [Quran 26:193](quran://26/193)). This conflates the angel Gabriel—who acts solely as a herald in [Luke 1:26-35](bible://lk/1/26)—with the divine Holy Spirit, the third Person of the Trinity who overshadows Mary so that her child is called the Son of God ([Luke 1:35](bible://lk/1/35); [Matthew 1:20](bible://mt/1/20)).

19:19.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Records Gabriel announcing Jesus as 'a boy who is pure (*ghulaman zakiyyan*)' ([Quran 19:19](quran://19/19); [Tafsir al-Tabari 19:19](tabari://19/19)), attributing moral purity uniquely to Christ at His conception. Canonical traditions in [Sahih al-Bukhari 3286](/hadith/bukhari/3286), [Sahih al-Bukhari 3431](/hadith/bukhari/3431), and [Sahih Muslim 2366a](/hadith/muslim/2366a) reinforce this concession by reporting Muhammad's statement that Satan touches every newborn descendant of Adam at birth except Mary and her Son, echoing the New Testament testimony to Christ's sinlessness ([Hebrews 4:15](bible://heb/4/15); [Luke 1:35](bible://lk/1/35)).

19:23.Contradicts the Bible: Depicts Mary giving birth alone in solitary anguish beside a remote date-palm trunk while wishing she had died and been forgotten ([Quran 19:22-23](quran://19/22); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 19:23](ibnkathir://19/23)). This account conflicts with the first-century historical narrative in [Luke 2:4-7](bible://lk/2/4) and [Matthew 1:24-25](bible://mt/1/24), where Mary travels with her betrothed husband Joseph to Bethlehem, rejoices in God her Savior ([Luke 1:46-47](bible://lk/1/46)), and delivers Jesus within a populated Judean town.

19:25.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Instructs the laboring Mary to shake a dry date-palm trunk so fresh ripe dates drop upon her while a miraculous stream flows beneath her ([Quran 19:24-25](quran://19/24); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 19:25](ibnkathir://19/25); [Tafsir al-Tabari 19:25](tabari://19/25)). This episode adapts a non-canonical legend preserved in the apocryphal *Gospel of Pseudo-Matthew* (chapter 20), where the infant Jesus commands a palm tree during the flight to Egypt to bend down its fruit for Mary and open a hidden spring of water from its roots, merging a late flight-to-Egypt folktale into the nativity itself.

19:28.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Has Mary's kinsfolk address her directly as 'Sister of Aaron!' (*ya ukhta Harun*, [Quran 19:28](quran://19/28)), conflating first-century Mary (*Maryam*) with Miriam (*Maryam*), the sister of Aaron and Moses who lived roughly fourteen centuries earlier ([Exodus 15:20](bible://ex/15/20); [Numbers 26:59](bible://nm/26/59)). Although Muhammad replied to the Christians of Najran in [Sahih Muslim 2135](/hadith/muslim/2135) (cf. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 19:28](ibnkathir://19/28)) that Israelites named people after pious predecessors, calling Mary both 'sister of Aaron' here and 'daughter of Imran' (Amram) in [Quran 66:12](quran://66/12) and [Quran 3:35](quran://3/35) reproduces two specific family relationships of Mosaic Miriam ([Numbers 26:59](bible://nm/26/59)) rather than a personal namesake.

19:30.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Portrays the newborn Jesus speaking articulately from the cradle to defend Mary ([Quran 19:29-30](quran://19/29); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 19:30](ibnkathir://19/30); [Tafsir al-Tabari 19:30](tabari://19/30)), an episode absent from the canonical Gospels ([Luke 2:21-40](bible://lk/2/21)) and derived from late Christian apocrypha preserved in the *Arabic Infancy Gospel* (chapter 1).
19:30.Contradicts the Bible: Places in the mouth of the infant Jesus the past-tense declaration, 'He has given me the Book and made me a prophet' ([Quran 19:30](quran://19/30); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 19:30](ibnkathir://19/30)). Treating the Gospel (*Injil*) as a pre-written codex conferred upon Jesus in infancy contradicts the New Testament witness that Jesus grew in wisdom ([Luke 2:52](bible://lk/2/52)), inaugurated His public ministry around age thirty ([Luke 3:23](bible://lk/3/23)), and personally embodied the Gospel message later recorded by apostolic eyewitnesses ([Luke 1:1-4](bible://lk/1/1)).

19:35.Contradicts the Bible: Asserts that 'it is not for God to take any son' ([Quran 19:35](quran://19/35); [Tafsir al-Tabari 19:35](tabari://19/35)), framing divine Sonship as an acquired creaturely adoption incompatible with creation by divine fiat. This repudiates the angel Gabriel's explicit announcement in the very nativity account being retold that Mary's child 'will be called the Son of the Most High' and 'the Son of God' ([Luke 1:32-35](bible://lk/1/32)), as well as the eternal Word's incarnation ([John 1:1-14](bible://jn/1/1)).

19:83.Theological Defect: States that Allah actively dispatches devils (*al-shayatin*) against unbelievers to incite and prod them fiercely into sin (*ta'uzzuhum azzan*, [Quran 19:83](quran://19/83)). Classical commentators including Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, and al-Tabari confirm in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 19:83](ibnkathir://19/83) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 19:83](tabari://19/83) that Allah sends demons to entice and push people into disobedience until they enter Hellfire, directly opposing the biblical revelation that God is holy and never tempts anyone to evil ([James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13); [Habakkuk 1:13](bible://hb/1/13)).

19:88.Contradicts the Bible: Condemns the confession that 'the Merciful has taken a son' as a monstrous utterance that nearly splits the heavens open and collapses the mountains ([Quran 19:88-90](quran://19/88); [Tafsir al-Tabari 19:88](tabari://19/88)). This polemic directly contradicts the Father's own voice from heaven declaring of Jesus, 'This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well-pleased' ([Matthew 3:17](bible://mt/3/17); [Matthew 17:5](bible://mt/17/5)), and the apostolic proclamation of Christ as the eternal Son ([John 3:16-18](bible://jn/3/16)).

19:92.Contradicts the Bible: Argues that it is unsuitable for the Merciful to have a son ([Quran 19:92](quran://19/92)), which [Tafsir al-Tabari 19:92](tabari://19/92) grounds in the physical assumption that sonship requires sexual desire and intercourse with a female consort (cf. [Quran 6:101](quran://6/101)). Christian Scripture never teaches physical procreation by God, instead revealing the Son as the eternal radiance of the Father's glory and exact imprint of His nature ([Hebrews 1:2-3](bible://heb/1/2); [John 1:18](bible://jn/1/18)).

19:93.Contradicts the Bible: Declares that every being in the heavens and earth approaches God strictly as a slave (*'abdan*, [Quran 19:93](quran://19/93)), which [Tafsir al-Tabari 19:93](tabari://19/93) explains as excluding any filial bond with God. This slave-master ontology denies both Christ's natural divine Sonship and the New Testament promise that believers receive the Spirit of adoption to cry 'Abba! Father!' as redeemed children and heirs, no longer slaves ([Galatians 4:4-7](bible://gal/4/4); [Romans 8:15-17](bible://rom/8/15); [John 1:12](bible://jn/1/12)).

20:22.Contradicts the Bible: Commands Moses to draw his hand to his side so that it emerges 'white, without any disease (*min ghayri su'*)' ([Quran 20:22](quran://20/22)), which Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah explicitly define in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 20:22](ibnkathir://20/22) as free from leprosy or ailment. This directly contradicts the original sign recorded in [Exodus 4:6-7](bible://ex/4/6), where Moses's hand emerges 'leprous like snow' before God restores it to healthy flesh to display His sovereign power over affliction and healing.

20:71.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Portrays Pharaoh threatening to amputate the magicians' opposite hands and feet and crucify (*wa-la-usallibannakum*) them on date-palm trunks ([Quran 20:71](quran://20/71); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 20:71](ibnkathir://20/71); [Tafsir al-Tabari 20:71](tabari://20/71)). Archaeological and historical records attest no practice of crucifixion in New Kingdom Bronze Age Egypt—a punishment developed centuries later by Neo-Assyrian and Achaemenid Persian rulers—while Pharaoh's exact formula mirrors the seventh-century *hirabah* penalty prescribed in [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33).

20:85.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Attributes the crafting of the Golden Calf at Mount Sinai to 'al-Samiri' ('the Samaritan,' [Quran 20:85](quran://20/85); cf. [Quran 20:87](quran://20/87) and [Quran 20:95](quran://20/95)). Because the city of Samaria was not founded by King Omri until c. 880 BC and the Samaritan community emerged only after the Assyrian resettlement following 722 BC ([Ezra 4:9-10](bible://ezr/4/9); [John 4:9](bible://jn/4/9)), placing a Samaritan at the Bronze Age Exodus introduces a multi-century chronological anachronism.
20:85.Theological Defect: Has Allah inform Moses, 'Surely We have tempted (*fatanna*) your people after you left them' ([Quran 20:85](quran://20/85); [Tafsir al-Tabari 20:85](tabari://20/85)), framing the Israelites' fall into calf-idolatry as a divine enticement orchestrated in Moses's absence. In [Exodus 32:7-8](bible://ex/32/7) and [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13), by contrast, human rebellion originates solely from creaturely unfaithfulness, as God never tempts anyone into idolatry.

20:88.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Describes the metallic Golden Calf emerging with a living 'mooing sound' (*khuwar*, [Quran 20:88](quran://20/88)), which classical exegetes in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 20:88](ibnkathir://20/88) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 20:88](tabari://20/88) explain as the idol coming to life and lowing when dust from Gabriel's steed was cast into it. This detail is absent from [Exodus 32:4](bible://ex/32/4) and derives from late rabbinic aggadah preserved in *Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer* (chapter 45), where the calf lows aloud to deceive Israel.

20:90.Contradicts the Bible: Exonerates Aaron by claiming he sternly warned the Israelites against worshipping the calf before Moses returned ([Quran 20:90-94](quran://20/90); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 20:90](ibnkathir://20/90); [Tafsir al-Tabari 20:90](tabari://20/90)) and shifted culpability entirely onto al-Samiri. This contradicts [Exodus 32:2-5](bible://ex/32/2), [Exodus 32:21-24](bible://ex/32/21), and [Deuteronomy 9:20](bible://dt/9/20), where Aaron personally collects the gold earrings, fashions the molten calf, builds an altar before it, and incurs God's severe wrath requiring Moses's intercession.

20:95.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Depicts Moses directly interrogating 'al-Samiri' by that gentilic title at Sinai ([Quran 20:95](quran://20/95)), reinforcing the anachronism of [Quran 20:85](quran://20/85) by treating 'the Samaritan' as a contemporary identity centuries before Samaria existed. Classical commentators in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 20:95](ibnkathir://20/95) struggled to resolve this title by conjecturing that he hailed from cow-worshipping Bajarma, Kirman in Persia, or the later Mesopotamian town of Samarra—mutually conflicting guesses that underscore the historical dislocation.

20:96.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Has al-Samiri explain that he seized a handful of dust from 'the footprint of the messenger' and tossed it into the molten calf ([Quran 20:96](quran://20/96)), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 20:96](ibnkathir://20/96) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 20:96](tabari://20/96) identify as magical life-giving soil from the hoofprint of Gabriel's horse at the Red Sea. This motif adapts post-biblical midrashic lore (cf. *Exodus Rabbah* 42:9 and *Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer* 45), where Micah or an idolater uses a mystical token from the Sea crossing to animate the Golden Calf.

20:116.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Recounts Allah commanding the angels to prostrate before newly created Adam while Iblis refuses ([Quran 20:116](quran://20/116); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 20:116](ibnkathir://20/116)). Entirely absent from [Genesis 1:26-27](bible://gn/1/26) and [Genesis 2:7](bible://gn/2/7)—where worship belongs exclusively to God ([Matthew 4:10](bible://mt/4/10); [Revelation 22:8-9](bible://rv/22/8))—this episode reproduces the apocryphal legend preserved in the *Life of Adam and Eve* (chapters 13-16) and the Syriac *Cave of Treasures*.

20:120.Contradicts the Bible: States that Satan whispered directly to Adam, offering to show him 'the Tree of Immortality (*shajarat al-khuld*) and a kingdom that does not decay' ([Quran 20:120](quran://20/120); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 20:120](ibnkathir://20/120)). In [Genesis 2:17](bible://gn/2/17) and [Genesis 3:1-6](bible://gn/3/1), by contrast, the serpent approaches Eve rather than Adam, and the forbidden tree is the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, distinctly separate from the Tree of Life ([Genesis 3:22](bible://gn/3/22)).

20:121.Theological Defect: Records that 'Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred' ([Quran 20:121](quran://20/121)), a verse that Muhammad interprets in [Sahih Muslim 2652c](/hadith/muslim/2652c) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 6614](/hadith/bukhari/6614) (cited in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 20:122](ibnkathir://20/122)) as proof that Adam defeated Moses in debate because Allah had pre-written Adam's sin forty years before creating him. Grounding Adam's exoneration in prior divine decree reduces human transgression to fatalistic predestination and undermines personal moral accountability ([Romans 5:12](bible://rom/5/12); [James 1:13-15](bible://jas/1/13)).

20:122.Contradicts the Bible: Claims that immediately after Adam's disobedience, 'his Lord chose him, turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him' ([Quran 20:122](quran://20/122); [Tafsir al-Tabari 20:122](tabari://20/122)), reducing the Fall to a private lapse resolved without atonement. This contradicts the biblical revelation that Adam's rebellion brought spiritual breach, mortality, and universal bondage to sin upon the human race, necessitating redemption through the obedience and atoning sacrifice of Christ, the last Adam ([Genesis 3:17-24](bible://gn/3/17); [Romans 5:12-19](bible://rom/5/12)).

21:7.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Commands Muhammad's skeptical audience, 'Just ask the People of the Reminder (*ahl al-dhikr*), if you do not know' ([Quran 21:7](quran://21/7); cf. [Quran 16:43](quran://16/43) and [Quran 10:94](quran://10/94)), whom both [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 21:7](ibnkathir://21/7) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 21:7](tabari://21/7) identify as the scholars of the Torah and the Gospel. Directing seventh-century inquirers to consult Jews and Christians as authoritative arbiters of prophetic history presupposes that their extant Scriptures remained reliable and uncorrupted.
21:7.Contradicts the Bible: Asserts alongside [Quran 21:8](quran://21/8) that Allah never sent anyone before Muhammad except mortal men (*rijalan*), reducing every prior divine envoy solely to creaturely prophet status ([Tafsir al-Tabari 21:7](tabari://21/7)). While biblical prophets were indeed human, the very Torah and Gospel to which the verse appeals testify that God ultimately sent His eternal, pre-existent Son in human flesh ([John 1:1-14](bible://jn/1/1); [Galatians 4:4](bible://gal/4/4); [Hebrews 1:1-3](bible://heb/1/1)).

21:23.Theological Defect: Declares of Allah, 'He will not be questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned' ([Quran 21:23](quran://21/23); [Tafsir al-Tabari 21:23](tabari://21/23)). In [Sahih Muslim 2650](/hadith/muslim/2650), Companions invoke this verse to silence moral objections after Muhammad states that human deeds are pre-decreed because Allah inspires every soul with its wickedness and piety ([Quran 91:8](quran://91/8)), grounding divine authority in sheer ownership rather than God's immutable moral righteousness ([Genesis 18:25](bible://gn/18/25); [Deuteronomy 32:4](bible://dt/32/4)).

21:30.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Claims that 'the heavens and the earth were once a solid mass (*ratqan*), and We split the two of them apart (*fataqnahuma*)' ([Quran 21:30](quran://21/30)), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 21:30](ibnkathir://21/30) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 21:30](tabari://21/30) explain as seven stacked heavens and the earth originally fused together before Allah separated them with air so rain could fall. Contrary to modern Big Bang reinterpretations, Planet Earth did not exist alongside the early cosmos to be split from the heavens, having accreted roughly nine billion years after cosmic expansion from heavy elements forged inside earlier generations of stars.

21:31.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: States that Allah placed firm mountains (*rawasi*) upon the earth 'so that it does not sway with them' ([Quran 21:31](quran://21/31); cf. [Quran 16:15](quran://16/15) and [Quran 31:10](quran://31/10)), interpreted in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 21:31](ibnkathir://21/31) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 21:31](tabari://21/31) as heavy stabilizing pegs preventing a water-surrounded landmass from tilting or quaking. Modern plate tectonics demonstrates the opposite: mountain ranges are pushed up by tectonic plate collisions and fault zones that are primary epicenters of seismic activity rather than stabilizers preventing earthquakes.

21:32.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Describes the sky as 'a guarded roof (*saqfan mahfuzan*)' erected over the earth ([Quran 21:32](quran://21/32)), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 21:32](ibnkathir://21/32) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 21:32](tabari://21/32) define as a physical dome raised without pillars and guarded from devils (cf. [Quran 22:65](quran://22/65) and [Quran 50:6](quran://50/6)). This reflects ancient Near Eastern solid-firmament cosmology rather than a gaseous atmosphere enveloping a spherical planet in open space.

21:33.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Pairs the creation of night and day with 'the sun and the moon, each floating in an orbit (*falak*)' ([Quran 21:33](quran://21/33); cf. [Quran 36:38-40](quran://36/38)), while omitting any motion of the earth. Classical authorities in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 21:33](ibnkathir://21/33) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 21:33](tabari://21/33) (citing Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid) describe this *falak* as revolving like a spindle whorl or hand-mill axis around a stationary earth, reflecting pre-modern geocentrism that attributes day and night to solar revolution rather than Earth's axial rotation.

21:58.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Narrates Abraham smashing his people's idols into pieces while sparing the largest statue so they would question it ([Quran 21:58](quran://21/58); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 21:58](ibnkathir://21/58)). Entirely absent from the patriarchal history in [Genesis 11:27-32](bible://gn/11/27) and [Genesis 12:1-5](bible://gn/12/1), this narrative reproduces the post-biblical rabbinic midrash preserved in *Genesis Rabbah* 38:13, where young Abram shatters Terah's idols and places an axe in the hand of the largest image.

21:63.Theological Defect: Records Abraham falsely declaring of the shattered idols, 'No! This big one of them did it' ([Quran 21:63](quran://21/63)), a statement derived from *Genesis Rabbah* 38:13 that Muhammad explicitly classifies in [Sahih al-Bukhari 3358](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3358) (cited in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 21:63](ibnkathir://21/63)) as one of three lies told by Abraham. Canonizing a midrashic fabrication as scripture forced classical theologians in [Tafsir al-Tabari 21:63](tabari://21/63) into strained grammatical qualifications to reconcile prophetic falsehood with the doctrine of prophetic impeccability (*'ismah*).

21:66.Theological Defect: Has Abraham rebuke idolaters for venerating objects 'that do not benefit you at all, or harm you, instead of God' ([Quran 21:66](quran://21/66); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 21:66](ibnkathir://21/66)). In [Sahih al-Bukhari 1597](/hadith/bukhari/1597) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 1605](/hadith/bukhari/1605), Caliph 'Umar ibn al-Khattab addresses Mecca's Black Stone with this exact formula—confessing it is merely a stone that can neither harm nor benefit anyone, kissed solely because Muhammad kissed it—highlighting the retention of pre-Islamic Arabian litholatry rites within Islamic pilgrimage.

21:68.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Depicts Abraham's Mesopotamian countrymen crying, 'Burn him, and help your gods!' and hurling him into a massive execution pyre ([Quran 21:68](quran://21/68); [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 21:68](ibnkathir://21/68); [Tafsir al-Tabari 21:68](tabari://21/68)). 33:51.Devalues Women: Removes any enforceable right of co-wives to equal time or marital companionship, instructing them instead to 'be pleased with what you give them—all of them' regardless of whether they are set aside or recalled ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 33:51](ibnkathir://33/51)), leaving aging wives like Sawda bint Zam'a to surrender their marital turn to Aisha out of fear of divorce ([Sahih al-Bukhari 5212](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5212)).

33:52.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: Even while restricting further free marriages or exchanging wives regardless of their beauty, the verse explicitly carves out an unrestricted exception for enslaved female concubines ('except for what your right hand owns'), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 33:52](ibnkathir://33/52) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 33:52](tabari://33/52) confirm allowed continued sexual access to slave women without marriage.

33:53.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Revealed on the night of Muhammad's wedding feast with Zaynab bint Jahsh to dismiss lingering dinner guests who annoyed him when he felt reluctant to ask them to leave, as Anas ibn Malik recounts in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4791](/hadith/bukhari/4791) and [Sahih Muslim 1428a](/hadith/muslim/1428a), while simultaneously enacting Umar ibn al-Khattab's demand for the veil ([Sahih al-Bukhari 402](/hadith/bukhari/402)) and permanently banning anyone from marrying Muhammad's widows ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 33:53](ibnkathir://33/53)).
33:53.Devalues Women: Mandates strict physical seclusion requiring men to speak to Muhammad's wives only 'from behind a veil (hijab)' and permanently forbids his widows from ever remarrying after his death ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 33:53](ibnkathir://33/53), [Tafsir al-Tabari 33:53](tabari://33/53)), consigning young widows such as Aisha—widowed at roughly eighteen—to lifelong celibacy to preserve Muhammad's posthumous honor.

33:57.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Pronounces God's curse in this world and the Hereafter upon 'those who hurt God and His messenger,' the exact charge Muhammad invoked when commissioning the assassination of the Jewish poet Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4037](/hadith/bukhari/4037) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 3031](/hadith/bukhari/3031), establishing a primary Quranic foundation in classical jurisprudence for executing critics accused of insulting Muhammad ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 33:57](ibnkathir://33/57)).

33:59.Devalues Women: Commands believing women to draw their outer garments (jalabib) over themselves 'so that they may be recognized and not hurt,' linking a woman's protection from male street harassment to her outer covering ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 33:59](ibnkathir://33/59), [Tafsir al-Tabari 33:59](tabari://33/59)).
33:59.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: Both [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 33:59](ibnkathir://33/59) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 33:59](tabari://33/59) explicitly explain that the outer jilbab veil was mandated specifically to distinguish free Muslim women from enslaved females (ima'), leaving enslaved women unveiled and legally unprotected from male accosting in the streets of Medina while safeguarding only free women's honor.
33:59.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Revealed immediately after Umar ibn al-Khattab repeatedly urged Muhammad to veil his wives and then publicly called out to Muhammad's wife Sawda bint Zam'a—'We have recognized you, O Sawda!'—when she went out at night to relieve herself, hoping a divine decree on veiling would descend, as recorded in [Sahih al-Bukhari 146](/hadith/bukhari/146), [Sahih al-Bukhari 6240](/hadith/bukhari/6240), and [Sahih Muslim 2170d](/hadith/muslim/2170d).

33:60.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Threatens Medinan hypocrites, doubters ('those in whose hearts is a sickness'), and spreaders of unsettling reports (al-murjifun) that Allah will incite Muhammad against them to forcibly expel them from Medina ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 33:60](ibnkathir://33/60), [Tafsir al-Tabari 33:60](tabari://33/60)), sanctioning state-directed banishment against internal political and religious dissenters.

33:61.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Escalates the threat against the Medinan dissidents of [Quran 33:60](quran://33/60) by declaring them accursed and commanding that 'wherever they are found, they will be seized and completely killed,' which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 33:61](ibnkathir://33/61) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 33:61](tabari://33/61) interpret as mandating their capture and summary execution if they persist in dissent.

33:69.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Warns believers not to hurt Moses as the Israelites did before Allah 'cleared him of what they said'—an episode that Muhammad himself, as quoted in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 33:69](ibnkathir://33/69), [Tafsir al-Tabari 33:69](tabari://33/69), [Sahih al-Bukhari 278](/hadith/bukhari/278), and [Sahih Muslim 339b](/hadith/muslim/339b), identifies as a tale in which a rock fled carrying Moses's clothes so he chased it naked before the Israelites to disprove rumors of a scrotal hernia and beat the stone leaving marks on it, an unhistorical folkloric legend absent from [Numbers 12:1](bible://nm/12/1).

34:9.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Threatens disbelievers that God could cause the earth to swallow them or let physical fragments (kisaf) of the sky fall upon them, which [Tafsir al-Tabari 34:9](tabari://34/9) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 34:9](ibnkathir://34/9) explain as dropping pieces of the celestial ceiling onto their heads. Treating the sky as a solid roof capable of fracturing into falling chunks reflects ancient Near Eastern firmament cosmology alongside [Quran 22:65](quran://22/65) and [Quran 52:44](quran://52/44) rather than a gaseous atmosphere.

34:11.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Commands King David in the tenth century BC to fashion full coats of mail (sabighat) and measure out the interlinking of iron rings (sard), with Qatadah in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 34:11](ibnkathir://34/11) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 34:11](tabari://34/11) asserting that David was the first in history to invent ring-linked chain mail in place of plate or scale armor. Archaeologically, Bronze and early Iron Age Levantine armor consisted of bronze or iron scales stitched onto backing, whereas interlinked chain mail first originated among Celtic smiths around the fourth to third century BC, nearly seven centuries after David.

34:12.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Subjects the wind to carry Solomon a month's journey in a single morning and evening, causes a spring of molten copper ('ayn al-qitr) to flow for him, and binds jinn laborers under his authority on pain of blazing punishment ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 34:12](ibnkathir://34/12), [Tafsir al-Tabari 34:12](tabari://34/12)). These supernatural motifs adapt late antique Jewish aggadic and pseudepigraphal demonology—attested in Targum Sheni, Babylonian Talmud Gittin 68a, and the Testament of Solomon—which are absent from the biblical record of Solomon's historical reign and temple works (see [Acts 7:47](bible://acts/7/47)).

34:13.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Portrays subjugated jinn constructing elevated sanctuaries (maharib), statues (tamathil), reservoir-sized basins, and immovable cauldrons at Solomon's command ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 34:13](ibnkathir://34/13), [Tafsir al-Tabari 34:13](tabari://34/13)). Whereas the Hebrew royal annals of Kings attribute Solomon's temple architecture and bronze basins to human craftsmen and labor levies ([Acts 7:47](bible://acts/7/47)), this passage canonizes post-biblical legends of demon artisans found in Babylonian Talmud Gittin 68a and the Testament of Solomon.

34:14.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Claims that when God decreed death for Solomon, his corpse remained standing propped upon his staff (minsa'atahu) while enslaved jinn continued hard labor unaware of his death until a wood-boring creature (dabbat al-ard) gnawed through the stick and he collapsed ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 34:14](ibnkathir://34/14), [Tafsir al-Tabari 34:14](tabari://34/14)). This episode incorporates post-biblical Midrashic folklore circulating in late antiquity rather than the biblical account of Solomon's earthly life and royal burial (see [Matthew 1:6](bible://mt/1/6) and [Nehemiah 13:26](bible://neh/13/26)).

34:23.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: In Muhammad's own exegesis of this verse preserved in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4701](/hadith/bukhari/4701) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 4800](/hadith/bukhari/4800) and cited in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 34:23](ibnkathir://34/23), eavesdropping devils stack one atop another up to the sky to overhear angelic decrees as angels tremble in heaven (see also [Tafsir al-Tabari 34:23](tabari://34/23)). According to that prophetic commentary, shooting-star flames pursue and burn the stacked jinn while they toss the overheard word downward to earthly soothsayers, misinterpreting atmospheric meteors as celestial projectiles (compare [Quran 37:6](quran://37/6)).

35:8.Theological Defect: Declares that God actively leads astray whomever He pleases (fa-inna Allaha yudillu man yasha'u) while evil deeds are made attractive to the sinner, and both [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 35:8](ibnkathir://35/8) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 35:8](tabari://35/8) affirm that no prophet can rescue those whom God has predestined to misguidance. Attributing moral delusion directly to divine causation undermines coherent human accountability and stands in sharp contrast to God's universal saving grace in [Titus 2:11](bible://ti/2/11).

35:18.Contradicts the Bible: Asserts categorically that no bearer of burdens can bear the sin-burden of another (wa-la taziru waziratun wizra ukhra), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 35:18](ibnkathir://35/18) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 35:18](tabari://35/18) interpret as an absolute exclusion of vicarious sin-bearing at final judgment. This directly denies the central biblical doctrine of substitutionary atonement foretold in [Isaiah 53:5](bible://is/53/5) and [Isaiah 53:6](bible://is/53/6) and fulfilled in Christ offering Himself to bear the sins of many in [Hebrews 9:28](bible://heb/9/28) and [Mark 10:45](bible://mk/10/45).

35:24.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Asserts unconditionally that there has never been a single community (ummah) in human history without a monotheistic warner (nadhir) having passed among them ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 35:24](ibnkathir://35/24), [Tafsir al-Tabari 35:24](tabari://35/24)). This universal historical claim is uncorroborated by the archaeological, epigraphic, and anthropological records of isolated civilizations across the pre-Columbian Americas, Oceania, and East Asia, and stands in internal tension with unwarned-ancestors passages such as [Quran 28:46](quran://28/46) and [Quran 36:6](quran://36/6).

35:31.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Declares that the Book inspired to Muhammad is truth confirming what was before it (musaddiqan lima bayna yadayhi), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 35:31](ibnkathir://35/31) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 35:31](tabari://35/31) identify as the previously revealed scriptures. Affirming the truthfulness of the extant Torah and Gospel alongside [Quran 3:3](quran://3/3) and [Quran 5:47](quran://5/47) reinforces the Islamic Dilemma, since seventh-century AD biblical manuscripts teach Christ's divine Sonship and redemptive death ([Matthew 26:28](bible://mt/26/28)).

36:6.Theological Defect: States that Muhammad was sent to warn a people whose forefathers were never warned (ma undhira aba'uhum, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 36:6](ibnkathir://36/6), [Tafsir al-Tabari 36:6](tabari://36/6)). Yet in [Sahih Muslim 203](/hadith/muslim/203), Muhammad informs a questioner that both the man's deceased father and Muhammad's own father 'Abdullah—who died during that unwarned pre-Islamic interval—are in Hellfire, colliding directly with the divine-justice principle in [Quran 17:15](quran://17/15) that God never punishes until He sends a messenger.

36:7.Theological Defect: Declares that the word of damnation has already proved mandatory against most of humanity so that they do not believe, which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 36:7](ibnkathir://36/7) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 36:7](tabari://36/7) explain as God's irrevocable prior decree fixing their disbelief and punishment. Condemning the majority of people through an antecedent decree that prevents faith conflicts with the biblical teaching that God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked but desires their repentance ([Ezekiel 18:23](bible://ez/18/23)).

36:8.Theological Defect: Portrays God Himself placing iron collars around unbelievers' necks up to their chins so their heads are forced aloft (inna ja'alna fi a'naqihim aghlalan), interpreted in [Tafsir al-Tabari 36:8](tabari://36/8) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 36:8](ibnkathir://36/8) as God actively restraining those doomed to wretchedness from accepting guidance. Depicting God as the active agent binding sinners away from truth undermines moral responsibility in contrast to [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13).

36:9.Theological Defect: States that God erected an obstructing barrier in front of unbelievers and behind them and covered their vision (fa-aghshaynahum) so they cannot see, which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 36:9](ibnkathir://36/9) glosses as God blinding their eyes to truth so moral guidance brings them no benefit (see also [Tafsir al-Tabari 36:9](tabari://36/9)). Making God the author of spiritual blindness against His own message inverts the biblical distinction between divine light and self-chosen resistance ([John 3:19](bible://jn/3/19)).

36:10.Theological Defect: Concludes that it is entirely the same to them whether Muhammad warns them or does not warn them because they will not believe, which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 36:10](ibnkathir://36/10) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 36:10](tabari://36/10) attribute to God having sealed their misguidance in advance. Rendering prophetic preaching futile by divine sealing empties the warning mission of redemptive purpose when measured against [Ezekiel 33:11](bible://ez/33/11).

36:38.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: States that the sun runs toward an appointed resting place (li-mustaqarrin laha); in [Sahih al-Bukhari 3199](/hadith/bukhari/3199), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4802](/hadith/bukhari/4802), and [Sahih Muslim 159a](/hadith/muslim/159a), Muhammad explains this verse at sunset by teaching that the sun travels nightly beneath God's Throne to prostrate and request permission to rise again. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 36:38](ibnkathir://36/38) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 36:38](tabari://36/38) transmit this prophetic explanation, with the former invoking a domed Throne ceiling over Earth against spherical astronomy.

36:40.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Asserts that the sun cannot overtake the moon nor can the night outrun the day, as each floats in an orbit (falak), likened in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 36:40](ibnkathir://36/40) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 36:40](tabari://36/40) to the revolving whorl of a spindle or celestial wheel. Grouping night and day alongside the sun and moon as bodies travelling along tracks presupposes a geocentric cosmos around a stationary Earth rather than terrestrial axial rotation causing day and night.

36:55.Devalues Women: Describes the male inhabitants of Paradise as 'busy rejoicing' (fi shughulin fakihun), which early exegetical authorities including Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Qatadah, al-Hasan, and al-Awza'i in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 36:55](ibnkathir://36/55) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 36:55](tabari://36/55) explicitly define as being preoccupied with 'deflowering virgins.' Framing heavenly bliss around perpetual male sexual consumption reduces female companions in Paradise to sensual instruments, contrasting sharply with Jesus's teaching on the resurrection in [Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30).

37:6.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Declares that God adorned the lowest heaven (al-sama' al-dunya) with the splendor of the stars (al-kawakib, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:6](ibnkathir://37/6), [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:6](tabari://37/6)). Placing all visible stars inside the nearest of seven stacked sky-ceilings—where [Quran 37:7](quran://37/7) and [Sahih Muslim 2229a](/hadith/muslim/2229a) assign them to guard the firmament with fiery projectiles—reflects pre-modern layered-dome cosmology rather than stars distributed across billions of light-years.

37:7.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Assigns the stars adorning the lowest heaven to serve as a physical guard (hifzan) against every rebellious devil ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:7](ibnkathir://37/7), [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:7](tabari://37/7)). Equating massive thermonuclear stars—vastly larger than Earth—with defensive sentry weapons protecting an overhead celestial border (compare [Quran 67:5](quran://67/5)) conflates astronomical stars with atmospheric meteors.

37:8.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Depicts devils attempting to eavesdrop physically on the angelic Exalted Assembly (al-mala' al-a'la) and being pelted from every side of the sky ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:8](ibnkathir://37/8), [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:8](tabari://37/8)). Muhammad elaborates this scene in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4701](/hadith/bukhari/4701) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 4800](/hadith/bukhari/4800) by portraying airborne jinn standing in a vertical chain up toward a spatial heaven located just above Earth's clouds.

37:9.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Explains meteor streaks as repelling bombardments (duhuran) that drive eavesdropping devils back from the threshold of the lowest sky ([Tafsir al-Tabari 37:9](tabari://37/9), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:9](ibnkathir://37/9)). In reality, shooting stars are millimetre-to-metre-scale interplanetary dust and rock fragments entering Earth's upper atmosphere on predictable orbital paths, having no connection to stars or demonic espionage.

37:10.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Asserts that any devil who snatches an overheard word from heaven is chased down by a piercing flame (shihab thaqib, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:10](ibnkathir://37/10), [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:10](tabari://37/10)). As reinforced by [Sahih Muslim 2229a](/hadith/muslim/2229a), this account attributes routine meteoric ablation some eighty to one hundred twenty kilometres above Earth's surface to targeted celestial missiles launched after fleeing jinn.

37:48.Devalues Women: Promises male believers in Paradise wide-eyed female companions who restrain their gazes exclusively to their husbands (qasirat al-tarf 'in, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:48](ibnkathir://37/48), [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:48](tabari://37/48)). Defining heavenly reward through compliant female consorts whose defining trait is visual and sexual devotion to men stands in stark contrast to the beatific communion with God described in [Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30).

37:49.Devalues Women: Compares the heavenly maidens awaiting men to hidden, untouched eggs (baydun maknun), which [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:49](tabari://37/49) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:49](ibnkathir://37/49) explain as pale, unblemished virgin bodies sheltered like the inner membrane of an egg never touched by hands. Objectifying female figures in Paradise in terms of skin coloration and intact physical delicacy reduces women's eschatological representation to male aesthetic gratification.

37:89.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Portrays Abraham glancing at the stars ([Quran 37:88](quran://37/88)) and declaring 'Surely I am sick' as a pretext to remain behind while his townsmen depart for an idol festival, an act classified among Abraham's three untruths in [Sahih al-Bukhari 3358](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3358), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:89](ibnkathir://37/89), and [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:89](tabari://37/89). This narrative prelude to smashing his community's idols derives from post-biblical Jewish aggadah (Genesis Rabbah 38:13) and has no counterpart in [Genesis 11:31](bible://gn/11/31).

37:93.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Depicts Abraham mocking his people's silent statues over food offerings and then striking the idols with his right hand ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:93](ibnkathir://37/93), [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:93](tabari://37/93); compare [Quran 21:58](quran://21/58)). This detailed story of young Abraham offering food to idols and shattering them reproduces fifth-century AD rabbinic Midrash in Genesis Rabbah 38:13 rather than any historical event in the canonical patriarchal narrative of [Genesis 12:1](bible://gn/12/1).

37:97.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Has Abraham's townsmen cry 'Build a structure for him and throw him into the blazing fire,' from which God delivers him unharmed ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:97](ibnkathir://37/97), [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:97](tabari://37/97); compare [Quran 21:68](quran://21/68)). The episode of Abraham being cast into a fiery furnace originated in Jewish midrashic exegesis (Genesis Rabbah 38:13; Targum Pseudo-Jonathan), which re-read the Sumerian city name 'Ur of the Chaldeans' in [Genesis 15:7](bible://gn/15/7) through the Hebrew noun ur ('fire/furnace').

37:101.Contradicts the Bible: Announces glad tidings to Abraham of an unnamed 'forbearing boy' (ghulamin halim) prior to the separate announcement of Isaac in [Quran 37:112](quran://37/112), generating deep exegetical division in which [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:101](tabari://37/101) identifies the sacrificial son as Isaac whereas [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:101](ibnkathir://37/101) argues for Ishmael and accuses Jews of altering their text. By omitting the son's name and prompting later substitution of Ishmael, the account diverges from [Genesis 22:2](bible://gn/22/2), which explicitly specifies Isaac, the covenant son promised through Sarah.

37:102.Contradicts the Bible: Portrays Abraham telling his unnamed son, 'Surely I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you; so look, what do you think?' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:102](ibnkathir://37/102), [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:102](tabari://37/102)). This departs substantially from [Genesis 22:2](bible://gn/22/2) and [Genesis 22:8](bible://gn/22/8), where God commands Abraham directly rather than through a sleep dream, names Isaac explicitly, and records Abraham withholding disclosure instead of polling his son's consent.

37:107.Contradicts the Bible: Concludes the sacrifice narrative ('We ransomed him with a great sacrifice') without ever identifying which son lay bound, leaving [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:107](tabari://37/107) defending Isaac while [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:107](ibnkathir://37/107) relocates the event to Mina near Mecca with Ishmael. Relocating the binding from Mount Moriah to Arabia and severing it from Isaac directly contradicts the geographic and covenantal record of [Genesis 22:2](bible://gn/22/2) and [Genesis 22:13](bible://gn/22/13).

37:152.Contradicts the Bible: Categorically brands the statement 'God has begotten' (walada Allahu) a lie ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 37:152](ibnkathir://37/152), [Tafsir al-Tabari 37:152](tabari://37/152)). Although spoken in a polemic against pagan claims regarding angels, its unqualified rejection of any divine begetting—using the same verb walada deployed in [Quran 112:3](quran://112/3)—flatly contradicts the biblical revelation of the eternally begotten Son of God in [Psalms 2:7](bible://ps/2/7) and [John 3:16](bible://jn/3/16).

38:22.Contradicts the Bible: Depicts two litigants physically climbing over the wall into King David's private prayer chamber (mihrab) and startling him ([Tafsir al-Tabari 38:22](tabari://38/22), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:22](ibnkathir://38/22), identifying the intruders in classical reports as disguised angels). This recasts the prophet Nathan's spoken judicial parable delivered in the Second Book of Samuel—memorialized in [Psalms 51:1](bible://ps/51/1)—into a literal break-in by two disputants while omitting Nathan altogether.

38:23.Contradicts the Bible: Presents one wall-climbing litigant accusing his brother of owning ninety-nine ewes while demanding his single ewe ([Tafsir al-Tabari 38:23](tabari://38/23), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:23](ibnkathir://38/23)). Whereas the biblical court history of Samuel delivers Nathan's ewe-lamb parable specifically to confront David's sin involving Bathsheba and Uriah the Hittite ([Psalms 51:1](bible://ps/51/1), [Matthew 1:6](bible://mt/1/6)), this retelling turns the parable into an actual courtroom dispute stripped of its historical context.

38:34.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: States that God tested Solomon and placed a body (jasad) upon his throne; [Tafsir al-Tabari 38:34](tabari://38/34) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:34](ibnkathir://38/34) explain this via the demon Sakhr stealing Solomon's signet ring, casting it into the sea to be swallowed by a fish, and usurping his throne—directly adapting the Ashmedai legend of Babylonian Talmud Gittin 68a–b—while [Sahih al-Bukhari 6639](/hadith/bukhari/6639) and [Sahih Muslim 1654e](/hadith/muslim/1654e) connect the jasad to a 'half-man' born after Solomon visited ninety wives in one night (contrast [Nehemiah 13:26](bible://neh/13/26)).

38:36.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Claims God answered Solomon's prayer by subjugating the wind to blow gently at his personal command wherever he directed ([Tafsir al-Tabari 38:36](tabari://38/36), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:36](ibnkathir://38/36)). Endowing King Solomon with magical mastery over atmospheric winds derives from post-biblical Jewish aggadic expansions such as Targum Sheni and has no basis in the biblical portrait of Solomon's historical wisdom and kingship ([Matthew 12:42](bible://mt/12/42)).

38:37.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Subjugates the demons (al-shayatin), 'every builder and diver,' to erect monumental structures and dive into the sea for pearls on Solomon's behalf ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:37](ibnkathir://38/37), [Tafsir al-Tabari 38:37](tabari://38/37)). This supernatural demon-workforce tradition incorporates late antique Jewish folklore from Babylonian Talmud Gittin 68a and the pseudepigraphal Testament of Solomon rather than the human temple builders attested in the Hebrew royal annals ([Acts 7:47](bible://acts/7/47)).
