38:38.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Describes rebellious devils bound together in iron fetters (muqarranina fi al-asfad) under Solomon's royal jurisdiction ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:38](ibnkathir://38/38), [Tafsir al-Tabari 38:38](tabari://38/38)). The motif of Solomon chaining recalcitrant demons in shackles closely follows late antique demon-binding folklore preserved in the Testament of Solomon and Babylonian Talmud Gittin 68a–b.

38:44.Theological Defect: Commands Job (Ayyub) to take a bundle (dighthan) of one hundred thin stalks and strike his wife once so as not to break his rash oath to lash her a hundred times ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:44](ibnkathir://38/44), [Tafsir al-Tabari 38:44](tabari://38/44)). Portraying God as devising a technical loophole to carry out a vowed beating against an innocent person contrasts sharply with biblical ethics, where rash or sinful oaths require confession rather than execution ([Leviticus 5:4](bible://lv/5/4); compare [Job 42:10](bible://jb/42/10)).
38:44.Devalues Women: Instructs Job to strike his devoted wife—who, according to [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:41](ibnkathir://38/41) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:44](ibnkathir://38/44), loyally nursed and supported him through eighteen years of severe illness—with a bundle of stalks to satisfy his angry vow (see also [Tafsir al-Tabari 38:44](tabari://38/44)). Issuing a divine command for a prophet to strike his blameless spouse normalizes husbandly physical discipline of wives alongside [Quran 4:34](quran://4/34), an episode completely absent from [Job 2:9](bible://jb/2/9).

38:52.Devalues Women: Promises pious men in the Gardens of Eden female companions of matching youth who restrain their glances solely to their spouses (qasirat al-tarf atrab, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:52](ibnkathir://38/52), [Tafsir al-Tabari 38:52](tabari://38/52)). Presenting age-matched, gaze-averting female consorts as a signature reward for men defines eternal salvation around male sexual possession rather than the non-marital resurrection state taught by Jesus in [Luke 20:35](bible://lk/20/35).

38:72.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Records God commanding all angels to fall down in prostration (fa-qa'u lahu sajidin) before newly formed Adam once divine spirit is breathed into him ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:72](ibnkathir://38/72), [Tafsir al-Tabari 38:72](tabari://38/72)). No such command exists in [Genesis 2:7](bible://gn/2/7); instead, the episode reproduces a well-known post-biblical apocryphal narrative preserved in the Life of Adam and Eve (13–14) and the pre-Islamic Syriac Cave of Treasures (2:12–24).

38:73.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: States that every angel prostrated together before Adam ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:73](ibnkathir://38/73), [Tafsir al-Tabari 38:73](tabari://38/73)). Collective angelic prostration to the first human directly echoes the apocryphal enthronement scene in the Life of Adam and Eve (14) and the Syriac Cave of Treasures (2:22–23), running counter to the biblical rule reserving prostrate veneration for God alone ([Revelation 19:10](bible://rv/19/10)).

38:74.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Singles out Iblis as the lone exception among the prostrating angels who grew arrogant and joined the disbelievers ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:74](ibnkathir://38/74), [Tafsir al-Tabari 38:74](tabari://38/74)). Tracing Satan's fall to his refusal to bow to Adam derives from the Life of Adam and Eve (14–16) and the Syriac Cave of Treasures (2:24–3:7), while excepting Iblis directly from 'the angels all together' creates internal classification tension with [Quran 18:50](quran://18/50), which calls him one of the jinn.

38:76.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Places on Iblis's lips the justification, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire, but You created him from clay' ([Tafsir al-Tabari 38:76](tabari://38/76), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 38:76](ibnkathir://38/76)). This specific contrast between fiery angelic or demonic substance and Adam's earthly clay closely parallels Satan's boast of elemental superiority over clay-formed Adam in the pre-Islamic Syriac Cave of Treasures (3:1–2).

39:4.Contradicts the Bible: Asserts that had God wished to take a son (waladan), He would simply have chosen whomever He pleased from among what He creates (mimma yakhluqu), a polemic that [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 39:4](ibnkathir://39/4) explicitly applies against Christian belief concerning Jesus (see also [Tafsir al-Tabari 39:4](tabari://39/4)). Framing divine Sonship as the arbitrary selection of a created being misconstrues and rejects the biblical teaching that the Son is the eternal, uncreated Word through whom all things were made ([John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1), [John 3:16](bible://jn/3/16), [Hebrews 1:2](bible://heb/1/2)).

39:6.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Claims God 'sent down' (anzala) eight mates of livestock—identified via [Quran 6:143](quran://6/143) in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 39:6](ibnkathir://39/6) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 39:6](tabari://39/6) as four domesticated Near Eastern species—and forms humans inside their mothers 'creation after creation, in three darknesses.' [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 39:6](ibnkathir://39/6) explains 'creation after creation' through the sequential stages of drop (nutfah), clinging blood-clot ('alaqah), and chewed lump (mudghah; compare [Quran 23:14](quran://23/14)) within belly, womb, and placenta, repeating ancient gross-anatomical guesswork including an erroneous blood-clot stage.

39:7.Contradicts the Bible: Declares unconditionally that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another (wa-la taziru waziratun wizra ukhra, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 39:7](ibnkathir://39/7), [Tafsir al-Tabari 39:7](tabari://39/7)). Repeating this categorical denial of vicarious atonement repudiates the heart of biblical redemption, in which the suffering Messiah bears the iniquities of sinners ([Isaiah 53:5](bible://is/53/5), [Isaiah 53:11](bible://is/53/11), [Hebrews 9:28](bible://heb/9/28)).

39:19.Theological Defect: Asks rhetorically whether Muhammad can rescue someone against whom God's decree of punishment has already proved mandatory (haqqa 'alayhi kalimatu al-'adhab), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 39:19](ibnkathir://39/19) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 39:19](tabari://39/19) interpret as people predestined by God to wretchedness whom no messenger can guide. Treating eternal damnation as locked in prior to prophetic appeal conflicts with God's genuine call for all people everywhere to repent in [Acts 17:30](bible://acts/17/30).

39:23.Theological Defect: States that God guides whomever He pleases, 'but whoever God leads astray has no guide' (wa-man yudlili Allahu fa-ma lahu min had, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 39:23](ibnkathir://39/23), [Tafsir al-Tabari 39:23](tabari://39/23)). Portraying God as the direct agent who leads human beings into irrecoverable error compromises divine moral perfection and contrasts with the biblical assurance that God's saving grace has appeared for all humanity ([Titus 2:11](bible://ti/2/11)).

39:29.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: Illustrates monotheism through a parable contrasting an owned slave shared among quarreling co-masters with a slave owned wholly by a single man ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 39:29](ibnkathir://39/29), [Tafsir al-Tabari 39:29](tabari://39/29)). Using chattel ownership of one human being by another as a self-evident moral analogy for divine lordship normalizes slavery as an enduring institution alongside [Quran 16:75](quran://16/75) and [Quran 30:28](quran://30/28).

40:10.Theological Defect: Announces to the damned in Hellfire that God's intense hatred (maqt) toward them during their earthly lives whenever invited to faith was even greater than their hatred of themselves in torment ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 40:10](ibnkathir://40/10), [Tafsir al-Tabari 40:10](tabari://40/10)). This characterization of divine hatred toward unbelievers while they are still being summoned to faith stands in direct antithesis to God's self-giving love for sinners while they were still enemies in [Romans 5:8](bible://rom/5/8).

40:24.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Groups Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun (Korah) together as a single Egyptian ruling front rejecting Moses's signs, with [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 40:24](ibnkathir://40/24) identifying Haman as Pharaoh's royal vizier (see also [Tafsir al-Tabari 40:24](tabari://40/24)). Conflating Korah—an Israelite Levite of the post-Exodus wilderness rebellion ([Numbers 16:1](bible://nm/16/1))—and Haman the Agagite—the fifth-century BC Persian court minister under King Ahasuerus/Xerxes I in [Esther 3:1](bible://est/3/1)—into Pharaoh's Bronze Age Egyptian court compresses figures separated by roughly a millennium.

40:25.Contradicts the Bible: Claims that after the adult Moses arrived before Pharaoh with divine signs (fa-lamma ja'ahum bi-l-haqqi), Pharaoh ordered, 'Kill the sons of those who have believed with him and spare their women,' compelling [Tafsir al-Tabari 40:25](tabari://40/25) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 40:25](ibnkathir://40/25) to posit a second infanticide decree during Moses's prophetic ministry. This conflicts directly with [Exodus 1:22](bible://ex/1/22) and [Exodus 5:6](bible://ex/5/6), where Pharaoh's decree to kill Hebrew newborn boys occurred eighty years earlier around Moses's birth while adult Moses's mission triggered harsher brick-making quotas instead.

40:31.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Places on the lips of a believing Egyptian nobleman inside Pharaoh's second-millennium BC royal council ([Tafsir al-Tabari 40:28](tabari://40/28), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 40:31](ibnkathir://40/31), [Tafsir al-Tabari 40:31](tabari://40/31)) a warning invoking the bygone destruction of the north-Arabian tribe of Thamud. Retrojecting seventh-century AD Hijazi preaching exempla into New Kingdom Egypt is historically anachronistic, as Thamud is unknown to Bronze Age Egyptian records and first appears in Neo-Assyrian annals of Sargon II around 715 BC.

40:35.Theological Defect: Declares that God sets a seal upon the heart (yatba'u Allahu 'ala kulli qalbi) of every arrogant tyrant, which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 40:35](ibnkathir://40/35) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 40:35](tabari://40/35) explain as God sealing their hearts against guidance so they can never subsequently recognize or follow truth. Portraying God as permanently locking human hearts against repentance conflicts with God's restorative invitation in [Ezekiel 18:32](bible://ez/18/32).

40:36.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Depicts Egypt's Pharaoh commanding 'Haman' to construct a lofty tower (sarhan), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 40:36](ibnkathir://40/36) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 40:36](tabari://40/36) link with baked-brick construction in [Quran 28:38](quran://28/38) while identifying Haman as Pharaoh's Egyptian chief minister and builder. This commits a major historical anachronism by transplanting Haman—the fifth-century BC Achaemenid Persian official of [Esther 3:1](bible://est/3/1)—nearly a thousand years backward into Bronze Age Egypt.

40:37.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Has Pharaoh declare that Haman's brick tower will enable him to reach 'the ropes of the heavens' (asbab al-samawat, glossed as heaven's physical gates or pathways in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 40:37](ibnkathir://40/37) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 40:37](tabari://40/37)) so as to peer up at the God of Moses. This narrative fuses the Mesopotamian baked-brick Tower of Babel account in [Genesis 11:3](bible://gn/11/3) and [Genesis 11:4](bible://gn/11/4) with the Egyptian Exodus and Persian-era [Esther 3:1](bible://est/3/1) while presupposing a low physical sky ceiling reachable by tall masonry.

40:64.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Describes God making the earth a fixed resting place (qararan, explained in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 40:64](ibnkathir://40/64) as spread out and stabilized so it does not move or shake) and the sky an overarching built structure (bina'an, glossed as a protective roof dome in [Tafsir al-Tabari 40:64](tabari://40/64) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 40:64](ibnkathir://40/64)). Paired with [Quran 2:22](quran://2/22), this architectural pairing reflects ancient Near Eastern flat-earth and solid-canopy cosmology.

40:67.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Traces human prenatal formation sequentially from dust, then from a drop of fluid (nutfah), and then from a clinging blood-clot ('alaqah) before emerging as an infant ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 40:67](ibnkathir://40/67), [Tafsir al-Tabari 40:67](tabari://40/67)). Like [Quran 23:14](quran://23/14), defining an obligatory stage of embryogenesis as congealed blood repeats pre-modern Galenic and Aristotelian misconceptions, since a living human embryo never develops from or passes through a clotted-blood stage.

41:9.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: States that Allah created the earth in two days, initiating a creation tally across [Quran 41:9](quran://41/9), [Quran 41:10](quran://41/10) (four days), and [Quran 41:12](quran://41/12) (two days) that sums to eight days rather than the six days asserted in [Quran 7:54](quran://7/54), [Quran 10:3](quran://10/3), and [Quran 50:38](quran://50/38). As [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 41:9](ibnkathir://41/9) and [Sahih Muslim 2789](/hadith/muslim/2789) confirm by comparing the earth to a building's foundation constructed prior to its roof, this sequence also places terrestrial formation before the cosmos and stars, inverting astrophysical history by roughly nine billion years.
41:9.Contradicts the Bible: Asserts that the earth was formed first over two days prior to the fashioning of the heavens ([Quran 41:11](quran://41/11), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 41:9](ibnkathir://41/9)) within an eight-day cumulative schedule ([Quran 41:9](quran://41/9), [Quran 41:10](quran://41/10), [Quran 41:12](quran://41/12)). This reverses the biblical creation order in [Genesis 1:1](bible://gn/1/1) through [Genesis 1:16](bible://gn/1/16) and conflicts with the six-day creation framework affirmed in [Exodus 20:11](bible://ex/20/11).

41:10.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Claims that Allah placed firm mountains on the earth and measured out its terrestrial sustenance in four days prior to turning toward the gaseous sky in [Quran 41:11](quran://41/11) and forming the stars in [Quran 41:12](quran://41/12). Classical exegesis in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 41:10](ibnkathir://41/10) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 41:10](tabari://41/10), corroborated by [Sahih Muslim 2789](/hadith/muslim/2789) (soil on Saturday, mountains on Sunday, trees on Monday, light on Wednesday), preserves a pre-scientific chronology in which earthly mountains and vegetation precede solar and stellar light.

41:11.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Depicts Allah turning (`thumma istawa`) to the sky while it was smoke (`dukhan`) only after the solid earth, its mountains, and its food provisions already existed ([Quran 41:9](quran://41/9), [Quran 41:10](quran://41/10)), as [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 41:11](ibnkathir://41/11) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 41:11](tabari://41/11) affirm in sequential architectural terms. In physical cosmology, primordial cosmic gas and generations of stars preceded the accretion of the rocky earth rather than coalescing into heavens above an already provisioned planet.

41:12.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Completes seven layered heavens in two additional days—bringing the explicit day counts of [Quran 41:9](quran://41/9), [Quran 41:10](quran://41/10), and [Quran 41:12](quran://41/12) to eight days against the six-day total in [Quran 7:54](quran://7/54)—and locates all stars as physical lamps (`masabih`) and missile-guards inside the lowest heaven ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 41:12](ibnkathir://41/12), [Quran 67:5](quran://67/5)). Modern astronomy demonstrates that stars reside across vast galactic distances rather than hanging inside an innermost atmospheric dome, and meteors are rocky solar-system debris rather than projectiles fired at eavesdropping spirits.
41:12.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Identifies the created lowest heaven (`al-sama' al-dunya`) into which, according to canonical traditions in [Sahih al-Bukhari 1145](/hadith/bukhari/1145) and [Sahih Muslim 758a](/hadith/muslim/758a), Allah Himself descends every night during its final third to address petitioners. Sunni creedal theology thus affirms that the transcendent Creator can enter a created cosmic realm without forfeiting His deity, undercutting standard philosophical objections against the Incarnation of the Word in [John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14).

42:8.Theological Defect: Declares that Allah could have united humanity as one guided community had He willed, yet—as [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 42:8](ibnkathir://42/8) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 42:8](tabari://42/8) explain—He deliberately guides whom He wills into mercy and misguides whom He wills toward the Fire without a helper. Making human unbelief the direct outcome of divine volition while punishing the unguided eternally introduces a severe tension in divine justice, contrasting with God's salvific will in [Ezekiel 33:11](bible://ez/33/11) and [John 3:16](bible://jn/3/16).

42:13.Contradicts the Bible: Asserts that Allah legislated for Muhammad the identical religion (`din`) enjoined upon Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 42:13](ibnkathir://42/13), [Tafsir al-Tabari 42:13](tabari://42/13)). Biblical revelation instead unfolds through progressive redemptive covenants centered on sacrificial blood atonement ([Exodus 24:8](bible://ex/24/8), [Leviticus 17:11](bible://lv/17/11)) and fulfilled in the divine Sonship, crucifixion, and resurrection of Jesus Christ ([Matthew 26:28](bible://mt/26/28), [Hebrews 1:1](bible://heb/1/1)).

42:15.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Commands Muhammad to proclaim, 'I believe in whatever Book God has sent down,' which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 42:15](ibnkathir://42/15) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 42:15](tabari://42/15) interpret as affirming every prior prophetic scripture revealed by God. By binding Muslims to accept the divine origin of the earlier Jewish and Christian scriptures ([Isaiah 40:8](bible://is/40/8), [Matthew 24:35](bible://mt/24/35)) without alleging textual loss, the verse reinforces the authority of the biblical canon that contradicts Quranic theology.

42:44.Theological Defect: States that whomever Allah actively leads astray (`man yudlili Allahu`) has no protector after Him and, as reiterated in [Quran 42:46](quran://42/46), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 42:44](ibnkathir://42/44), and [Tafsir al-Tabari 42:44](tabari://42/44), possesses no possible pathway to truth once God has decreed his misguidance. Holding creatures eternally culpable for an error sovereignly inflicted upon them by God Himself undermines coherent moral agency.

42:51.Contradicts the Bible: Asserts that it is not fitting for God to speak to any human being except by indirect inspiration, from behind a veil, or through an angelic emissary ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 42:51](ibnkathir://42/51), [Tafsir al-Tabari 42:51](tabari://42/51)). This categorical restriction contradicts the biblical record in which God appeared to Abraham ([Genesis 18:1](bible://gn/18/1)), spoke with Moses face to face as with a friend ([Exodus 33:11](bible://ex/33/11), [Numbers 12:8](bible://nm/12/8)), and spoke definitively in His incarnate Son ([Hebrews 1:2](bible://heb/1/2), [John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14)).

43:10.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Describes Allah making the earth a flat cradle or resting bed (`mahdan`), which [Tafsir al-Tabari 43:10](tabari://43/10) glosses as a flattened expanse and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 43:10](ibnkathir://43/10) explains as a stationary plane resting over water and held steady by mountains lest it shake. This reflects pre-modern flat-earth cosmology rather than a rotating spherical planet orbiting the sun.

43:18.Devalues Women: Characterizes the female sex (`man yunasha'u fi al-hilyati`) as one brought up amid ornaments who is unable to present a clear argument in dispute (`wa-huwa fi al-khisami ghayru mubin`). Both [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 43:18](ibnkathir://43/18) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 43:18](tabari://43/18) explicitly interpret this verse as declaring woman deficient outwardly and inwardly in intellect and expression, enshrining female cognitive inferiority within divine revelation (parallel to [Sahih al-Bukhari 304](/hadith/bukhari/304)).

43:36.Theological Defect: Declares that Allah actively appoints (`nuqayyid`) a devil (`shaytan`) to remain bound as an intimate companion (`qarin`) to anyone who turns from the remembrance of the Merciful ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 43:36](ibnkathir://43/36), [Tafsir al-Tabari 43:36](tabari://43/36); cf. [Sahih Muslim 2814a](/hadith/muslim/2814a)). Portraying God as commissioning demonic agents to deepen human spiritual blindness attributes active moral corruption to the Creator (contrast [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13)).

43:37.Theological Defect: States that the devils assigned by Allah in [Quran 43:36](quran://43/36) bar people from the path while causing them to suppose that they are rightly guided ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 43:37](ibnkathir://43/37), [Tafsir al-Tabari 43:37](tabari://43/37)). Under this framework, sincere conviction of divine guidance provides no epistemic assurance within Islamic theology, since God Himself assigns spirits that induce persuasive delusion prior to eternal punishment.

43:59.Contradicts the Bible: Asserts that Jesus was 'only a servant' (`in huwa illa 'abdun`) whom Allah blessed ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 43:59](ibnkathir://43/59), [Tafsir al-Tabari 43:59](tabari://43/59)), reducing Christ to purely creaturely status. While the New Testament affirms that the eternal Word voluntarily took the form of a servant in the Incarnation ([Philippians 2:6](bible://phil/2/6)), it explicitly proclaims His eternal divine nature and Sonship ([John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1), [Colossians 2:9](bible://col/2/9)).
43:59.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Concedes even within a polemical context that Allah uniquely favored Jesus and set Him forth as an extraordinary sign and model (`mathalan`) for the Sons of Israel—explained in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 43:59](ibnkathir://43/59) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 43:59](tabari://43/59) through His miraculous virgin birth and healing miracles ([Matthew 1:23](bible://mt/1/23), [Acts 2:22](bible://acts/2/22)).

43:61.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Declares that Jesus Himself is 'knowledge for the Hour' (or 'a sign for the Hour' in variant canonical readings), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 43:61](ibnkathir://43/61), [Tafsir al-Tabari 43:61](tabari://43/61), [Sahih al-Bukhari 2476](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2476), [Sahih al-Bukhari 3448](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3448), and [Sahih Muslim 155a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:155a) interpret as Christ's bodily descent from heaven prior to Resurrection Day as a just judge. By assigning cosmic eschatological return and judgment exclusively to the living Jesus while Muhammad remains buried, Islamic sources concede a uniquely divine prerogative attested in [Matthew 24:30](bible://mt/24/30) and [Acts 1:11](bible://acts/1/11).
43:61.Contradicts the Bible: Canonical exegesis of [Quran 43:61](quran://43/61) in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 43:61](ibnkathir://43/61), [Sahih al-Bukhari 2476](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2476), and [Sahih Muslim 155a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:155a) frames Jesus's second coming as an anti-Christian mission in which He breaks the cross, slaughters swine, and enforces Islamic law. This directly contradicts Jesus's own prophecies of His glorious return as the crucified and risen Son of Man ([Matthew 24:30](bible://mt/24/30), [Revelation 1:17](bible://rv/1/17)) and apostolic preaching of the cross ([Galatians 6:14](bible://gal/6/14), [Colossians 1:20](bible://col/1/20)).

43:64.Contradicts the Bible: Places on Jesus's lips an egalitarian disclaimer ('Surely God – He is my Lord and your Lord, so serve Him') that [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 43:64](ibnkathir://43/64) deploys to equate Christ's creaturely servitude with that of ordinary mortals. In the Gospels, by contrast, Jesus distinguishes His unique filial relationship to the Father from that of His disciples ([John 20:17](bible://jn/20/17)), claims equality of honor with the Father ([John 5:23](bible://jn/5/23), [John 10:30](bible://jn/10/30)), and receives worship as 'My Lord and my God!' ([John 20:28](bible://jn/20/28)).

43:81.Contradicts the Bible: Instructs Muhammad to declare, 'If the Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the ones who served'—a conditional statement that split classical commentators in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 43:81](ibnkathir://43/81) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 43:81](tabari://43/81) over whether it means worshiping such a son, serving God alone, or disdaining the claim (`anifan`). The argument presupposes that divine Sonship entails a contingent, newly acquired offspring (`walad`), misrepresenting the biblical doctrine of the eternally begotten Word ([John 1:18](bible://jn/1/18), [Hebrews 1:2](bible://heb/1/2)).

44:28.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: States that after Pharaoh and his army drowned, Allah caused 'another people' to inherit Egypt's gardens, springs, noble stations, and prosperity ([Quran 44:25](quran://44/25) through [Quran 44:28](quran://44/28)), whom [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 44:28](ibnkathir://44/28) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 44:28](tabari://44/28)—matching the explicit wording of [Quran 26:59](quran://26/59)—identify as the Children of Israel. Historically, the Israelites never returned to rule or inherit Pharaonic Egypt after the Exodus, and New Kingdom Egyptian administration continued uninterrupted under native dynasties.
44:28.Contradicts the Bible: Claims, as confirmed by [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 44:28](ibnkathir://44/28), [Tafsir al-Tabari 44:28](tabari://44/28), and [Quran 26:59](quran://26/59), that the departing Israelites inherited the gardens, springs, and estates left behind by Pharaoh's drowned elite in Egypt. In the Torah, Israel permanently departed Egypt into the Sinai wilderness for forty years before inheriting Canaan rather than Egypt ([Exodus 13:18](bible://ex/13/18), [Numbers 14:33](bible://nm/14/33), [Joshua 21:43](bible://jo/21/43)).

44:54.Devalues Women: Promises to wed righteous men in Paradise to wide-eyed virgin maidens (`hur 'in`), whom [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 44:54](ibnkathir://44/54) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 44:54](tabari://44/54) describe as fair, translucent females untouched by man or jinn and gifted alongside earthly wives for male sexual gratification. Framing eternal beatitude around passive female consorts created as rewards for men reduces femininity in the afterlife to an instrument of male pleasure.
44:54.Theological Defect: Depicts heavenly salvation in terms of sensual marriage to dark-eyed maidens (`hur 'in`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 44:54](ibnkathir://44/54), [Tafsir al-Tabari 44:54](tabari://44/54); cf. [Quran 52:20](quran://52/20), [Quran 55:56](quran://55/56)), projecting physical marital appetite into eternity in sharp contrast to Jesus's teaching that the resurrected neither marry nor are given in marriage ([Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30)).

45:16.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Affirms that Allah bestowed upon the Sons of Israel 'the Book, and the judgment, and the prophetic office'—which [Tafsir al-Tabari 45:16](tabari://45/16) explicitly defines as 'the Torah and the Gospel' along with authentic prophetic understanding ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 45:16](ibnkathir://45/16)). This concession validates the divine inspiration of the Jewish and Christian scriptures ([Romans 3:2](bible://rom/3/2), [Romans 9:4](bible://rom/9/4)), leaving Islam unable to dismiss the extant biblical text that refutes Quranic Christology.

45:23.Theological Defect: Asserts that Allah led the erring person astray 'on (the basis of) knowledge, and set a seal on his hearing and his heart, and made a covering on his sight,' concluding rhetorically, 'Who will guide him after God?' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 45:23](ibnkathir://45/23), [Tafsir al-Tabari 45:23](tabari://45/23)). Attributing the sealing of human faculties against repentance directly to God's own decree while demanding moral accountability ('Will you not take heed?') creates an acute deterministic tension.

46:9.Theological Defect: Commands Muhammad to declare, 'I do not know what will be done with me or with you,' a confession corroborated in [Sahih al-Bukhari 7018](/hadith/bukhari/7018), [Sahih al-Bukhari 7003](/hadith/bukhari/7003), and [Sahih al-Bukhari 3929](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3929) at the funeral of Uthman bin Maz'un where Muhammad swore that even as Allah's Messenger he did not know his own posthumous fate. Although commentators in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 46:9](ibnkathir://46/9) claim [Quran 48:2](quran://48/2) later abrogated this uncertainty, a salvific revelation whose founding prophet lacked assurance of his own eternal destiny leaves believers without grounded hope.
46:9.Contradicts the Bible: Records Muhammad disclaiming knowledge of his own eternal outcome and that of his followers ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 46:9](ibnkathir://46/9), [Tafsir al-Tabari 46:9](tabari://46/9), [Sahih al-Bukhari 7018](/hadith/bukhari/7018)). This contrasts directly with Jesus Christ, who authoritatively promised His followers eternal life that can never perish ([John 10:28](bible://jn/10/28), [John 14:2](bible://jn/14/2)) and inspired apostolic certainty of salvation ([John 5:24](bible://jn/5/24), [Romans 8:1](bible://rom/8/1)).

46:12.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Recognizes 'the Book of Moses as a model and mercy' and presents the Arabic Quran as 'a Book confirming (it)' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 46:12](ibnkathir://46/12), [Tafsir al-Tabari 46:12](tabari://46/12)). By appealing to the Torah then possessed by seventh-century Jews as an authoritative benchmark of divine truth ([Deuteronomy 31:24](bible://dt/31/24)), the verse establishes the Islamic Dilemma whenever the Quran contradicts Mosaic teaching.

46:29.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Narrates an episode in which Allah directed a band of invisible jinn at Nakhlah to crowd around Muhammad's prayer recitation and return as preachers after flaming meteors barred them from eavesdropping on heaven ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 46:29](ibnkathir://46/29), [Tafsir al-Tabari 46:29](tabari://46/29); cf. [Quran 72:1](quran://72/1)). The account incorporates pre-Islamic Arabian desert-jinn folklore and shooting-star divination lore directly into Quranic revelation.

46:30.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Portrays the believing jinn testifying to their people that they heard a scripture 'sent down after Moses, confirming what was before it' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 46:30](ibnkathir://46/30), [Tafsir al-Tabari 46:30](tabari://46/30)). Even while omitting any mention of Jesus's Gospel between Moses and Muhammad—an omission [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 46:30](ibnkathir://46/30) attempts to explain by treating the Injil as a mere supplement to Mosaic law—the text again concedes the intact authority of the Torah ([Luke 24:27](bible://lk/24/27)).

47:4.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Commands believers upon encountering disbelievers in battle to execute 'a striking of the necks' (`darba al-riqab`)—glossed in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 47:4](ibnkathir://47/4) as cutting them down completely with swords until wide slaughter subdues them—before binding survivors as war captives for release or ransom until war lays down its burdens ([Tafsir al-Tabari 47:4](tabari://47/4)). This codifies lethal battlefield decapitation and captive-taking as divinely ordained religious testing.
47:4.Contradicts the Bible: Mandates striking the necks of unbelievers in religious warfare and promises Paradise to fighters slain in combat ([Quran 47:4](quran://47/4) through [Quran 47:6](quran://47/6), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 47:4](ibnkathir://47/4)). This inverts the New Testament ethic of martyrdom and spiritual warfare, where Jesus rebuked violent sword-wielding ([Matthew 26:52](bible://mt/26/52), [John 18:36](bible://jn/18/36)) and commanded love for enemies ([Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44)).

47:12.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Contrasts believers entering heavenly Gardens with disbelievers who 'take their enjoyment and eat as the cattle eat' (`ka-ma ta'kulu al-an'am`) while awaiting the Fire—a comparison [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 47:12](ibnkathir://47/12) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 47:12](tabari://47/12) reinforce as animalistic gluttony devoid of higher reflection. Equating non-Muslims with grazing livestock fosters religious contempt toward outsiders (contrast [Genesis 1:26](bible://gn/1/26), [James 3:9](bible://jas/3/9)).

47:19.Theological Defect: Commands Muhammad directly, 'Ask forgiveness for your sin (`li-dhanbika`), and for the believing men and the believing women'—supported in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 47:19](ibnkathir://47/19) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 47:19](tabari://47/19) by canonical prophetic prayers confessing Muhammad's past, future, secret, unintentional, and deliberate errors (cf. [Sahih al-Bukhari 6398](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6398)). This explicit divine command refutes the later Islamic doctrine of absolute prophetic sinlessness (`'ismah`) and contrasts with the sinless Mediator attested in [Hebrews 4:15](bible://heb/4/15) and [Hebrews 7:26](bible://heb/7/26).

47:20.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Rebukes believers who recoil in fear when a decisive surah prescribing fighting (`qital`) is sent down, diagnosing reluctance to wage lethal jihad as 'a sickness' in their hearts and pronouncing 'Woe to them!' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 47:20](ibnkathir://47/20), [Tafsir al-Tabari 47:20](tabari://47/20)). Treating moral or personal hesitation toward bloodshed as spiritual pathology coerces believers into military combat.

47:35.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Prohibits Muslims from growing weak and calling for peace (`al-salm`) when they hold military superiority (`wa-antumu al-a'lawna`). As [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 47:35](ibnkathir://47/35) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 47:35](tabari://47/35) explicitly explain, this verse forbids ending warfare through peace treaties whenever Muslims outnumber and overpower non-Muslims, permitting truces like Hudaybiyyah solely as temporary tactical measures during Muslim weakness (contrast [Matthew 5:9](bible://mt/5/9), [Romans 12:18](bible://rom/12/18)).

48:1.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Reframes the AD 628 Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah—where Quraysh blocked Muhammad's promised pilgrimage into Mecca, provoking sharp dismay among companions such as Umar ibn al-Khattab ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:1](ibnkathir://48/1), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:27](ibnkathir://48/27))—as a divinely bestowed 'clear victory' (`fathan mubinan`, [Tafsir al-Tabari 48:1](tabari://48/1)), shielding Muhammad's political concession from internal dissent.

48:2.Theological Defect: States that victory was granted 'so that God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is (still) to come' (`ma taqaddama min dhanbika wa-ma ta'akhkhara`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:2](ibnkathir://48/2), [Tafsir al-Tabari 48:2](tabari://48/2)). This confirms that Muhammad committed both earlier and subsequent sins—unlike Jesus, whom [Hebrews 4:15](bible://heb/4/15), [John 8:46](bible://jn/8/46), and even [Sahih Muslim 194a](/hadith/muslim/194a) record without any sin (`dhanb`)—while raising ethical questions over pre-forgiving future transgressions.
48:2.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Confers upon Muhammad an exclusive divine amnesty forgiving all past and future sins in advance—an unprecedented privilege that [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:2](ibnkathir://48/2) explicitly highlights as shared by no other human being in authentic Islamic tradition.

48:10.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Declares that companions swearing military allegiance not to flee in battle for Muhammad at Hudaybiyyah are in fact swearing allegiance to God Himself, with 'the hand of God' over their hands ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:10](ibnkathir://48/10), [Tafsir al-Tabari 48:10](tabari://48/10); cf. [Quran 4:80](quran://4/80)). Equating political and martial fealty to Muhammad directly with a divine covenant renders any dissent from his leadership treason against God.

48:16.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Commands Bedouin Arabs who stayed behind to march against 'a people of harsh violence'—identified across [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:16](ibnkathir://48/16) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 48:16](tabari://48/16) as rival Arab tribes or the Persian and Byzantine empires—under the ultimatum 'You will fight them or they will surrender (`aw yuslimun`),' threatening painful divine torment for refusing offensive conscription.

48:19.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Rewards those who pledged allegiance to Muhammad under the tree in [Quran 48:18](quran://48/18) with 'many spoils to take,' which [Tafsir al-Tabari 48:19](tabari://48/19) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:20](ibnkathir://48/20) specify as the rich wealth of the Jewish settlement of Khaybar reserved exclusively for Hudaybiyyah participants.
48:19.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Presents the seizure of 'many spoils' (`maghanim kathirah`) from conquered non-Muslim communities—fulfilled shortly afterward in the AD 628 assault on Jewish Khaybar ([Tafsir al-Tabari 48:19](tabari://48/19))—as a direct manifestation of divine might, wisdom, and spiritual reward.

48:20.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Celebrates Allah hastening abundant war plunder (`maghanim kathirah`) for believers—identified in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:20](ibnkathir://48/20) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 48:20](tabari://48/20) with the conquest of Khaybar—as 'a sign to the believers' that guides them on a straight path, sanctifying offensive raiding and expropriation as divine guidance.
48:20.Sanctions Slavery & Concubinage: Refers to the hastened war spoils of Khaybar ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:20](ibnkathir://48/20)), where—as documented in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4200](/hadith/bukhari/4200) and [Sahih al-Bukhari 947](/hadith/bukhari/947)—Muslim forces slew the settlement's fighting men, enslaved its women and children as war booty, and distributed captives including Safiyya bint Huyayy.

48:21.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Promises believers 'other (spoils) which you were not able (to take)' that Allah has already encompassed for them—interpreted across [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:21](ibnkathir://48/21) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 48:21](tabari://48/21) as subsequent conquests of Mecca, Persia, and Byzantium until Resurrection Day, institutionalizing open-ended imperial plunder.

48:27.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Defends Muhammad after his pre-Hudaybiyyah dream of entering Mecca's Sacred Mosque failed to materialize in AD 628—prompting Umar ibn al-Khattab in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:27](ibnkathir://48/27) to ask, 'Haven't you told us that we will go to the House and perform Tawaf around it?'—by qualifying the vision with 'if God pleases' (`in sha'a Allahu`, [Tafsir al-Tabari 48:27](tabari://48/27)) and redirecting expectations toward a near military victory.

48:28.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Declares that Allah sent Muhammad with Islam 'so that He may cause it to prevail over religion – all of it' (repeated verbatim in [Quran 9:33](quran://9/33) and [Quran 61:9](quran://61/9)), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:28](ibnkathir://48/28) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 48:28](tabari://48/28) interpret as subjugating all Arabs and non-Arabs and invalidating every rival faith across the earth.

48:29.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Praises Muhammad's companions for being 'harsh against the disbelievers, (but) compassionate among themselves' (`ashidda'u 'ala al-kuffar ruhama'u baynahum`), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:29](ibnkathir://48/29) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 48:29](tabari://48/29) explain as maintaining sternness, anger, and minimal mercy toward non-Muslims while reserving warmth strictly for fellow Muslims (contrast [Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44), [Galatians 6:10](bible://gal/6/10)).
48:29.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Claims that the portrait of Muhammad's followers in 'the Gospel' (`al-Injil`) is 'like a seed (that) puts forth its shoot, and strengthens it, and it becomes stout and stands straight on its stalk, pleasing the sowers' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 48:29](ibnkathir://48/29), [Tafsir al-Tabari 48:29](tabari://48/29)). This borrows Jesus's parable of the growing seed from [Mark 4:26](bible://mk/4/26) through [Mark 4:29](bible://mk/4/29) while inverting its peaceful Kingdom meaning into a prophecy of militant Muslim expansion designed 'to enrage the disbelievers.'

49:1.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Commands believers not to 'be forward before God and His messenger' (`la tuqaddimu bayna yadayi Allahi wa-rasulihi`), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 49:1](ibnkathir://49/1) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 49:1](tabari://49/1) interpret as forbidding any independent decision, opinion, or speech prior to Muhammad's directive, pairing his personal authority directly alongside God's.

49:2.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Forbids believers from raising their voices above Muhammad's voice or addressing him aloud as peers—revealed after Abu Bakr and Umar argued audibly in his presence ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 49:2](ibnkathir://49/2), [Tafsir al-Tabari 49:2](tabari://49/2), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4845](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4845))—under threat that a breach of vocal decorum around Muhammad will erase a lifetime of righteous deeds.
49:2.Theological Defect: Warns that merely speaking louder than Muhammad can cause all of a believer's righteous works to 'come to nothing without your realizing (it)' (`an tahbata a'malukum wa-antum la tash'urun`, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 49:2](ibnkathir://49/2), [Tafsir al-Tabari 49:2](tabari://49/2)). Making eternal moral standing hinge on unwitting acoustic volume before a human leader rather than inward holiness or divine grace distorts proportional justice.

49:4.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Rebukes visitors who called out to Muhammad from outside his wives' private rooms (`al-hujurat`) by declaring in timeless scripture that 'most of them do not understand' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 49:4](ibnkathir://49/4), [Tafsir al-Tabari 49:4](tabari://49/4)), deploying divine revelation to police domestic etiquette around Muhammad's living quarters.

49:15.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Defines authentic believers exclusively (`innama al-mu'minuna`) as those who have not doubted and have 'struggled with their wealth and their lives in the way of God'—explicitly glossed in [Tafsir al-Tabari 49:15](tabari://49/15) as waging jihad against polytheists so that Allah's word becomes uppermost ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 49:15](ibnkathir://49/15)), making martial combat a criterion of genuine faith.

50:6.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Challenges skeptics to inspect the sky above them—'how We have built it, and adorned it, and it has no cracks (`furuj`)'—which [Tafsir al-Tabari 50:6](tabari://50/6) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 50:6](ibnkathir://50/6) explain as a solid, protected overhead roof adorned with star-lamps and devoid of physical rifts or detached segments. This presupposes an ancient Near Eastern solid firmament rather than a boundless vacuum of space.

50:7.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Depicts the earth as 'stretched out' (`madadnaha`) with 'firm mountains' cast onto it—explained in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 50:7](ibnkathir://50/7) as heavy anchors placed atop a flat earth settled over surrounding water to keep it from shaking ([Tafsir al-Tabari 50:7](tabari://50/7)). Geophysics establishes that mountains are not stabilizing weights dropped onto a watery disc, but folded crust formed along tectonic plate boundaries where earthquakes concentrate.

50:30.Theological Defect: Portrays Gehenna asking on Judgment Day, 'Are there any more (to come)?'—which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 50:30](ibnkathir://50/30), [Tafsir al-Tabari 50:30](tabari://50/30), [Sahih al-Bukhari 6661](/hadith/bukhari/6661), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4850](/hadith/bukhari/4850), and [Sahih Muslim 2848a](/hadith/muslim/2848a) explain as remaining unfilled until Allah places His own physical foot or leg (`qadamahu` / `rijlahu`) directly inside Hellfire so its walls constrict and cry 'Enough!' This stark corporeal anthropomorphism simultaneously undermines Islamic polemics claiming a transcendent God cannot enter created space.

50:38.Contradicts the Bible: Adds after mentioning six-day creation that 'No weariness touched Us' (`wa-ma massana min lughub`), which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 50:38](ibnkathir://50/38) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 50:38](tabari://50/38) record as a polemical rebuttal accusing Jews of teaching that God rested from physical fatigue on the seventh day. This misreads Hebrew `shabbat` (cessation from creative work) in [Genesis 2:2](bible://gn/2/2) as bodily exhaustion, overlooking that the Hebrew Bible itself explicitly proclaims the Creator 'does not faint or grow weary' ([Isaiah 40:28](bible://is/40/28)).

51:47.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: States concerning the sky, 'We built it with (Our own) hands, and surely We were (its) extenders indeed' (`wa-inna la-musi'un`). Contrary to modern claims reading Edwin Hubble's expanding universe into this verse, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 51:47](ibnkathir://51/47) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 51:47](tabari://51/47) define it within ancient dome cosmology as Allah having raised the sky as a vast, high solid roof hanging independently without supporting pillars.

51:48.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Declares, 'And the earth – We spread it out (`farashnaha`). Excellent were the smoothers (`al-mahidun`)!'—glossed in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 51:48](ibnkathir://51/48) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 51:48](tabari://51/48) as spreading the earth flat like a resting mattress (`firash`) beneath the solid roof of [Quran 51:47](quran://51/47), reflecting pre-scientific flat-earth geography.

51:49.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Asserts universally, 'And We created pairs (`zawjayn`) of everything, so that you might take heed,' which [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 51:49](ibnkathir://51/49) and Ibn Zayd in [Tafsir al-Tabari 51:49](tabari://51/49) apply across living creatures as male and female counterparts (cf. [Quran 36:36](quran://36/36)). In biology, vast domains of life—including bacteria, archaea, numerous fungi and plants, and parthenogenetic vertebrates such as whiptail lizards—reproduce asexually without male-female pairing.

52:20.Devalues Women: Promises believers reclining on lined couches that Allah will wed them to wide-eyed maidens (`hur 'in`), whom [Tafsir al-Tabari 52:20](tabari://52/20) explicitly specifies as female spouses awarded exclusively to 'the males among these pious ones' and whom [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 52:20](ibnkathir://52/20) depicts awaiting male sexual attention for decades at a time. Structuring eternal reward around passive female consorts subordinated to male desire devalues women's spiritual equality.
52:20.Theological Defect: Portrays heavenly bliss through luxurious banquet couches and marriage to dark-eyed houris ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 52:20](ibnkathir://52/20), [Tafsir al-Tabari 52:20](tabari://52/20); cf. [Quran 44:54](quran://44/54)), offering a thoroughly carnal vision of Paradise at odds with the beatific, non-marital resurrection life taught by Jesus in [Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30).

52:24.Theological Defect: Promises that immortal servant youths 'of their own, as if they were hidden pearls' (`ghilmanun lahum ka-annahum lu'lu'un maknun`) will circulate among Paradise's inhabitants bearing the wine cups of [Quran 52:23](quran://52/23) ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 52:24](ibnkathir://52/24), [Tafsir al-Tabari 52:24](tabari://52/24); cf. [Quran 56:17](quran://56/17)). Modeling eternal salvation after late-antique aristocratic wine banquets attended by permanently servile, pearl-white boys projects earthly class hierarchy and sensual luxury into heaven.

53:19.Theological Defect: Introduces the Meccan pagan goddesses al-Lat and al-'Uzza ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 53:19](ibnkathir://53/19), [Tafsir al-Tabari 53:20](tabari://53/20)) at the exact juncture where early Islamic historians and [Tafsir al-Tabari 22:52](tabari://22/52)—transmitting reports from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Muhammad ibn Qays, and Ibn Ishaq—record that Satan cast the *Gharaniq* ('Satanic Verses') praising pagan intercession onto Muhammad's tongue during public recitation. A prophetic channel susceptible to satanic verbal intrusion during scripture delivery undermines confidence in revelatory preservation.

53:20.Theological Defect: Names 'Manat, the third, the other,' completing the triad after which [Tafsir al-Tabari 22:52](tabari://22/52) reports Muhammad recited Satan's interpolated praise ('Those are the high Gharaniq, and indeed their intercession is to be hoped for'), prompting both Muslims and Quraysh polytheists to prostrate together at the close of the surah (corroborated by the joint idolater-Muslim prostration in [Sahih al-Bukhari 4862](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4862) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 53:1](ibnkathir://53/1)).

53:22.Devalues Women: Declares attributing female offspring to Allah while men retain males to be 'an unfair division!' (`qismatun diza`), which [Tafsir al-Tabari 53:22](tabari://53/22) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 53:23](tabari://53/23) explicitly define as 'an unjust, unequal division, deficient and incomplete' because daughters are the inferior share men dislike ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 53:22](ibnkathir://53/22)).

53:23.Theological Defect: Repudiates al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat as mere humanly coined names devoid of divine authority ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 53:23](ibnkathir://53/23))—a corrective passage that early exegetical tradition in [Tafsir al-Tabari 22:52](tabari://22/52) situates after Gabriel informed a grieving Muhammad that he had spoken words Allah never revealed, necessitating divine cancellation (`naskh`) of Satan's interpolation.

53:38.Contradicts the Bible: Claims—while purporting in [Quran 53:36](quran://53/36) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 53:38](tabari://53/38) to summarize 'what is in the scriptures of Moses'—'that no one bearing a burden bears the burden of another,' a principle [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 53:38](ibnkathir://53/38) deploys to rule out vicarious sin-bearing altogether. This misrepresents the Mosaic Torah itself, where sacrificial victims and the Day of Atonement scapegoat bore Israel's iniquities ([Leviticus 16:21](bible://lv/16/21)), foreshadowing the Messiah bearing humanity's sins in [Isaiah 53:6](bible://is/53/6), [Hebrews 9:28](bible://heb/9/28), and [John 1:29](bible://jn/1/29).

53:39.Contradicts the Bible: Asserts 'that a person will receive only what he (himself) strives for' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 53:39](ibnkathir://53/39))—teaching strictly works-merited salvation that contradicts biblical justification by grace through faith apart from human merit ([Ephesians 2:8](bible://eph/2/8), [Romans 3:28](bible://rom/3/28)), while even clashing internally with [Quran 52:21](quran://52/21), which Ibn Abbas in [Tafsir al-Tabari 53:39](tabari://53/39) cited as abrogating this verse.

53:46.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: States across [Quran 53:45](quran://53/45) and [Quran 53:46](quran://53/46) that Allah created male and female 'from a drop, when it is emitted' (`min nutfatin idha tumna`), which [Tafsir al-Tabari 53:46](tabari://53/46) explains via ancient two-seed fluid theory as 'a drop, when the man and the woman emit it' ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 53:46](ibnkathir://53/46)). Human reproduction requires fertilization of a non-emitted female ovum rather than emitted female sexual fluid, and fixing sex at the emitted-drop stage also conflicts with [Quran 75:37](quran://75/37) through [Quran 75:39](quran://75/39), where sex is fashioned stages later after the clinging clot (`'alaqah`).

54:1.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Classical exegesis and canonical hadith unanimously interpret this verse as a literal physical splitting of the moon into two distinct halves during Muhammad's Meccan ministry ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 54:1](ibnkathir://54/1), [Tafsir al-Tabari 54:1](tabari://54/1), [Sahih al-Bukhari 3636](/hadith/bukhari/3636), [Sahih al-Bukhari 3868](/hadith/bukhari/3868), [Sahih Muslim 2800b](/hadith/muslim/2800b)). No contemporary 7th-century AD astronomical chronicle or historical record across the Byzantine, Persian, Indian, or Chinese worlds viewing the same lunar hemisphere documents such a cataclysm, and Meccan passages elsewhere state that Allah refrained from sending requested sensory miracles ([Quran 17:59](quran://17/59), [Quran 13:7](quran://13/7)).

55:22.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Referring to the meeting of the sweet freshwater sea and the salty marine sea ([Quran 55:19](quran://55/19), [Quran 25:53](quran://25/53)), this verse asserts that pearls and coral (*al-marjan*) emerge "from both of them" (*minhuma*), even though precious coral is strictly marine and does not inhabit freshwater bodies. In [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:22](ibnkathir://55/22), the commentator explicitly concedes alongside [Quran 35:12](quran://35/12) that wearable sea ornaments come "only from the salty, not the fresh," forcing exegetes to reinterpret the dual pronoun as applying to only one sea while citing reports that raindrops falling into oysters turn into pearls ([Tafsir al-Tabari 55:22](tabari://55/22)).

55:56.Devalues Women: Rewards male inhabitants of Paradise with female consorts "restraining their glances" (*qasirat al-tarf*) whose highlighted virtue is that neither human nor jinn has previously deflowered them ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:56](ibnkathir://55/56), [Tafsir al-Tabari 55:56](tabari://55/56)). Framing female perfection in eternity around exclusive sexual subordination and intact physical virginity reduces women in the afterlife to passive rewards reserved for male gratification.
55:56.Theological Defect: Centers eternal beatitude on sexual deflowering—even specifying that no jinn has had prior sexual intercourse with Paradise's maidens ([Tafsir al-Tabari 55:56](tabari://55/56), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:56](ibnkathir://55/56))—projecting earthly carnal appetites onto the world to come. This stands in sharp contrast to Jesus's teaching that the resurrected neither marry nor engage in marital relations, living instead like the angels before God ([Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30)).

55:58.Devalues Women: Compares the virgin consorts of [Quran 55:56](quran://55/56) to ornamental gemstones ("ruby and coral"), an image elaborated in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:58](ibnkathir://55/58), [Tafsir al-Tabari 55:58](tabari://55/58), and [Sahih al-Bukhari 3254](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3254) as women so physically translucent that the marrow of their shins is visible through their flesh and garments. Such descriptions objectify female bodies as decorative luxuries crafted for the visual and physical enjoyment of men.

55:70.Devalues Women: Catalogs "good and beautiful" females (*khayratun hisan*) among the amenities of the lower gardens of Paradise immediately alongside gushing springs, fruits, date-palms, and pomegranates ([Quran 55:66](quran://55/66), [Quran 55:68](quran://55/68), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:70](ibnkathir://55/70), [Tafsir al-Tabari 55:70](tabari://55/70)). Treating female attractiveness as an item of celestial estate awarded to male believers subordinates women's eternal personhood to male reward.

55:72.Devalues Women: Depicts Paradise's wide-eyed *hur* as "confined in tents" (*maqsuratun fi al-khiyam*), glossed in [Tafsir al-Tabari 55:72](tabari://55/72) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:72](ibnkathir://55/72) as women restrained inside pavilions rather than roaming freely. Extending strict domestic seclusion into Paradise itself treats female immobilization and isolation for a husband's exclusive access as an eternal ideal.
55:72.Theological Defect: Canonical hadith and classical commentary explain these pavilions as hollowed pearls sixty miles high housing secluded wives in separate corners whom the male believer visits in rotation out of sight of one another ([Sahih Muslim 2838a](/hadith/muslim/2838a), [Sahih Muslim 2838b](/hadith/muslim/2838b), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:72](ibnkathir://55/72)). Envisioning heaven around vast polygamous harems diverges fundamentally from the biblical New Jerusalem centered on direct, holy communion with God ([Revelation 21:3](bible://rv/21/3), [Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30)).

55:74.Devalues Women: Reiterates that the tent-secluded maidens of [Quran 55:72](quran://55/72) have never been touched (*lam yatmithhunna*) by man or jinn, with *tamth* explicitly defined in [Tafsir al-Tabari 55:74](tabari://55/74) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:74](ibnkathir://55/74) as sexual intercourse causing hymenal bleeding. Repeating physical deflowering across [Quran 55:56](quran://55/56) and [Quran 55:74](quran://55/74) as a primary heavenly blessing defines female value through male sexual possession.

56:17.Theological Defect: Populates Paradise with "immortalized boys" (*wildanun mukhalladun*)—described in [Tafsir al-Tabari 56:17](tabari://56/17) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 56:17](ibnkathir://56/17) as perpetually juvenile attendants adorned with earrings and bracelets who never age—created to circulate as servants for reclining banqueters. Modeling eternal life on aristocratic court servitude diverges from Christ's Kingdom, where greatness is defined by humble service rather than lording status over permanent attendants ([Mark 10:43](bible://mk/10/43), [Mark 10:45](bible://mk/10/45)).

56:22.Devalues Women: Introduces wide-eyed *hur 'in* immediately after circulated wine, fruit, and fowl meat ([Quran 56:18](quran://56/18), [Quran 56:20](quran://56/20), [Quran 56:21](quran://56/21)), with several canonical readers cited in [Tafsir al-Tabari 56:22](tabari://56/22) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 56:22](ibnkathir://56/22) placing them in the same grammatical case as the banquet provisions bestowed on male believers. Grouping specially formed female consorts alongside food and drink portrays women in Paradise as consumable luxuries.
56:22.Theological Defect: Promises wide-eyed female consorts (*hur 'in*) as an essential component of eternal reward for the foremost believers ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 56:22](ibnkathir://56/22), [Tafsir al-Tabari 56:22](tabari://56/22); [Sahih Muslim 2834a](/hadith/muslim/2834a)). Offering physical harems as an incentive for piety stands in direct opposition to Jesus's declaration that resurrection life transcends marriage and sexual union ([Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30)).

56:23.Devalues Women: Likens the wide-eyed consorts of [Quran 56:22](quran://56/22) to "hidden pearls" (*al-lu'lu'i al-maknun*), explained in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 56:23](ibnkathir://56/23) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 56:23](tabari://56/23) as lustrous pearls preserved untouched inside closed shells until opened by their possessors. Equating female worth with unblemished, concealed objects awaiting male ownership reinforces a possessive and ornamental view of women.

56:35.Devalues Women: States that Allah specially fashioned or re-created Paradise's women (*ansha'nahunna insha'an*) in connection with elevated beds ([Quran 56:34](quran://56/34)), interpreted in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 56:35](ibnkathir://56/35) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 56:35](tabari://56/35) as refashioning elderly, bleary-eyed earthly women alongside *hur* solely to make them desirable consorts for their husbands. Women's resurrection is thus framed around reconstructing their physical appeal for men rather than their own beatific union with God.
56:35.Theological Defect: Describes a special eschatological creation of female consorts designed for marital beds in Paradise ([Quran 56:34](quran://56/34), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 56:35](ibnkathir://56/35), [Tafsir al-Tabari 56:35](tabari://56/35)). Re-engineering resurrected bodies specifically for ongoing sexual intercourse contradicts Christ's teaching that children of the resurrection do not enter marital unions ([Luke 20:35](bible://lk/20/35), [Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30)).

56:36.Devalues Women: Specifies that Allah transformed the resurrected women and *hur* of [Quran 56:35](quran://56/35) into perpetual virgins (*abkaran*), with [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 56:36](ibnkathir://56/36) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 56:36](tabari://56/36) citing traditions that elderly non-virgin women are remade as maidens whose virginity is continually restored for their husbands. Defining women's glorified state by perpetual hymenal restoration reduces female eschatological destiny to male sexual preference.
56:36.Theological Defect: Makes physical re-virginization (*abkaran*) a divine priority of the resurrection order ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 56:36](ibnkathir://56/36), [Tafsir al-Tabari 56:36](tabari://56/36)). Projecting repetitive deflowering onto eternal life stands at odds with the glorified transformation of the resurrection body taught in the New Testament ([Luke 20:36](bible://lk/20/36), [Philippians 3:21](bible://phil/3/21)).

56:37.Devalues Women: Describes these remade virgin wives ([Quran 56:36](quran://56/36)) as *'uruban atraban*—coquettish, passionately infatuated with their husbands, and fixed at uniform youth—with Ibn 'Abbas in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 56:37](ibnkathir://56/37) comparing an *'arub* wife's passion for her husband to "a she-camel in heat" (also [Tafsir al-Tabari 56:37](tabari://56/37)). Programming women's eternal affections and age around gratifying male desire strips female personhood of independent spiritual purpose.

56:38.Devalues Women: Designates the newly produced, amorous virgins of [Quran 56:35](quran://56/35), [Quran 56:36](quran://56/36), and [Quran 56:37](quran://56/37) collectively "for the companions on the right" (*li-ashab al-yamin*, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 56:38](ibnkathir://56/38), [Tafsir al-Tabari 56:38](tabari://56/38)). Addressing salvation's rewards exclusively to male recipients receiving female consorts, without any symmetrical promise addressing women as autonomous heirs, entrenches male-centered hierarchy in eternity ([Galatians 3:28](bible://gal/3/28)).

57:13.Borrowed Mythology & Plagiarism: Portrays hypocrites on Judgment Day begging believers for a share of their light ("Wait for us! Let us borrow from your light!"), being told to turn back and seek light elsewhere, and finding a wall with a shut door erected between inner mercy and outer punishment ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 57:13](ibnkathir://57/13), [Tafsir al-Tabari 57:13](tabari://57/13)). This scene directly adapts the narrative structure and dialogue of Jesus's 1st-century AD Parable of the Ten Virgins, where the foolish virgins beg the wise for lamp oil, are told to go back and buy their own, and are shut outside the closed door ([Matthew 25:8](bible://mt/25/8), [Matthew 25:9](bible://mt/25/9), [Matthew 25:10](bible://mt/25/10)).

57:22.Theological Defect: Asserts that every earthly catastrophe and personal affliction was already pre-inscribed in a Book before Allah created the world or human souls ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 57:22](ibnkathir://57/22), [Tafsir al-Tabari 57:22](tabari://57/22)), reinforced by [Sahih Muslim 2653b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2653b) stating Allah wrote all decrees fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and the earth. When paired with classical commentary attributing personal afflictions to sins ([Tafsir al-Tabari 57:22](tabari://57/22)), this hard determinism implies that human moral failures and their resulting calamities were pre-scripted prior to human existence ([James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13)).

57:23.Theological Defect: Applies the pre-creation determinism of [Quran 57:22](quran://57/22) by instructing believers neither to grieve over losses nor exult over gifts because every event was irrevocably fixed beforehand ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 57:23](ibnkathir://57/23), [Tafsir al-Tabari 57:23](tabari://57/23)). Teaching that all human outcomes are unalterably pre-written fosters fatalistic resignation rather than genuine moral agency and personal communion with a responsive Father ([Luke 11:9](bible://lk/11/9)).

57:27.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Explicitly affirms that Allah sent Jesus, son of Mary, gave him the Gospel (*al-Injil*), and placed deep kindness and mercy (*ra'fatan wa-rahmatan*) in the hearts of those who followed him ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 57:27](ibnkathir://57/27), [Tafsir al-Tabari 57:27](tabari://57/27)). This concession attests both to the divine origin of the Christian Gospel and to the authentic Christlike compassion characterizing Jesus's historical disciples ([John 13:35](bible://jn/13/35)).
57:27.Contradicts the Bible: Treats the Gospel (*al-Injil*) as a book handed directly to Jesus rather than the good news of His saving death and resurrection ([Mark 1:1](bible://mk/1/1), [Luke 24:46](bible://lk/24/46), [Romans 1:16](bible://rom/1/16)), while criticizing Christian celibate asceticism and monasticism (*rahbaniyyah*) as an unprescribed human innovation ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 57:27](ibnkathir://57/27), [Tafsir al-Tabari 57:27](tabari://57/27)). In the Gospels, Jesus Himself explicitly commends voluntary celibacy undertaken for undivided devotion to the Kingdom of Heaven ([Matthew 19:11](bible://mt/19/11), [Matthew 19:12](bible://mt/19/12)).

58:12.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Commands believers to pay a monetary charity fee (*sadaqah*) before holding any private consultation (*najwa*) with Muhammad ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 58:12](ibnkathir://58/12), [Tafsir al-Tabari 58:12](tabari://58/12)). Erecting a financial barrier around access to God's messenger to shield Muhammad from petitioners contrasts sharply with Jesus freely welcoming crowds, children, and the destitute without charge ([Matthew 10:8](bible://mt/10/8), [Mark 10:14](bible://mk/10/14)).

58:13.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Immediately rescinds the mandatory consultation fee enacted in the very preceding verse ([Quran 58:12](quran://58/12)) once believers held back from paying—with [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 58:13](ibnkathir://58/13) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 58:13](tabari://58/13) recording that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib alone paid a dinar before the rule was dropped. Such rapid legislative reversal around Muhammad's personal audience rules reflects situational policy adjustment rather than timeless moral law.
58:13.Theological Defect: Abrogates the divine command of [Quran 58:12](quran://58/12) almost as soon as it was issued, after only a single Companion complied and the community found the payment burdensome ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 58:13](ibnkathir://58/13), [Tafsir al-Tabari 58:13](tabari://58/13)). Enacting and cancelling an impractical statute within an allegedly eternal scripture inscribed on a guarded heavenly tablet ([Quran 85:22](quran://85/22)) undermines divine foresight and legislative consistency.

58:22.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Declares that true believers in Allah and the Last Day cannot bear affection (*yuwadduna*) toward anyone who opposes Allah and His Messenger, even their own fathers, sons, brothers, or kinsfolk, with [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 58:22](ibnkathir://58/22) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 58:22](tabari://58/22) praising Companions who fought or killed their non-Muslim fathers and brothers at Badr. Making the severance of natural familial love a test of faith stands in direct opposition to Jesus's command to love one's enemies and pray for persecutors ([Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44)).

59:2.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Celebrates the military siege and forced expulsion of the Jewish tribe of Banu Nadir from Medina, boasting that Allah cast dread (*al-ru'b*) into their hearts while their homes were demolished by their own hands and the hands of the believers ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 59:2](ibnkathir://59/2), [Tafsir al-Tabari 59:2](tabari://59/2), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4028](/hadith/bukhari/4028)). Framing the terrorizing and collective uprooting of a minority religious community as a divine lesson sanctifies religious displacement and coercion.

59:3.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Asserts that Allah divinely prescribed collective exile (*al-jala'*) upon the Jews of Banu Nadir and would otherwise have inflicted worldly slaughter and captivity upon them prior to the punishment of Hellfire ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 59:3](ibnkathir://59/3), [Tafsir al-Tabari 59:3](tabari://59/3), [Sahih al-Bukhari 4028](/hadith/bukhari/4028)). Presenting forced banishment as merciful leniency compared to execution legitimizes state violence against non-Muslim populations.

59:4.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Justifies the siege, terror, and expulsion of Banu Nadir ([Quran 59:2](quran://59/2), [Quran 59:3](quran://59/3)) on the ground that "they opposed God and His messenger," explicitly defined in [Tafsir al-Tabari 59:4](tabari://59/4) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 59:4](ibnkathir://59/4) as including their denial of Muhammad's prophethood and refusal to follow him. Equating theological rejection of Muhammad with punishable defiance against God provides an enduring rationale for suppressing religious dissent.

59:5.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Grants explicit divine sanction for Muhammad's order to chop down and burn the date-palm orchards (*linah*) of the besieged Jewish Banu Nadir at al-Buwayrah in order to terrorize and "disgrace the wicked" ([Sahih Muslim 1746a](/hadith/muslim/1746a), [Sahih Muslim 1746b](/hadith/muslim/1746b), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 59:5](ibnkathir://59/5)). Endorsing scorched-earth destruction of civilian orchards directly overturns the Torah's wartime prohibition against felling fruit-bearing trees during a siege ([Deuteronomy 20:19](bible://dt/20/19)).
59:5.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Revealed immediately after Banu Nadir protested that Muhammad claimed to forbid corruption on earth while burning their date palms—and after Companions themselves disputed felling the trees ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 59:5](ibnkathir://59/5), [Tafsir al-Tabari 59:5](tabari://59/5), [Sahih Muslim 1746a](/hadith/muslim/1746a))—to declare both felled and standing trees approved by Allah. Retroactively absolving a controversial wartime tactic demonstrates revelation functioning to shield Muhammad's military decisions from moral critique.

59:6.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Exempts uncontested property (*fay'*) seized from Banu Nadir without cavalry combat from ordinary division among troops and awards it directly to Muhammad under Allah's grant of authority over whomever He pleases ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 59:6](ibnkathir://59/6), [Tafsir al-Tabari 59:6](tabari://59/6)). As 'Umar ibn al-Khattab reports in [Sahih al-Bukhari 3093](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3093) and [Sahih Muslim 1757a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1757a), Banu Nadir's estates became Muhammad's exclusive personal domain, funding a full year's upkeep for his household and equipping his military forces.

59:7.Self-Serving Revelations & Prophetic Pri: Extends the Banu Nadir *fay'* rule ([Quran 59:6](quran://59/6)) to conquered towns generally, assigning seized wealth to Allah, Muhammad, his near kin, and designated dependents while commanding believers, "Whatever (spoils) the messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, stop (asking for it)" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 59:7](ibnkathir://59/7), [Tafsir al-Tabari 59:7](tabari://59/7)). Coupling Muhammad's discretionary control over confiscated estates ([Sahih al-Bukhari 3093](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3093), [Sahih Muslim 1757a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1757a)) with a threat of harsh divine retribution silences financial questioning from his followers.

60:1.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Forbids believers from taking Allah's and their disbelieving adversaries as allies or offering them affection (*mawaddah*), warning that anyone who extends secret friendship to them has strayed from the right path ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 60:1](ibnkathir://60/1), [Tafsir al-Tabari 60:1](tabari://60/1); [Sahih Muslim 2494a](/hadith/muslim/2494a)). Prohibiting love toward religious opponents stands in direct antithesis to Christ's command to love one's enemies and do good to those who hate you ([Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44), [Luke 6:27](bible://lk/6/27)).

60:4.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Presents Abraham and his companions as an enduring model (*uswatun hasanah*) for believers to imitate in repudiating their non-believing people and declaring, "between us and you enmity has shown itself, and hatred forever (*al-'adawatu wa-l-baghda'u abadan*), until you believe in God alone" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 60:4](ibnkathir://60/4), [Tafsir al-Tabari 60:4](tabari://60/4)). Elevating perpetual enmity and hatred against non-monotheists—and even forbidding prayer for an unbelieving father's forgiveness—codifies permanent religious hostility until conversion.
60:4.Contradicts the Bible: Attributes a manifesto of perpetual hatred against unbelieving neighbors to Abraham, whereas Genesis portrays Abraham as God's chosen channel of blessing to all families of the earth who lived peaceably by treaty with Gentile neighbors and interceded fervently to spare wicked Sodom ([Genesis 12:3](bible://gn/12/3), [Genesis 18:23](bible://gn/18/23), [Genesis 21:27](bible://gn/21/27)). Its command to maintain hatred until conversion also directly contradicts Jesus's command to love and pray for enemies ([Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44)).

60:10.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Nullifies existing interfaith marriages by declaring emigrating believing women unlawful for their non-Muslim husbands ("They are not permitted to them, nor are they permitted to them") and ordering Muslim men to sever marital ties (*'isam*) with disbelieving wives ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 60:10](ibnkathir://60/10), [Tafsir al-Tabari 60:10](tabari://60/10); [Sahih al-Bukhari 2731](/hadith/bukhari/2731)). Mandating the legal breakup of established marriages solely on religious grounds enforces strict sectarian segregation across family life.
60:10.Contradicts the Bible: Commands believers to dissolve established marriages with unbelieving spouses ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 60:10](ibnkathir://60/10), [Tafsir al-Tabari 60:10](tabari://60/10)), directly contradicting Jesus's teaching that what God has joined together no human authority may separate ([Matthew 19:6](bible://mt/19/6), [Mark 10:9](bible://mk/10/9)) and His restriction of divorce away from severing intact marriages over religious difference ([Matthew 19:9](bible://mt/19/9)).

60:13.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Commands believers not to befriend or ally with "a people with whom God is angry," identified in [Tafsir al-Tabari 60:13](tabari://60/13) as the Jews and broadened in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 60:13](ibnkathir://60/13) to Jews, Christians, and all non-Muslims under divine wrath (echoing [Quran 1:7](quran://1/7) and [Quran 5:51](quran://5/51)). Equating non-Muslim communities with hopeless grave-dwellers barred from friendship entrenches permanent social and religious alienation.

61:4.Incites Violence & Intolerance: Declares that Allah loves those who fight (*yuqatiluna*) in His cause drawn up in battle ranks like a solid structure—explained in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 61:4](ibnkathir://61/4) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 61:4](tabari://61/4) as armed combat against disbelievers so that Islam prevails over all other religions ([Quran 61:9](quran://61/9)). Making battlefield warfare a primary object of divine love contrasts sharply with Jesus blessing peacemakers as sons of God and rejecting armed combat for His Kingdom ([Matthew 5:9](bible://mt/5/9), [John 18:36](bible://jn/18/36)).

61:6.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Places on the lips of Jesus, son of Mary, the explicit declaration that he came "confirming what was before me of the Torah" (*musaddiqan lima bayna yadayya mina al-Tawrah*, [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 61:6](ibnkathir://61/6), [Tafsir al-Tabari 61:6](tabari://61/6)). Because Jesus read and affirmed the 1st-century AD Hebrew Scriptures attested by extant Dead Sea Scrolls ([Matthew 5:17](bible://mt/5/17), [Luke 24:44](bible://lk/24/44)), this concession undermines later claims that the Torah had been textually corrupted.
61:6.Historical, Scientific & Cosmological Er: Asserts as historical fact that 1st-century AD Jesus announced to Israel a future messenger named "Ahmad" ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 61:6](ibnkathir://61/6), [Tafsir al-Tabari 61:6](tabari://61/6)), a claim wholly absent from all extant Greek Gospel manuscripts and early patristic witnesses. The claim reflects an anachronistic Arabic rendering stemming from conflating the Johannine Greek title *Parakletos* ("Advocate/Counselor" in [John 14:16](bible://jn/14/16)) with *periklytos* ("praised," matching Arabic *Ahmad*).
61:6.Contradicts the Bible: Replaces Jesus's promise of the *Parakletos* in [John 14:16](bible://jn/14/16) and [John 16:7](bible://jn/16/7) with a human prophet named Ahmad, whereas Jesus explicitly identifies that Counselor as the invisible "Spirit of truth" whom the world cannot see, sent by the Father in Jesus's name to indwell the disciples forever ([John 14:17](bible://jn/14/17), [John 14:26](bible://jn/14/26), [Acts 2:4](bible://acts/2/4)). It simultaneously reduces Christ from God's final, supreme Son ([Hebrews 1:1](bible://heb/1/1)) to a herald for Muhammad.

61:14.Concedes Christian & Biblical Truths: Declares that Allah supported Jesus's believing disciples (*al-hawariyyun*) against their Israelite opponents so that Jesus's followers "were the ones who prevailed" (*fa-asbahu zahirin*). Because apostolic Christianity proclaiming Christ's crucifixion, resurrection, and divine Sonship ([Acts 1:8](bible://acts/1/8), [Acts 2:32](bible://acts/2/32), [Romans 1:4](bible://rom/1/4)) is the sole movement of Jesus's disciples that historically prevailed across the ancient world—forcing [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 61:14](ibnkathir://61/14) and [Tafsir al-Tabari 61:14](tabari://61/14) to claim that allegedly "Muslim" disciples were annihilated for six centuries—this verse either vindicates historic Christianity or falsifies its own claim that Jesus's true followers prevailed.
61:14.Contradicts the Bible: Recasts Jesus's disciples on the model of Muhammad's Medinan military helpers (*ansar*)—linked by Qatadah in [Tafsir al-Tabari 61:14](tabari://61/14) to the pledge at al-'Aqabah to wage war against all Arabs until they submit—while Ibn 'Abbas's narrative in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 61:14](ibnkathir://61/14) claims a young volunteer had Jesus's likeness cast upon him and was crucified in his place. Both claims directly contradict Jesus's non-violent mission ([Matthew 26:52](bible://mt/26/52), [John 18:36](bible://jn/18/36)) and the eyewitness Gospel testimony to His crucifixion ([John 19:35](bible://jn/19/35)).

62:5.Promotes Division & Discrimination: Likens Jews entrusted with the Torah who fail to uphold it—interpreted in [Tafsir al-Tabari 62:5](tabari://62/5) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 62:5](ibnkathir://62/5) as rejecting Muhammad's prophethood—to "a donkey carrying books" (*ka-mathali al-himari yahmilu asfaran*), with [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 62:5](ibnkathir://62/5) declaring them "worse than the donkey." Using animalistic ridicule against the Jewish people contrasts sharply with Paul's affirmation of Israel's enduring honor as entrusted with the very oracles of God ([Romans 3:1](bible://rom/3/1), [Romans 9:4](bible://rom/9/4)).

64:2.Theological Defect: Asserts that Allah created humanity such that "one of you is a disbeliever, and one of you a believer," explicitly explained in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 64:2](ibnkathir://64/2) as Allah creating humans with those characteristics and willing disbelief and belief for them, and paired in [Tafsir al-Tabari 64:2](tabari://64/2) with fetal predestination decrees recording whether each womb's child is "wretched or blessed" ([Sahih Muslim 2643a](/hadith/muslim/2643a)).
